faqs.question: What is the Upper Mustang Jeep Tour?
faqs.answer: It is a 13-day overland 4WD Jeep tour from Kathmandu that takes you through Kali Gandaki Valley to Lo Manthang in Upper Mustang without requiring long multi-day walks.

faqs.question: Do I need a special permit for the Upper Mustang Tour?
faqs.answer: Yes, you need the Special Restricted Area Permit (USD 500 for 10 days) and an ACAP permit. Zenex Travels & Tours handles all permit applications.

faqs.question: Is this tour suitable for families and senior citizens?
faqs.answer: Yes! Since the journey is in a 4WD vehicle with only short village walks, it is suitable for seniors, families, and travelers of all age groups.

faqs.question: What is the highest altitude reached on the tour?
faqs.answer: The highest points are Lo-Ghyakar Gompa (3,950 m), Lo Manthang (3,810 m), and Muktinath (3,800 m).

faqs.question: What type of vehicle is used?
faqs.answer: We use private 4WD Mahindra Scorpio or Toyota Land Cruiser SUVs for groups of 1-5 passengers, and tourist mini-buses for larger groups.

faqs.question: When is the best time for the Upper Mustang Jeep Tour?
faqs.answer: Upper Mustang lies in a rain shadow and can be visited year-round, including Spring (March-May), Autumn (Sept-Nov), and Summer Monsoon (June-August).

faqs.question: What type of accommodation is provided during the tour?
faqs.answer: Comfortable 3-star hotels in Kathmandu and Pokhara, and clean mountain teahouses and lodges with attached or shared bathrooms in Mustang.

faqs.question: What food is available during the Upper Mustang Tour?
faqs.answer: Lodges serve fresh local Dal Bhat, momos, noodles, fried rice, soups, Tibetan bread, as well as Western dishes like pasta, pizza, and pancakes.

faqs.question: Do I need to be physically fit for the tour?
faqs.answer: Basic physical fitness is sufficient. There is no technical climbing or long daily trekking involved.

faqs.question: Can I visit Lo Manthang and Chhoser caves by Jeep?
faqs.answer: Yes, 4WD dirt tracks connect Lo Manthang, Chhoser sky caves, Ghar Gompa, and Charang village.

faqs.question: Can the 13-day itinerary be customized?
faqs.answer: Yes! Zenex Travels & Tours can adjust hotel categories, add extra days in Pokhara or Lo Manthang, or combine with flight options from Jomsom.

faqs.question: What should I pack for the Upper Mustang Tour?
faqs.answer: Pack windproof jackets, warm layers for cool nights, comfortable walking shoes, sunglasses, sunscreen (SPF 50+), and a daypack.

faqs.question: Is Wi-Fi or mobile signal available in Upper Mustang?
faqs.answer: NTC and Ncell mobile networks work in major settlements (Jomsom, Kagbeni, Lo Manthang), and most teahouses offer Wi-Fi for a small fee.

faqs.question: Can I use credit cards in Mustang?
faqs.answer: Credit cards are only accepted in Kathmandu and Pokhara. Please bring sufficient cash (NPR) for personal expenses in Mustang.

faqs.question: Why travel with Zenex Travels & Tours?
faqs.answer: Zenex Travels & Tours brings over two decades of Himalayan travel experience, licensed guides, reliable 4WD vehicles, and transparent pricing.

faqs.question: Is tipping expected for tour guide and driver?
faqs.answer: Tipping is customary in Nepal for good service and is greatly appreciated by guides and drivers.

treks.title: Upper Mustang Trek - 18 Days
treks.location: Upper Mustang & Lo Manthang, Mustang District, Nepal

treks.overview:
Short Upper Mustang Trek 18 Days | Discover Nepal's Forbidden Kingdom & Tibetan Culture

The 18-Day Upper Mustang Trek in Nepal is a culturally rich and scenic mountain expedition into one of Nepal's most remote and preserved Himalayan destinations. Often referred to as the "Last Forbidden Kingdom", Upper Mustang was closed to foreign travelers until 1992, preserving its ancient Tibetan Buddhist traditions, centuries-old monasteries, cliffside cave dwellings, and desert-like landscapes.

Starting with a scenic flight or drive from Pokhara to Jomsom, the trail leads past black Shaligram fossils in Kali Gandaki Valley to Kagbeni, the restricted boundary of Upper Mustang. Trekkers walk through colorful traditional villages like Chele, Samar, Syanbochen, Ghami, and Charang before reaching the ancient walled capital of Lo Manthang (3,810 m). The return trail crosses the high Gyu La Pass (4,077 m) to holy Muktinath Temple.

At Zenex Travels & Tours, we manage all logistics—including Special Restricted Area Permits (RAP USD 500), Annapurna Conservation Area Permits (ACAP), round-trip domestic flights/transfers, licensed high-altitude guides, porters, teahouse bookings, and hotel stays in Kathmandu and Pokhara.
highlights: Scenic Flight to Jomsom: Fly over the Kali Gandaki Gorge, the world's deepest gorge, with stunning views of Dhaulagiri and Annapurna.
Explore Kagbeni: Visit the historic village of Kagbeni, the gateway to Upper Mustang, filled with traditional mud-brick houses and Tibetan chortens.
Ancient Salt Trade Route: Walk historic trails once used by salt traders between Nepal and Tibet, passing windswept canyons and red-rock cliffs.
Visit Chungsi Cave: A sacred meditation cliffside cave used by Guru Rinpoche (Padmasambhava) tucked near Syanbochen.
Lo Manthang – The Walled Kingdom: Discover the old capital of Mustang with its 5-story Royal Palace and centuries-old gompas (Jampa, Thubchen & Chode).
Rich Tibetan Buddhist Heritage: Experience traditional dress, prayer flags, Mani walls, and centuries-old monasteries.
Vibrant Villages: Trek through Chele, Samar, Ghami, Dhakmar, and Charang, each offering distinct character and mountain vistas.
Gyu La Pass & Muktinath Temple: Cross Gyu La Pass (4,077 m) and visit sacred Muktinath Temple, holy to both Hindus and Buddhists.
Rain-Shadow Desert Scenery: Experience dry, high-altitude desert plateaus suitable even for summer monsoon trekking.

itinerary.title: Arrival in Kathmandu
itinerary.highlights: Airport pickup, hotel transfer, pre-trip briefing & guide meeting.
itinerary.description: Upon arrival at Tribhuvan International Airport (TIA) in Kathmandu, your Zenex Travels representative will transfer you by private vehicle to your hotel. After check-in, we hold a pre-trip briefing to review the restricted permit requirements and introduce your trekking guide. Overnight at hotel.

itinerary.title: Preparation for Restricted Permit + Sightseeing in Kathmandu
itinerary.highlights: Passport check for Special Permit, UNESCO tour of Kathmandu Durbar Square, Swayambhunath, Boudhanath & Pashupatinath.
itinerary.description: Submit original passports to the Nepal Immigration Department for the Special Restricted Area Permit. Spend the rest of the day on a guided UNESCO World Heritage tour of Kathmandu, visiting ancient palaces at Kathmandu Durbar Square, Swayambhunath Stupa, Boudhanath Stupa, and Pashupatinath Temple. Overnight at hotel.

itinerary.title: Kathmandu – Pokhara
itinerary.highlights: Drive through Trishuli and Marshyangdi river valleys to lakeside Pokhara.
itinerary.description: Travel from Kathmandu to Pokhara by comfortable vehicle (approx. 7-8 hrs drive, or optional 25-minute domestic flight). Arrive in Pokhara, check into your hotel, and spend a relaxing evening by Phewa Lake. Overnight at hotel.

itinerary.title: Pokhara – Jomsom (2,700 m) – Trek to Kagbeni
itinerary.highlights: 25-min flight to Jomsom over Annapurna & Dhaulagiri, trek along Kali Gandaki riverbed past Shaligram fossils.
itinerary.description: Take an early morning 25-minute flight from Pokhara to Jomsom (or 6-hr drive). Assemble with your trekking crew in Jomsom and trek for 3 hours along the Kali Gandaki riverbed to Kagbeni (2,800 m), searching for ancient black Shaligram fossils along the way. Visit 15th-century Kagchode Thubten Sampheling Gompa. Overnight at lodge.

itinerary.title: Kagbeni – Chele
itinerary.highlights: Check restricted permit at Kagbeni, trek past Tangbe stone houses, Chhusang red cliffs & Chele village.
itinerary.description: Verify your restricted area permit at the Kagbeni checkpoint and officially enter Upper Mustang. Trek through Tangbe village with its narrow whitewashed alleys, apple orchards, and barley fields. Pass Chhusang red cliffs and cross the river bridge to reach Chele village (3,050 m). Overnight at lodge.

itinerary.title: Chele – Samar
itinerary.highlights: Cross Taklam La (3,624 m) & Dajori La (3,735 m), views of Tilicho Peak & Damodar Danda, poplar trees of Samar.
itinerary.description: Climb steeply out of Chele up a rocky gully to Ghyakar village. Cross Taklam La (3,624 m) and Dajori La (3,735 m) passes, enjoying dramatic views of Tilicho Peak and Damodar Danda. Descend into Samar (3,660 m), a pleasant village shaded by poplar trees. Overnight at lodge.

itinerary.title: Samar – Chungsi Cave – Syanbochen
itinerary.highlights: Descend into deep canyon to visit sacred Chungsi Meditation Cave, cross Yamda La (3,850 m) to Syanbochen.
itinerary.description: Descend into a deep gorge and trek up to Chungsi Cave—a sacred meditation cave tucked into a cliff face used by Guru Rinpoche in the 8th century. Continue ascending past Bhena and cross Yamda La pass (3,850 m) before descending gently into Syanbochen village (3,800 m). Overnight at lodge.

itinerary.title: Syanbochen – Ghami
itinerary.highlights: Cross Syangboche La (3,850 m) & Nyi La (4,010 m), views of Geling valley, arrive in Ghami village.
itinerary.description: Ascend gradually to Syangboche La pass (3,850 m) with views over Geling valley. Continue climbing to Nyi La pass (4,010 m)—the highest point on today's route. Descend steeply into Ghami (3,520 m), one of the largest villages in Upper Mustang, surrounded by green fields and ancient monasteries. Overnight at lodge.

itinerary.title: Ghami – Charang
itinerary.highlights: Walk past the longest Mani wall in Mustang, visit 1300-yr Gekar Gompa, explore 5-story Tsarang Palace & library.
itinerary.description: Trek past the longest Mani prayer wall in Mustang, intricately decorated with carved stone mantras. Visit ancient Gekar Gompa before crossing a pass into Charang (Tsarang, 3,560 m). Explore the 5-story Tsarang Palace and the ancient monastery holding rare Buddhist scriptures. Overnight at lodge.

itinerary.title: Charang – Lo Manthang
itinerary.highlights: Cross Lo La pass (3,950 m) for first panorama of walled city of Lo Manthang, enter city gates.
itinerary.description: Descend into Charang canyon, cross the river, and climb steadily up to Lo La pass (3,950 m). Catch your first breathtaking view of the ancient walled city of Lo Manthang against the Tibetan plateau. Descend gently into the city gates of Lo Manthang (3,810 m). Overnight at lodge.

itinerary.title: Lo Manthang Exploration (Monasteries, Royal Palace & Chhoser Sky Caves)
itinerary.highlights: Jampa Gompa, Thubchen Gompa, Chhoede Gompa, Royal Palace & multi-story Jhong Sky Cave at Chhoser.
itinerary.description: Spend a full day exploring ancient Lo Manthang. Visit 15th-century Jampa Gompa, Thubchen Gompa, and active Chhoede Gompa. Take a short excursion to Chhoser to explore Jhong Cave—a multi-story cliff dwelling used for centuries as meditation cells and storage. Walk along the historic city walls. Overnight at lodge.

itinerary.title: Lo Manthang – Dhakmar – Ghami
itinerary.highlights: Trek high alpine meadows, descend past dramatic red rock cliffs of Dhakmar back to Ghami.
itinerary.description: Begin the return trek on the highland trail, crossing high alpine pastures before dropping down a steep, eroded canyon into Dhakmar, famous for towering blood-red rock cliffs. Enjoy lunch in Dhakmar and continue down the valley to Ghami (3,520 m). Overnight at lodge.

itinerary.title: Ghami – Geling – Samar
itinerary.highlights: Trek past Geling Tibetan village, cross Yamda La back to Samar village.
itinerary.description: Trek from Ghami following a winding trail past Geling village. Re-cross Yamda La pass and descend into the quiet poplar-shaded village of Samar (3,660 m). Overnight at lodge.

itinerary.title: Samar – Gyu La Pass (4,077 m) – Muktinath
itinerary.highlights: Climb Gyu La Pass (4,077 m) for mountain views, cross Chhusang river bridge, arrive at holy Muktinath Temple.
itinerary.description: Climb steadily up to Gyu La Pass (4,077 m), enjoying panoramic views across Upper Mustang and snow-capped peaks. Descend through rugged canyons towards Chhusang apple orchards, then follow the trail up to holy Muktinath Temple (3,800 m). Visit the 108 stone water spouts and eternal natural flame. Overnight at lodge.

itinerary.title: Muktinath – Kagbeni – Jomsom
itinerary.highlights: Descend from Muktinath to Kagbeni, trek down Kali Gandaki riverbed back to Jomsom.
itinerary.description: Trek downhill from Muktinath to Kagbeni (approx. 2.5 hrs), taking in morning views of Dhaulagiri. Continue walking along the wide Kali Gandaki riverbed past Ekle Bhatti back to Jomsom (2,700 m). Celebrate the completion of the trek with your guide and porters. Overnight at lodge.

itinerary.title: Jomsom – Pokhara
itinerary.highlights: Morning scenic flight from Jomsom to Pokhara, free afternoon by Phewa Lake.
itinerary.description: Take an early morning 25-minute flight from Jomsom to Pokhara (or overland drive if flight delayed by wind). Check into your hotel in Pokhara and spend the rest of the day relaxing, enjoying spa massages, or visiting Lakeside cafes. Overnight at hotel.

itinerary.title: Pokhara – Kathmandu
itinerary.highlights: Return drive to Kathmandu, evening official farewell dinner with cultural show.
itinerary.description: Travel back to Kathmandu from Pokhara in a tourist vehicle (approx. 7-8 hrs drive). Check into your hotel and enjoy free time for souvenir shopping in Thamel. In the evening, join Zenex Travels for a traditional farewell dinner with cultural performances. Overnight at hotel.

itinerary.title: Departure from Kathmandu
itinerary.highlights: Airport transfer for departure flight.
itinerary.description: Enjoy breakfast at your hotel. At your scheduled departure time, your Zenex Travels representative will transfer you by private vehicle to Tribhuvan International Airport for your international departure flight.

It requires walking 5 to 8 hours daily over rocky, dry, windswept trails with ascents over high passes like Nyi La (4,010 m) and Gyu La Pass (4,077 m). While technical climbing is not required, good physical stamina and acclimatization are essential.

altitudeSickness.description: Reaching a maximum altitude of 4,077 meters at Gyu La Pass and 3,810 meters at Lo Manthang, altitude sickness (AMS) can affect trekkers. Gradual ascent and acclimatization built into the 18-day itinerary keep risks low.
prevention: Trek at a slow, steady pace without rushing uphill.
Drink 3 to 4 liters of clean water daily and enjoy warm ginger/garlic soups.
Avoid alcohol, smoking, and reduce caffeine intake during high altitude trek days.
Inform your Zenex Travels guide immediately if you experience headache, nausea, or dizziness.

faqs.question: Where is Upper Mustang located?
faqs.answer: Upper Mustang is located in northwestern Nepal inside the Mustang District along the border of Tibet, behind the Dhaulagiri and Annapurna ranges.

faqs.question: How difficult is the 18-day Upper Mustang Trek?
faqs.answer: It is rated HARD due to 5-8 hours of daily walking over dry, dusty trails, high passes up to 4,077 m, and windy mountain terrain.

faqs.question: Is a special permit required for Upper Mustang?
faqs.answer: Yes, a Special Restricted Area Permit (USD 500 per person for 10 days) and ACAP permit are mandatory. Zenex Travels & Tours handles all permits.

faqs.question: Can I trek solo in Upper Mustang?
faqs.answer: No, government rules mandate a minimum group of 2 trekkers accompanied by a licensed guide from a registered agency like Zenex Travels & Tours.

faqs.question: What accommodation is available on the trek?
faqs.answer: Lodges and teahouses in villages like Kagbeni, Chele, Ghami, Charang, and Lo Manthang provide clean twin-sharing rooms with basic facilities.

faqs.question: Is internet and electricity available in Upper Mustang?
faqs.answer: Yes, major villages (Jomsom, Kagbeni, Lo Manthang) have mobile network coverage (NTC/Ncell) and teahouses offer Wi-Fi and solar battery charging for a small fee.

treks.overview:
Upper Mustang Trek with Luri Gompa 22 Days | Hidden Kingdom & Sacred Cliffside Cave Monastery

The 22-Day Upper Mustang Trek with Luri Gompa is a unique cultural and spiritual expedition into the heart of the ancient Kingdom of Lo in Nepal. Beyond the classic Lo Manthang circuit, this remote loop takes adventurers off the main trail into the untouched villages of Dhi, Yara, Ghara, and Tangge. The pinnacle of the trek is visiting Luri Gompa, a mystical 13th–14th-century cave monastery carved high inside a sandstone cliff face.

Luri Gompa shelters ancient Buddhist wall frescoes, a sacred domed chorten (stupa), and rare religious texts preserved in high-altitude desert air. Along the circuit, trekkers experience traditional Mustang village life, ochre red canyon walls, sky cave complexes in Chhoser, and breathtaking panoramas of Nilgiri, Dhaulagiri, and Annapurna peaks before returning via high passes to holy Muktinath Temple.

At Zenex Travels & Tours, we handle all logistics—including Special Restricted Area Permits (RAP USD 500), Annapurna Conservation Area Permits (ACAP), round-trip domestic flights (Pokhara – Jomsom – Pokhara), licensed high-altitude guides, porters, lodge bookings, and 3-star hotel stays in Kathmandu and Pokhara.
highlights: Scenic flight to Jomsom over Kali Gandaki River Gorge, the deepest gorge in the world, with views of Dhaulagiri and Annapurna.
Explore Kagbeni, the medieval gateway to Upper Mustang with ancient mud-brick houses and Tibetan Buddhist chortens.
Discover the walled city of Lo Manthang — former royal capital of Mustang with ancient palaces, assembly halls, and monkish culture.
Trek off-the-beaten-path to remote Yara and Ghara villages surrounded by dramatic sandstone canyon walls.
Hike up to mystical Luri Gompa, a 13th–14th-century cliffside cave monastery featuring ancient Buddhist frescoes and a sacred chorten.
Visit 1,300-year-old Lo Gekhar Monastery (Ghar Gompa) built by Guru Padmasambhava to subdue mountain spirits.
Explore Chhoser and Jhong Sky Caves, multi-story cliff dwellings carved thousands of years ago for meditation and refuge.
Return via remote Tangge, Paha pass (4,210 m), and Tetang village for a complete wilderness loop through Upper Mustang.
Visit sacred Muktinath Temple at 3,800 m, revered by both Hindus and Buddhists with 108 eternal water spouts.

itinerary.title: Arrival in Kathmandu
itinerary.highlights: Airport pickup, hotel transfer, pre-trip briefing & guide meeting.
itinerary.description: Upon arrival at Tribhuvan International Airport (TIA) in Kathmandu, your Zenex Travels representative will transfer you by private vehicle to your hotel. After check-in, we arrange a pre-trip briefing to review your trek permits, answer questions, and introduce your trekking guide. Overnight at hotel.

itinerary.title: Preparation for Restricted Permit + Sightseeing in Kathmandu
itinerary.highlights: Permit verification, UNESCO tour: Kathmandu Durbar Square, Swayambhunath, Boudhanath & Pashupatinath.
itinerary.description: Verify your passport documents for the Special Restricted Area Permit. Spend the day on a guided UNESCO World Heritage tour of Kathmandu, exploring Kathmandu Durbar Square, Swayambhunath Stupa, Boudhanath Stupa, and Pashupatinath Temple. Overnight at hotel.

itinerary.title: Kathmandu – Pokhara
itinerary.highlights: Scenic drive past Trishuli and Marshyangdi rivers to Pokhara lakeside.
itinerary.description: Drive from Kathmandu to Pokhara by tourist vehicle (approx. 8-9 hours drive, or optional 25-minute domestic flight). Check into your hotel in Pokhara and spend the evening relaxing by Phewa Lake. Overnight at hotel.

itinerary.title: Pokhara – Jomsom (2,700 m flight) – Kagbeni
itinerary.highlights: 25-min flight to Jomsom over Kali Gandaki Gorge, trek past black Shaligram fossils to Kagbeni.
itinerary.description: Transfer to Pokhara Airport for a 25-minute flight to Jomsom (2,700 m) with views of Dhaulagiri and Annapurna. Assemble with your guide and porters and trek 3 hours along the Kali Gandaki riverbed past Shaligram fossils to Kagbeni (2,800 m). Visit 15th-century Kagchode Thubten Sampheling Gompa. Overnight at lodge.

itinerary.title: Kagbeni – Chuksang
itinerary.highlights: Check restricted permit, trek past whitewashed stone houses of Tangbe to Chuksang cliffs.
itinerary.description: Submit your Restricted Area Permit at the Kagbeni checkpoint. Trek along the flat riverbed past Tangbe village, famous for whitewashed houses, narrow alleys, and apple orchards. Continue past red cliff formations to Chuksang (2,980 m) at the river confluence. Overnight at lodge.

itinerary.title: Chuksang – Chele – Samar
itinerary.highlights: Cross Kali Gandaki steel bridge, ascend past Chele village & Takalese Plateau to Samar.
itinerary.description: Cross the Kali Gandaki River via a steel bridge and ascend through narrow gorges to Chele village. Continue climbing over Takalese Plateau and Taklam La pass, taking in views of eroded hills and deep canyons. Descend into poplar-shaded Samar village (3,660 m). Overnight at lodge.

itinerary.title: Samar – Shyangbochen – Geling
itinerary.highlights: Trek juniper valley, cross Yamda La to Shyangbochen, descend into barley fields of Geling.
itinerary.description: Climb from Samar to a mountain ridge and descend into a valley past a Buddhist Chorten. Trek through juniper woods and cross a stream before climbing over Yamda La to Shyangbochen. Descend gently into Geling (3,570 m), surrounded by wide green barley fields and traditional stone homes. Overnight at lodge.

itinerary.title: Geling – Ghemi
itinerary.highlights: Cross Nyi La pass (4,010 m), arrive in Ghemi, explore old monasteries & longest Mani wall.
itinerary.description: Climb steadily up from Geling to cross Nyi La pass (4,010 m), taking in sweeping views of Upper Mustang's desert landscape. Descend to Ghemi (3,520 m), one of Mustang's largest settlements, famous for its ancient monasteries, traditional royal court, and the longest Mani prayer wall in the region. Overnight at lodge.

itinerary.title: Ghemi – Tsarang (Charang)
itinerary.highlights: Trek past Gekar Gompa, visit 5-story Tsarang Palace & ancient monastery library.
itinerary.description: Trek alongside Ghemi's carved Mani wall, cross a small stream, and climb up to visit ancient Gekar Gompa. Traverse barren plateaus into Tsarang (Charang, 3,560 m), a historic village perched above a deep canyon. Visit the 5-story Tsarang Palace and the ancient monastery housing sacred Buddhist texts. Overnight at lodge.

itinerary.title: Tsarang – Lo La Pass – Lo Manthang
itinerary.highlights: Climb Lo La pass (3,950 m) for first sight of walled Lo Manthang, enter medieval city gates.
itinerary.description: Descend into Tsarang canyon, cross the river, and ascend steadily to Lo La pass (3,950 m). Catch your first panoramic view of the walled city of Lo Manthang surrounded by barren desert hills. Descend into the city gates of Lo Manthang (3,810 m). Overnight at lodge.

itinerary.title: Lo Manthang Exploration (Monasteries, Royal Palace & Chhoser Sky Caves)
itinerary.highlights: Jampa Gompa, Thubchen Gompa, Chhoede Gompa, Royal Palace & Jhong Sky Cave complex at Chhoser.
itinerary.description: Spend a full day exploring ancient Lo Manthang. Visit 15th-century Jampa Gompa (God House), Thubchen Gompa assembly hall, and active Chhoede Gompa. Take an excursion to Chhoser to explore Jhong Cave—a multi-story cliff dwelling used for centuries as meditation cells and storage. Overnight at lodge.

itinerary.title: Lo Manthang – Dhi Gaon
itinerary.highlights: Trek off the beaten track across highland pastures to peaceful Dhi Gaon river village.
itinerary.description: Leave Lo Manthang and head southeast into remote, uncrowded territory. Cross highland meadows and open desert plateaus with panoramic views of snow peaks. Descend steadily to Dhi Gaon (3,400 m), a peaceful stone village built along the riverbank. Overnight at lodge/homestay.

itinerary.title: Dhi Gaon – Yara Gaon
itinerary.highlights: Short scenic trek through wind-sculpted river canyons to traditional Yara Gaon.
itinerary.description: Trek a short and scenic route along the riverbed through sandstone cliffs carved by wind into natural pillar sculptures. Arrive early at Yara Gaon (3,650 m), a peaceful Tibetan Buddhist village nestled among barley fields and clay cliffs. Overnight at lodge.

itinerary.title: Rest Day at Yara Gaon: Excursion to Tashi Gompa & Sacred Luri Gompa
itinerary.highlights: Visit Tashi Gompa & mystical 13th-century Luri Gompa cave monastery carved into sandstone cliffs.
itinerary.description: Spend a dedicated cultural day visiting sacred monastic sites. Hike to nearby Tashi Gompa before continuing up to Sukhang to visit **Luri Gompa**—a 13th-century cliffside cave monastery featuring ancient Buddhist wall murals, a sacred domed chorten, and rare spiritual energy. Return to Yara Gaon for overnight lodge stay.

itinerary.title: Yara – Tangge
itinerary.highlights: Cross Dhechang and Tangge streams, arrive in remote, isolated village of Tangge.
itinerary.description: Trek downhill through open wilderness, crossing Dhechang and Tangge streams. Pass traditional farmland and sculpted sandstone cliffs to reach Tangge (3,240 m)—a remote, tranquil village known for unique rows of ancient Buddhist chortens and traditional Mustangi architecture. Overnight at lodge.

itinerary.title: Tangge – Paha
itinerary.highlights: Ascend high summer yak pastures, reach highest elevation of trek at Paha (4,210 m).
itinerary.description: Ascend steeply out of Tangge onto high mountain ridge pastures used by locals for summer grazing. Enjoy wide open vistas of surrounding Himalayan peaks. Arrive at Paha (4,210 m), the highest point of the 22-day circuit. Overnight at lodge/camp.

itinerary.title: Paha – Baha Bhanjyang (Cha Cho La Pass) – Tetang
itinerary.highlights: Cross Baha Bhanjyang (Cha Cho La Pass), descend to ancient stone village of Tetang.
itinerary.description: Cross Baha Bhanjyang (Cha Cho La Pass) with views over Kali Gandaki Valley and Nilgiri Peak. Descend steadily down a wide valley into Tetang (3,040 m), a fortified stone village preserving traditional Tibetan architecture and lifestyle. Overnight at lodge.

itinerary.title: Tetang – Muktinath Temple
itinerary.highlights: Ascend past apple orchards and Tibetan hamlets to holy Muktinath Temple.
itinerary.description: Trek uphill from Tetang through mountain trails, passing apple orchards, grazing yaks, and ancient meditation caves. Arrive at sacred Muktinath Temple (3,800 m), an important pilgrimage site for Hindus and Buddhists featuring 108 stone spouts and an eternal gas flame. Overnight at lodge.

itinerary.title: Muktinath – Kagbeni – Jomsom
itinerary.highlights: Gentle downhill walk from Muktinath via Kagbeni back to Jomsom hub.
itinerary.description: Descend gently from Muktinath to Kagbeni (approx. 2.5 hrs) along the Kali Gandaki riverbed. Continue walking to Jomsom (2,700 m). Celebrate the completion of the 22-day high Mustang circuit with your guide and porters. Overnight at lodge.

itinerary.title: Jomsom – Pokhara
itinerary.highlights: Scenic morning flight from Jomsom to Pokhara, lakeside relaxation.
itinerary.description: Take an early morning 25-minute flight from Jomsom to Pokhara. Transfer to your hotel and spend a relaxed day enjoying Pokhara's cafes, Lake Phewa boating, and mountain scenery. Overnight at hotel.

itinerary.title: Pokhara – Kathmandu
itinerary.highlights: Return drive to Kathmandu, official farewell dinner with cultural dance performance.
itinerary.description: Travel back to Kathmandu from Pokhara in a tourist vehicle (approx. 7-8 hrs drive). Check into your hotel and enjoy free time for souvenir shopping in Thamel. In the evening, join your Zenex Travels team for an official farewell dinner. Overnight at hotel.

itinerary.title: Departure from Kathmandu
itinerary.highlights: Airport transfer for international departure flight.
itinerary.description: Enjoy breakfast at your hotel. At your scheduled departure time, your Zenex Travels representative will transfer you by private vehicle to Tribhuvan International Airport for your international departure flight.

treks.difficultyInfo: The 22-day Upper Mustang Trek with Luri Gompa is graded HARD. It requires walking 5 to 7 hours daily over rocky, dry, windswept trails with ascents over high passes like Nyi La (4,010 m), Paha (4,210 m), and Baha Bhanjyang (Cha Cho La Pass). Good physical fitness and stamina are required.

altitudeSickness.description: Reaching maximum altitudes of 4,210 meters at Paha and 3,810 meters at Lo Manthang, altitude sickness (AMS) can occur. Gradual ascent and acclimatization built into the 22-day itinerary keep risks low.
prevention: Trek at a steady pace without rushing uphill.
Drink 3 to 4 liters of clean water daily and enjoy warm ginger/garlic soups.
Avoid alcohol, smoking, and reduce caffeine intake during high altitude trek days.
Inform your Zenex Travels guide immediately if you experience headache, nausea, or dizziness.

faqs.question: What is the Upper Mustang Trek with Luri Gompa?
faqs.answer: It is an extended 22-day trekking circuit in Upper Mustang that explores the classic Lo Manthang route as well as remote eastern villages of Yara, Ghara, Tangge, and the 13th-century cliff cave monastery of Luri Gompa.

faqs.question: How difficult is the 22-day Upper Mustang Trek?
faqs.answer: It is rated HARD due to 5-7 hours of daily walking over dry, dusty trails, remote terrain, and high passes up to 4,210 meters.

faqs.question: Is a special permit required?
faqs.answer: Yes, a Special Restricted Area Permit (USD 500 per person for 10 days) and ACAP permit are mandatory. Zenex Travels & Tours handles all permits.

faqs.question: Can I trek solo on this route?
faqs.answer: No, government rules mandate a minimum group of 2 trekkers accompanied by a licensed guide from a registered agency like Zenex Travels & Tours.

faqs.question: What accommodation is available?
faqs.answer: Lodges and teahouses in villages like Kagbeni, Chele, Ghemi, Charang, Lo Manthang, Yara, and Tangge provide clean twin-sharing rooms with basic facilities.

faqs.question: Is internet and electricity available in Upper Mustang?
faqs.answer: Yes, major villages (Jomsom, Kagbeni, Lo Manthang) have mobile network coverage (NTC/Ncell) and teahouses offer Wi-Fi and solar battery charging for a small fee.

treks.overview:
Nar Phu and Upper Mustang Trek 27 Days | High Altitude Wilderness & Trans-Himalayan Pass Expedition

The 27-Day Nar Phu and Upper Mustang Trek is one of the most adventurous, remote, and culturally rich expeditions in the Nepalese Himalayas. Crossing two restricted regions—the hidden Tibetan-influenced valleys of Nar and Phu in Manang and the ancient Kingdom of Upper Mustang—this trek links both regions via the formidable, wild Teri La Pass (5,595 m).

The expedition begins along the Annapurna Circuit from Besisahar to Koto before turning off into Nar Phu's narrow gorges, ancient stone villages, and Tashi Lhakhang Monastery. Crossing the uninhabited alpine wilderness over Teri La Pass (5,595 m) requires full wilderness tented camping and camping support staff. Descending into Upper Mustang, trekkers explore Tangge, Yara, the walled city of Lo Manthang (3,810 m), Charang, and Kagbeni before flying back from Jomsom.

At Zenex Travels & Tours, we manage all logistics—including Nar Phu Restricted Area Permits, Upper Mustang Restricted Area Permits (RAP USD 500), Annapurna Conservation Area Permits (ACAP), full wilderness camping gear, licensed high-altitude guides, camping cooks, porters, domestic flights (Jomsom – Pokhara – Kathmandu), and hotel stays in Kathmandu.
highlights: Explore two unique restricted regions: Nar Phu Valley in Manang and Upper Mustang.
Trek through ancient Tibetan-influenced villages of Meta, Kyang, Phu, and Nar with preserved centuries-old culture.
Cross the formidable Teri La Pass (5,595 m), enjoying 360-degree views of Himlung Himal, Annapurna II, and Tilicho Peak.
Visit the medieval walled city of Lo Manthang — former royal capital of Mustang with ancient palaces and active gompas.
Experience high-wilderness tented camping across uninhabited alpine meadows (Dharamshala, Pokhari, Teri Bhanjyang Phedi, Yak Kharka).
Visit historic monasteries including Tashi Lhakhang in Phu, Guru Choling in Nar, and 1,300-year-old Ghar Gompa.
Traverse diverse Himalayan landscapes—from pine forests and river gorges to high-altitude rain-shadow desert canyons.
Spot rare Himalayan wildlife such as blue sheep (Bharal) and snow leopard tracks in remote high passes.
Enjoy full camping crew support (cook, kitchen staff, porters, camping tents & equipment).
Fly out from Jomsom to Pokhara and Kathmandu over spectacular Himalayan mountain ranges.
Travel with licensed high-altitude guides from Zenex Travels & Tours with deep expertise in restricted region logistics.

quickFacts.accommodation: 3-Star Hotel in Kathmandu / Teahouses & Tented Camping

itinerary.title: Arrival in Kathmandu
itinerary.highlights: Airport pickup, hotel transfer, pre-trip expedition briefing & guide meeting.
itinerary.description: Upon arrival at Tribhuvan International Airport (TIA) in Kathmandu, your Zenex Travels representative will transfer you by private vehicle to your hotel. After check-in, we hold a comprehensive pre-trip briefing to verify high-altitude climbing/trekking gear, review restricted permits, and introduce your guide. Overnight at hotel.

itinerary.title: Preparation for Restricted Permits + Sightseeing in Kathmandu
itinerary.highlights: Permit processing (Nar Phu & Upper Mustang RAPs), guided UNESCO tour of Patan Durbar Square, Boudhanath & Pashupatinath.
itinerary.description: Submit original passports to the Department of Immigration for Nar Phu and Upper Mustang Restricted Area Permits. Enjoy a guided UNESCO World Heritage tour of Patan Durbar Square, sacred Pashupatinath Temple, and the giant stupa at Boudhanath. Finalize gear checks. Overnight at hotel.

itinerary.title: Kathmandu – Besisahar
itinerary.highlights: Drive along Trishuli and Marshyangdi rivers to gateway town of Besisahar.
itinerary.description: Drive east and north from Kathmandu along scenic river valleys and terraced hillsides to Besisahar (760 m), the starting town for the Annapurna Circuit. Check into your lodge and rest. Overnight at lodge.

itinerary.title: Besisahar – Koto
itinerary.highlights: Off-road drive through Marshyangdi gorge, views of Annapurna II & Manaslu, arrival at Koto checkpoint.
itinerary.description: Drive by 4WD jeep along the rugged Marshyangdi River valley, passing villages like Bagarchhap, Timang, and Dharapani. Enjoy views of Annapurna II (7,937 m) and Mount Manaslu. Arrive in Koto (2,600 m), the official entrance gate to Nar Phu Valley. Overnight at lodge.

itinerary.title: Koto – Meta
itinerary.highlights: Check restricted permit at Koto, walk narrow Soti Khola gorge, suspension bridges & pine forests to Meta plateau.
itinerary.description: Register restricted permits at Koto post and turn off the main Annapurna trail into the narrow Soti Khola gorge. Cross suspension bridges, pass Chhongche caves, and ascend through pine forests and waterfalls past Dharmasala. Climb up to Meta (3,560 m), an open Tibetan plateau with views of Annapurna II and Himlung Himal. Overnight at lodge.

itinerary.title: Meta – Kyang
itinerary.highlights: Trek high desert valley along Phu Khola, pass Khampa winter settlements, views of Pisang Peak & Kangaru Himal.
itinerary.description: Trek along the Phu Khola through a high-altitude mountain desert featuring eroded clay cliffs, narrow gorges, and ancient seasonal Khampa settlements. Enjoy vistas of Pisang Peak and Kangaru Himal before arriving in Kyang (3,887 m). Overnight at lodge.

itinerary.title: Kyang – Phu Gaun
itinerary.highlights: Trek past ancient wooden gate of Phu, explore 800-year-old Tashi Lhakhang Monastery in historic Phu village.
itinerary.description: Ascend through dry, rugged canyon landscapes along glacial streams. Pass ancient chortens and stone Mani walls while looking for rare blue sheep on cliff slopes. Pass through the carved wooden entrance gate into ancient Phu Gaun (4,080 m). Visit Tashi Lhakhang Monastery blessed by the Dalai Lama. Overnight at lodge.

itinerary.title: Phu Gaun – Nar Phedi
itinerary.highlights: Descend Phu valley, cross suspension bridge at Phu Khola, stay at Nar Phedi Monastery.
itinerary.description: Trek back down the Phu valley past Kyang and Upper Chyako. Cross the suspension bridge over Phu Khola and ascend gently to Nar Phedi (3,490 m). Stay in the peaceful monastery lodge and observe evening butter lamp prayer rituals with resident monks. Overnight at lodge.

itinerary.title: Nar Phedi – Nar Village
itinerary.highlights: Ascend winding trail past chortens & yak pastures to ancient Nar village, visit 4 historic gompas.
itinerary.description: Climb steeply out of Nar Phedi past long lines of Mani walls and chortens into Nar Village (4,200 m). Nar is a traditional stone-built Gurung-Tibetan village larger than Phu. Explore its four main historic monasteries: Guru Choling, Samten Pelgye Ling, Kunsei Dechen, and Samdru Choling. Overnight at lodge.

itinerary.title: Acclimatization Day at Nar Village
itinerary.highlights: Rest and high-altitude acclimatization day, village walks, interaction with Tibetan weaving communities.
itinerary.description: Rest day in Nar village (4,200 m) to allow your body to properly adjust before heading into high wilderness camping over Teri La Pass. Take short walks up nearby ridges, observe local women weaving wool rugs, and rest. Overnight at lodge.

itinerary.title: Nar – Dharamshala / Lapse Kharka (Camping Begins)
itinerary.highlights: Leave lodge settlements behind, enter pristine alpine pastures at Dharamshala, set up tented camp.
itinerary.description: Leave Nar village and step onto the unpopulated wilderness trail leading towards Teri La Pass. Trek through high alpine meadows filled with wildflowers and grazing yaks. Reach Dharamshala (Lapse Kharka, 4,500 m) where your camping crew sets up sleeping, dining, and kitchen tents. Overnight at tented camp.

itinerary.title: Dharamshala – Pokhari
itinerary.highlights: Ascend past high glacial moraines & mountain tarns to Pokhari camp at 5,150 m.
itinerary.description: Trek uphill through rugged mountain terrain and lateral moraines. Gain altitude steadily as views of surrounding snow peaks expand. Arrive at Pokhari (5,150 m), a high alpine tarn meadow serving as a key acclimatization camp. Overnight at tented camp.

itinerary.title: Pokhari – Teri Bhanjyang Phedi
itinerary.accommodation: Tented Camp at Teri Bhanjyang Phedi
itinerary.highlights: Trek through high rocky scree slopes to High Base Camp of Teri La Pass.
itinerary.description: Trek across rocky scree and barren high-altitude plateaus towards the base of Teri La Pass. Reach Teri Bhanjyang Phedi (5,500 m), tucked beneath snow ridges. Prepare climbing gear and early morning pass crossing strategy with your guide. Overnight at tented camp.

itinerary.title: Teri Bhanjyang Phedi – Cross Teri La Pass (5,595 m) – Yak Kharka
itinerary.highlights: Pre-dawn start, climb steep snow/scree to Teri La Pass (5,595 m), 360° panoramas of Himlung Himal & Tibetan plateau, descent to Yak Kharka (4,600 m).
itinerary.description: Start before dawn for the steep and challenging climb to **Teri La Pass (5,595 m)**—the pinnacle of the expedition. Reach the flag-strewn summit pass for breathtaking panoramas of Himlung Himal, Annapurna II, Tilicho Peak, and the vast Tibetan plateau. Descend long scree and moraine slopes down into Upper Mustang territory at Yak Kharka (4,600 m). Overnight at tented camp.

itinerary.title: Yak Kharka – Bhedi Kharka (Camping Ends)
itinerary.highlights: Descend alpine pastures into Upper Mustang river valleys, final night of tented camping.
itinerary.description: Trek down from high alpine pastures through rolling grassy valleys and rocky ravines. Pass seasonal herder pastures where yaks and sheep graze. Reach Bhedi Kharka (3,450 m) for your final wilderness camp night. Overnight at tented camp.

itinerary.title: Bhedi Kharka – Tangge
itinerary.highlights: Descend into ancient Mustang village of Tangge, rejoin teahouse accommodation.
itinerary.description: Trek downhill into the isolated Upper Mustang village of Tangge (3,240 m). Tangge is famous for its long rows of colorful chortens, clay-walled houses, and peaceful remote atmosphere. Rejoin teahouse accommodation. Overnight at lodge.

itinerary.title: Tangge – Yara
itinerary.highlights: Cross Dhechang River, walk beneath wind-sculpted sandstone cliff pillars to Yara village.
itinerary.description: Trek out of Tangge across the Dhechang River and ascend gently past sculpted clay cliff formations. Reach Yara village (3,650 m), a peaceful hamlet nestled under vertical canyon walls with optional excursion towards Luri Gompa cave monastery. Overnight at lodge.

itinerary.title: Yara – Lo Manthang
itinerary.highlights: Trek across plateau, enter ancient walled city of Lo Manthang.
itinerary.description: Trek across dry desert plateaus, crossing small streams and passing ancient chortens. Reach the famous walled capital city of **Lo Manthang (3,810 m)**. Check into your lodge and stroll through historic narrow alleys. Overnight at lodge.

itinerary.title: Lo Manthang Exploration (Monasteries, Royal Palace & Chhoser Sky Caves)
itinerary.highlights: Jampa Gompa, Thubchen Gompa, Chhoede Gompa, 5-story Royal Palace & Jhong Sky Caves at Chhoser.
itinerary.description: Spend a full day exploring ancient Lo Manthang. Visit 15th-century Jampa Gompa, Thubchen Gompa, and active Chhoede Gompa. Take an excursion to Chhoser to explore Jhong Cave—a multi-story cliff dwelling used for centuries as meditation cells and refuge. Overnight at lodge.

itinerary.title: Lo Manthang – Charang (Tsarang)
itinerary.highlights: Cross Lo La pass, descend to Charang village, visit 5-story Tsarang Palace & monastery library.
itinerary.description: Trek out of Lo Manthang across Lo La pass (3,950 m) and descend into Charang (3,560 m). Visit the historic 5-story Tsarang Palace and the ancient monastery holding rare Buddhist scriptures. Overnight at lodge.

itinerary.title: Charang – Geling
itinerary.highlights: Trek past Ghemi's long Mani wall, cross Nyi La pass (4,010 m) to Geling.
itinerary.description: Trek past Ghemi village and its famous carved Mani wall. Cross Nyi La pass (4,010 m) and descend into Geling village (3,570 m), surrounded by wide barley fields. Overnight at lodge.

itinerary.title: Geling – Chele
itinerary.highlights: Trek through Syangbochen & Samar past red canyon walls down to Chele.
itinerary.description: Trek back through Syangbochen and poplar-shaded Samar village, descending through narrow red rock gorges down to Chele (3,050 m). Overnight at lodge.

itinerary.title: Chele – Kagbeni
itinerary.highlights: Trek past Chhusang & Tangbe stone houses to Kagbeni gateway town.
itinerary.description: Trek past Chhusang red cliffs and Tangbe apple orchards back to Kagbeni (2,810 m), completing the restricted Upper Mustang loop. Overnight at lodge.

itinerary.title: Kagbeni – Jomsom
itinerary.highlights: Gentle trek along Kali Gandaki riverbed back to Jomsom, celebration with crew.
itinerary.description: Trek or drive gently along the Kali Gandaki riverbed past Ekle Bhatti back to Jomsom (2,700 m). Celebrate the completion of the 27-day expedition with your guide and camping crew. Overnight at lodge.

itinerary.title: Jomsom – Pokhara – Kathmandu
itinerary.highlights: Morning flight Jomsom – Pokhara – Kathmandu with views of Annapurna & Dhaulagiri.
itinerary.description: Take an early morning flight from Jomsom to Pokhara (25 mins), connecting directly to your flight back to Kathmandu (25 mins). Transfer to your hotel and rest after the expedition. Overnight at hotel.

itinerary.title: Free Day in Kathmandu
itinerary.highlights: Relaxation, spa treatments, Thamel shopping, official farewell dinner.
itinerary.description: Reserve day in Kathmandu for rest, shopping, or optional sightseeing. In the evening, join your Zenex Travels team for an official farewell dinner with traditional cultural performances. Overnight at hotel.

itinerary.highlights: Airport transfer for international departure flight.
itinerary.description: Enjoy breakfast at your hotel. At your scheduled departure time, your Zenex Travels representative will transfer you by private vehicle to Tribhuvan International Airport for your return flight home.

treks.difficultyInfo: The 27-day Nar Phu and Upper Mustang Trek is graded HARD. It involves high pass crossing over Teri La Pass (5,595 m), multi-day wilderness camping in remote unpopulated terrain, and 5 to 11 hours of daily walking over steep scree and high desert trails. Experienced physical fitness, stamina, and prior high-altitude trekking experience are essential.

altitudeSickness.description: Reaching a maximum altitude of 5,595 meters at Teri La Pass, altitude sickness (AMS) is a significant factor. Gradual ascending stages, built-in acclimatization days at Nar (4,200 m), and experienced guide monitoring ensure safety.
prevention: Maintain a slow, steady pace during high pass climbs.
Follow acclimatization rest days built into the 27-day itinerary.
Drink 3 to 4 liters of clean water and warm fluids daily.
Avoid alcohol, smoking, and notify your Zenex Travels guide immediately if feeling unwell.

items: Fleece jacket & heavy expedition down jacket (-15°C rated)
Heavy waterproof gloves & inner fleece gloves

extendedInfo.title: Teri La Pass (5,595 m) – High Mountain Remote Pass
extendedInfo.description: Teri La Pass (5,595 m) is one of Nepal's most remote high-altitude pass crossings, connecting Nar Phu Valley in Manang directly to Upper Mustang through uninhabited alpine wilderness.

extendedInfo.title: Nar Phu Valley – Forbidden Valleys of Manang
extendedInfo.description: Opened to foreign trekkers only in 2003, Nar Phu Valley preserves ancient stone villages, uncrowded trails, and traditional Tibetan-Buddhist heritage.

extendedInfo.title: Lo Manthang – Walled Capital of Mustang
extendedInfo.description: Founded in 1380, Lo Manthang is a medieval walled fortress city preserving royal palaces, ancient monasteries, and living Tibetan culture.

extendedInfo.title: Why Trek with Zenex Travels & Tours?
extendedInfo.description: Zenex Travels & Tours brings over two decades of high-altitude Himalayan logistics experience, licensed guides, camping crews, and transparent pricing.

faqs.question: How long is the Nar Phu and Upper Mustang Trek?
faqs.answer: The full expedition takes 27 days from arrival to departure in Kathmandu, covering Nar Phu, Teri La Pass (5,595 m), and Upper Mustang.

faqs.question: Do I need special permits for this trek?
faqs.answer: Yes, you need Nar Phu Restricted Area Permit, Upper Mustang Restricted Area Permit (USD 500 for 10 days), and ACAP permit. Zenex Travels & Tours handles all permit arrangements.

faqs.question: What is the difficulty level of the trek?
faqs.answer: It is rated HARD due to crossing a 5,595 m high mountain pass, 5 nights of wilderness camping, and 5-11 hours of daily walking in remote high-altitude terrain.

faqs.question: When is the best time for the Nar Phu & Upper Mustang Trek?
faqs.answer: Spring (March to May) and Autumn (September to November) offer clear weather, dry pass conditions, and excellent mountain visibility.

faqs.question: Is this trek suitable for beginners?
faqs.answer: No, this trek is recommended for experienced trekkers with prior multi-day high altitude experience and high physical fitness.

faqs.question: What accommodation is available on the trek?
faqs.answer: A mix of teahouses/lodges in villages (Meta, Kyang, Phu, Nar, Tangge, Lo Manthang) and full wilderness tented camping during the pass crossing (Dharamshala to Bhedi Kharka).

faqs.question: What food will I get during the trek?
faqs.answer: Freshly cooked meals by the camping crew during camping days, and traditional local Dal Bhat, momos, noodles, soups, and pancakes in teahouses.

faqs.question: Will I experience altitude sickness?
faqs.answer: The trek reaches 5,595 m at Teri La Pass. Acclimatization rest days built into the 27-day itinerary help your body adjust gradually.

faqs.question: Do I need a licensed guide?
faqs.answer: Yes, government regulations require at least 2 trekkers accompanied by a licensed guide from a registered agency like Zenex Travels & Tours.

faqs.question: How do I prepare physically?
faqs.answer: Train 2-3 months in advance with cardio, stair climbing, hiking with a backpack, and leg strength conditioning.

faqs.question: What should I pack?
faqs.answer: Pack four-season sleeping bag (-15°C), expedition down jacket, Gore-Tex outerwear, sturdy high-altitude boots, thermal layers, and headlamp.

faqs.question: Is internet or mobile signal available?
faqs.answer: Mobile network works in lower villages and Jomsom/Lo Manthang, but there is no mobile signal or Wi-Fi during the high pass camping days.

faqs.question: How do I book this trek?
faqs.answer: Contact Zenex Travels & Tours to customize your departure dates, confirm permit requirements, and reserve your expedition slot.

treks.overview:
Kanchenjunga North Base Camp Trek 17 Days | Expedition to Mount Kanchenjunga (8,586 m)

The Kanchenjunga North Base Camp Trek (17 Days) is one of Nepal's most spectacular off-the-beaten-path mountain adventures. Located in far eastern Nepal, this trek takes you to the foot of Mount Kanchenjunga (8,586 m)—the world's third-highest peak. The northern route leads directly to the primary north base camp at Pangpema (5,143 m), offering a rare opportunity to sleep under the formidable north face of this Himalayan giant.

Passing through the peaceful trails of the Kanchenjunga Conservation Area, trekkers encounter remote settlements such as Sekathum, Amjilasa, Gyabla, Ghunsa, Khambachen, and Lhonak. Enjoy breathtaking panoramas of towering peaks including Kumbhakarna (Mount Jannu – 7,710 m), Wedge Peak, Nepal Peak, Kirat Chuli, and Pathibhara Peak, alongside the massive Kanchenjunga Glacier.

At Zenex Travels & Tours, we provide personalized trek arrangements—including domestic flights (Kathmandu – Bhadrapur), private jeep overland transfers to Taplejung and Sekathum, Kanchenjunga Conservation Area Permits (KCAP), Special Restricted Area Permits (RAP), expert local English-speaking guides, experienced mountain porters, teahouse accommodations, all meals, and hotel stay in Kathmandu.
highlights: Stand at Kanchenjunga North Base Camp (Pangpema – 5,143 m) and witness jaw-dropping views of Mount Kanchenjunga (8,586 m).
Experience peaceful nights in remote high-altitude settlements surrounded by dramatic glaciers and high peaks.
Trek through unspoiled landscapes, deep river gorges, and alpine forests in one of Nepal's least-explored regions.
Explore traditional Sherpa, Limbu, and Tibetan-influenced villages of Ghunsa, Khambachen, Lhonak, and Gyabla.
Traverse the Kanchenjunga Conservation Area with opportunities to spot rare wildlife like red pandas and Himalayan blue sheep.
Enjoy spectacular panoramic views of Kumbhakarna (Jannu – 7,710 m), Wedge Peak, Nepal Peak, and Tent Peak.
Scenic overland drive through the tea gardens of Ilam and Taplejung in eastern Nepal.
Full logistics support by Zenex Travels & Tours including permits, flights, private transport, guide, and porters.

itinerary.description: Welcome to Nepal! We will host a pre-trip briefing meeting to introduce your guide and answer any questions. Rest of the day is at your leisure.

itinerary.description: While our team submits your passport details to immigration to acquire the Kanchenjunga Special Restricted Area Permit, you enjoy a free day exploring UNESCO World Heritage Sites in Kathmandu, such as Pashupatinath, Boudhanath Stupa, and Bhaktapur Durbar Square.

itinerary.title: Kathmandu - Bhadrapur (Flight) & Drive to Taplejung (1,820 m)
itinerary.description: After breakfast, transfer to Kathmandu airport for a scenic 45-minute flight to Bhadrapur in eastern Nepal. Meet your local transportation team and embark on a scenic 7 to 8 hour overland drive (214 km) through the rolling tea gardens of Ilam to Taplejung.

itinerary.title: Taplejung - Sekathum (1,585 m)
itinerary.description: Board a private 4WD local jeep for a 4 to 5 hour drive (31 km) to Sekathum. The rugged dirt road winds alongside terraced farmlands, traditional Limbu and Sherpa settlements, and dense forested hills above the Tamor River.

itinerary.title: Sekathum - Amjilasa (2,395 m)
itinerary.description: Begin your on-foot trekking adventure along the Ghunsa Khola valley. The 6-hour trail ascends through dense bamboo and rhododendron forests, crossing suspension bridges and cascading waterfalls over stone staircases to reach the quiet cliffside village of Amjilasa.

itinerary.title: Amjilasa - Gyabla (2,730 m)
itinerary.description: Trek for about 6 hours through mature oak and dense rhododendron forests. Watch for soaring eagles overhead and yaks grazing in lush glades as you pass Thyangyan before ascending gently to Gyabla, a serene Tibetan-Sherpa village settlement.

itinerary.title: Gyabla - Ghunsa (3,427 m)
itinerary.description: Follow the trail for 7 hours into higher mountain terrain, walking past Phale village where Tibetan refugees reside and produce traditional handicrafts. Cross iron bridges over Ghunsa Khola to reach Ghunsa—the largest village in the valley with teahouses, health post, and Kanchenjunga Conservation Area office.

itinerary.title: Ghunsa - Khambachen (4,050 m)
itinerary.description: Trek for 5 hours through pine and larch forests alongside glacial melt rivers. Pass mani walls and prayer flags as mountain vistas open up to display Mount Kumbhakarna (Jannu), Nupchu Himal, and Chang Himal. Overnight at teahouse in Khambachen.

itinerary.title: Acclimatization Day in Khambachen (Hiking to Kumbhakarna Base Camp)
itinerary.description: Essential acclimatization day. Take a side hike uphill (approx. 3 hours) towards Kumbhakarna (Jannu) Base Camp (4,100 m) for stunning close-up views of the sheer rock face of Jannu. Return to Khambachen for rest and overnight.

itinerary.title: Khambachen - Lhonak (4,780 m)
itinerary.description: Ascend gradually over rocky moraines and boulder fields alongside the massive Kanchenjunga Glacier. Pass Ramtang viewpoint with views of Mera Peak, Kirat Chuli, and Nepal Peak. Reach the high windswept plateau of Lhonak after 5 hours.

itinerary.title: Lhonak - Kanchenjunga North Base Camp (Pangpema – 5,143 m) - Lhonak
itinerary.description: Highlight of the expedition! Depart early morning on a 3.5-hour trek along the lateral moraine of Kanchenjunga Glacier to reach Pangpema (5,143 m). Marvel at the gigantic north wall of Mt. Kanchenjunga (8,586 m), Wedge Peak, Tent Peak, and Nepal Peak. After soaking in the views, descend back to Lhonak (2 hours).

itinerary.title: Lhonak - Ghunsa (3,427 m)
itinerary.description: Retrace your steps down the valley past Khambachen, descending through high-alpine landscapes along the Tamur River to Ghunsa (6 to 7 hours walking). Enjoy a warm meal and comfortable teahouse stay.

itinerary.title: Ghunsa - Sekathum (1,585 m)
itinerary.description: Begin a long descent down the Ghunsa Khola gorge past Gyabla and Amjilasa, returning to subtropical lower elevations at Sekathum (approx. 7 to 8 hours).

itinerary.title: Sekathum - Taplejung - Ilam (1,200 m)
itinerary.description: Board a private jeep from Sekathum to Taplejung and continue overland to Ilam (7 to 8 hours total drive). Enjoy the lush tea gardens and cooler climate of Nepal's famed tea country.

itinerary.title: Ilam - Bhadrapur (Drive) & Fly to Kathmandu (1,350 m)
itinerary.description: Drive from Ilam to Bhadrapur Airport (2.5 hours) and catch your domestic flight back to Kathmandu. Upon arrival in Kathmandu, transfer to your hotel for rest and relaxation.

itinerary.title: Free Buffer / Rest Day in Kathmandu
itinerary.description: A reserve day in Kathmandu in case of flight or road delays in eastern Nepal. Use the day for relaxing, shopping in Thamel, or visiting city attractions. Farewell dinner hosted by Zenex Travels & Tours in the evening.

itinerary.title: Final Departure from Kathmandu
itinerary.description: Enjoy breakfast at the hotel. Our Zenex Travels & Tours representative will transfer you to Tribhuvan International Airport 3 hours prior to your international flight departure.

treks.essentialInfo:
Essential Information for Kanchenjunga North Base Camp Trek

Permits Required

Trekking in the Kanchenjunga region requires two mandatory permits:

  • Kanchenjunga Conservation Area Permit (KCAP): NPR 3,000 per person.
  • Special Restricted Area Permit (RAP): USD $20 per person per week.

Due to restricted area regulations, solo trekking is prohibited. A minimum of two trekkers accompanied by a licensed guide from a registered agency like Zenex Travels & Tours is required.

Best Time to Trek

The optimal trekking seasons are:

  • Spring (March to May): Mild temperatures, vibrant rhododendron blooms, and clear morning mountain views.
  • Autumn (September to November): Stable weather, dry trails, and exceptional mountain clarity post-monsoon.

Accommodations & Meals

Lodges along the Kanchenjunga trail are basic family-run teahouses. Rooms are simple twin-sharing with shared facilities. High-altitude lodges (Lhonak, Pangpema) have minimal amenities, so a quality -10°C to -15°C sleeping bag is required.

Group Tariff (2026/2027)

  • 2 - 3 Pax: US$ 1,720 per person
  • 4 - 7 Pax: US$ 1,505 per person
  • 8 - 11 Pax: US$ 1,470 per person
  • 12 - 15 Pax: US$ 1,400 per person

faqs.question: Where is Kanchenjunga North Base Camp located?
faqs.answer: Kanchenjunga North Base Camp (Pangpema) is situated at an elevation of 5,143 meters in Taplejung district of far eastern Nepal, near the borders of Sikkim and Tibet.

faqs.question: How difficult is the Kanchenjunga North Base Camp Trek?
faqs.answer: The trek is graded Hard. It involves reaching high altitudes (up to 5,143 m), remote terrain, daily walks of 5 to 8 hours, and basic teahouse facilities. Good physical fitness and prior trekking experience are recommended.

faqs.question: What is the highest altitude on Kanchenjunga North BC Trek?
faqs.answer: The highest point of the trek is Kanchenjunga North Base Camp (Pangpema) at 5,143 meters (16,873 feet).

faqs.question: Do I need a special permit for Kanchenjunga trekking?
faqs.answer: Yes, you need the Kanchenjunga Conservation Area Permit (KCAP) and the Special Restricted Area Permit (RAP). RAP requires a minimum of 2 trekkers accompanied by a licensed guide.

faqs.question: What is the best time to trek to Kanchenjunga North Base Camp?
faqs.answer: Spring (March to May) and Autumn (September to November) offer the best weather, clear skies, and safe trail conditions.

faqs.question: How remote is the Kanchenjunga region?
faqs.answer: Kanchenjunga is one of Nepal's most remote, quiet, and unspoiled regions, receiving very few trekkers each year compared to Everest or Annapurna.

faqs.question: What kind of accommodation is available during Kanchenjunga trek?
faqs.answer: Accommodation is in basic family-run teahouses with twin beds and shared toilets. High-altitude stops like Lhonak are rustic, so warm sleeping bags are necessary.

faqs.question: Can Kanchenjunga North Base Camp be done solo?
faqs.answer: No, Nepal government restricted area regulations require at least 2 travelers trekking together with a licensed guide.

faqs.question: What makes the Kanchenjunga North BC trek special?
faqs.answer: It provides breathtaking close-up views of Mt. Kanchenjunga (8,586 m), Mt. Jannu/Kumbhakarna, vast glaciers, pristine Himalayan wilderness, and authentic Tibetan/Limbu cultural encounters without commercial crowds.

faqs.question: Is travel insurance mandatory for Kanchenjunga trekking?
faqs.answer: Yes, travel insurance covering emergency high-altitude medical evacuation up to 6,000 meters is mandatory.

treks.overview:
Kanchenjunga South Base Camp Trek 14 Days | Untouched Eastern Himalayan Wilderness

The Kanchenjunga South Base Camp Trek (14 Days) is one of the shortest yet most rewarding journeys in eastern Nepal, taking trekkers to the foot of Mount Kanchenjunga (8,586 m)—the third-highest mountain on Earth. This off-the-beaten-path route inside the Kanchenjunga Conservation Area offers an ideal blend of raw high-altitude scenery, deep solitude, and authentic cultural immersion.

The crowning highlight of the trek is reaching Oktang View Point (4,730 m), offering jaw-dropping views of the south and west faces of Mount Kanchenjunga (8,586 m), Yalung Kang (8,505 m), Khambachen Peak (7,903 m), Kabru Range, and the expansive Yalung Glacier. Along the trail, trekkers pass through terraced farmlands, lush rhododendron forests, and traditional Rai, Limbu, and Sherpa villages like Yasang, Tortang, Tseram, and Ramche.

At Zenex Travels & Tours, we handle every detail of your expedition—including domestic flights (Kathmandu – Bhadrapur), private jeep transfers to Taplejung and Hellok, Kanchenjunga Conservation Area Permits (KCAP), Special Restricted Area Permits (RAP), licensed local English-speaking guides, experienced porters, lodge reservations, and hotel stays in Kathmandu.
highlights: Stand at Oktang View Point (4,730 m) for breathtaking 360-degree panoramas of Mt. Kanchenjunga (8,586 m) South Face and Yalung Glacier.
Enjoy spectacular views of Yalung Kang (8,505 m), Khambachen Peak (7,903 m), Rathong (6,678 m), and Kabru Peaks.
Explore the pristine wilderness of Kanchenjunga Conservation Area, home to red pandas, Himalayan black bears, and rare birds.
Trek through changing eco-zones—from subtropical bamboo and rhododendron forests to high alpine meadows and glacial valleys.
Experience authentic hospitality, ancient traditions, and animist/Buddhist culture in Rai, Limbu, and Sherpa villages.

itinerary.description: Fly early morning (45 mins) from Kathmandu to Bhadrapur in eastern Nepal. Meet your local drive crew and embark on a scenic 7 to 8 hour overland drive (214 km) through the lush tea hills of Ilam to Taplejung.

itinerary.title: Taplejung - Hellok (1,550 m) - Kyansar / Yasang (1,700 m)
itinerary.description: Drive off-road by private 4WD jeep from Taplejung to Hellok (approx. 6 hours) along the Tamor River. After lunch in Hellok, begin trekking uphill through bamboo forests for 2.5 hours to reach Yasang (1,700 m). Overnight at lodge.

itinerary.title: Kyansar / Yasang - Tortang (2,995 m)
itinerary.description: Trek for 6 hours alongside the Amji Khola river, walking through pristine pine and rhododendron forests and high pasture lands. Reach Tortang (2,995 m) by afternoon and stay at a local lodge.

itinerary.title: Tortang - Tseram (3870 m)
itinerary.description: Trek uphill for 4 to 5 hours through dense high-altitude forest following the Simbuwa Khola. As you reach Tseram (3,870 m), enjoy stunning views of Rathong Peak (6,678 m). Tseram is a traditional Limbu settlement. Overnight at lodge.

itinerary.title: Tseram - Ramche (4,580 m)
itinerary.description: Ascend gradually through alpine meadows for 3 to 4 hours, passing grazing yaks and glacial streams. Visuals of Mt. Kokthang (6,148 m), Rathong (6,678 m), and Boktoh (6,020 m) greet you on arrival at Ramche.

itinerary.title: Ramche - Oktang View Point (4,730 m) - Ramche (4,580 m)
itinerary.description: Highlight day! Early morning hike (2 hours) along the lateral moraine of Yalung Glacier to Oktang View Point (4,730 m). Marvel at the dramatic 360-degree views of Kanchenjunga South (8,586 m), Yalung Kang (8,505 m), and Khambachen Peak (7,903 m). Visit local Limbu shrine before descending back to Ramche.

itinerary.title: Ramche - Tseram - Tortang (2,995 m)
itinerary.description: Descend from Ramche past Tseram following the Simbuwa Khola down to Tortang (approx. 7 hours walking). Enjoy the warmer air as you re-enter forested terrain.

itinerary.title: Tortang - Kyansar / Yasang (1,700 m)
itinerary.description: Retrace your trail down through bamboo and pine forests to Yasang / Kyansar (5 to 6 hours walking). Stay overnight at a local mountain lodge.

itinerary.title: Yasang - Hellok (Trek) - Taplejung - Ilam (1,200 m) (Drive)
itinerary.description: Trek 2 hours down to Hellok, then board your private jeep to drive via Taplejung to Ilam (8 hours total drive). Relax in the peaceful surroundings of Ilam's renowned tea plantations.

itinerary.title: Ilam - Bhadrapur (Drive) & Fly to Kathmandu (1,350 m)
itinerary.description: Drive 2.5 hours from Ilam to Bhadrapur Airport and fly back to Kathmandu. Transfer to your hotel and enjoy free time in the evening.

itinerary.title: Free Day in Kathmandu (Optional Sightseeing / Everest Flight)
itinerary.description: A free leisure day in Kathmandu for optional mountain flights over Mt. Everest, exploring souvenir markets in Thamel, or visiting World Heritage Sites like Boudhanath Stupa and Bhaktapur.

itinerary.title: Final Departure from Kathmandu
itinerary.description: Enjoy breakfast at the hotel. Our Zenex Travels & Tours representative will transfer you to Tribhuvan International Airport 3 hours prior to your international flight departure.

treks.essentialInfo:
Essential Information for Kanchenjunga South Base Camp Trek

Permits Required

Trekking in the Kanchenjunga region requires two mandatory permits:

  • Kanchenjunga Conservation Area Permit (KCAP): NPR 2,000 per person.
  • Special Restricted Area Permit (RAP): Required for entry into restricted zones, issued via registered agencies like Zenex Travels & Tours. Minimum 2 trekkers required.

Best Time to Trek

The optimal trekking seasons are:

  • Spring (March to May): Mild temperatures, blooming rhododendrons, and clear morning vistas.
  • Autumn (September to November): Crisp air, post-monsoon clarity, and stable weather.

Accommodations & Meals

Accommodation is in basic family-run teahouses with simple twin rooms and shared facilities. Bringing a warm -10°C sleeping bag is recommended for higher stops like Ramche (4,580 m).

Group Tariff (2026/2027)

  • 2 - 3 Pax: US$ 1,590 per person
  • 4 - 7 Pax: US$ 1,390 per person
  • 8 - 11 Pax: US$ 1,350 per person

faqs.question: Where is Kanchenjunga South Base Camp located?
faqs.answer: Kanchenjunga South Base Camp (Oktang View Point) is located in the Taplejung district of eastern Nepal, facing the dramatic south face of Mt. Kanchenjunga (8,586 m).

faqs.question: How difficult is the Kanchenjunga South Base Camp Trek?
faqs.answer: The trek is graded Moderate. It reaches a peak elevation of 4,730 m at Oktang View Point and highest sleeping altitude of 4,580 m at Ramche. It involves 4 to 7 hours of daily walking.

faqs.question: What is the highest point on Kanchenjunga South BC Trek?
faqs.answer: The highest point reached on the trek is Oktang View Point at 4,730 meters (15,518 feet).

faqs.question: Do I need special permits for Kanchenjunga South Base Camp Trek?
faqs.answer: Yes, you need the Kanchenjunga Conservation Area Permit (KCAP) and the Special Restricted Area Permit (RAP), which requires a minimum of 2 trekkers and a licensed guide.

faqs.question: What is the best time to trek Kanchenjunga South BC?
faqs.answer: Spring (March to May) and Autumn (September to November) offer the clearest mountain views, pleasant temperatures, and dry trails.

faqs.question: What scenery can I expect from Oktang View Point?
faqs.answer: Oktang View Point offers breathtaking close-up panoramas of Mt. Kanchenjunga (8,586 m) South Face, Yalung Kang (8,505 m), Khambachen Peak (7,903 m), Kabru range, and the expansive Yalung Glacier.

faqs.question: What kind of accommodation is available on the trek?
faqs.answer: Accommodation is in basic local teahouses with twin-share rooms and shared toilets. Warm sleeping bags are recommended for higher elevations.

faqs.question: Can I trek Kanchenjunga South Base Camp solo?
faqs.answer: No, restricted area regulations in Nepal require a minimum of 2 trekkers accompanied by a licensed guide from a registered agency.

faqs.question: Is travel insurance mandatory?
faqs.answer: Yes, travel insurance covering medical expenses and emergency high-altitude helicopter evacuation up to 5,000 meters is compulsory.

faqs.question: How do I book this trek?
faqs.answer: Contact Zenex Travels & Tours to customize your departure dates, process restricted permits, and reserve your expedition.

treks.overview:
Kanchenjunga Circuit Trek 22 Days | Full Expedition to North & South Base Camps

The Kanchenjunga Circuit Trek (22 Days) is the ultimate high-altitude adventure in eastern Nepal, taking seasoned trekkers to both the North Base Camp (Pangpema – 5,143 m) and South Base Camp (Yalung – 5,400 m) of Mount Kanchenjunga (8,586 m)—the world's third-highest peak. As a key section of Nepal's Great Himalayan Trail (GHT), this circuit traverses raw, uncrowded landscapes from subtropical bamboo forests to glacial moraines.

The expedition crosses three challenging high-altitude Himalayan passes: Sele La (4,290 m), Sinion La (4,646 m), and Mirgin Pass (4,480 m), offering 360-degree panoramas of Mt. Kanchenjunga, Mt. Jannu (Kumbhakarna – 7,711 m), Yalung Kang (8,505 m), Kabru Peaks, and Rathong. Along the circuit, explore authentic Sherpa and Limbu villages like Ghunsa, Gyabla, Khambachen, Lhonak, Tseram, and Ramche.

At Zenex Travels & Tours, we provide complete, professional expedition logistics—including domestic flights (Kathmandu – Bhadrapur), private 4WD jeep transfers to Taplejung and Sekathum, Kanchenjunga Conservation Area Permits (KCAP), Special Restricted Area Permits (RAP), licensed English-speaking mountain guides, experienced porters, lodge bookings, and 3-star hotel stays in Kathmandu.
highlights: Visit both Kanchenjunga North Base Camp (Pangpema – 5,143 m) and Yalung South Base Camp (5,400 m) on a single 22-day circuit.
Cross three high Himalayan passes above 4,000 meters: Sele La (4,290 m), Sinion La (4,646 m), and Mirgin Pass (4,480 m).
Stand at Oktang View Point (4,730 m) for jaw-dropping close-up views of Kanchenjunga South Face and Yalung Glacier.
Marvel at towering peaks: Kumbhakarna (Jannu – 7,711 m), Yalung Kang (8,505 m), Nepal Peak, Tent Peak, and Kabru Range.
Trek along a key section of the Great Himalayan Trail (GHT) through pristine, uncrowded eastern wilderness.
Immerse in authentic Sherpa, Limbu, and Rai mountain heritage in villages like Ghunsa, Gyabla, and Phale.
Explore the Kanchenjunga Conservation Area, sanctuary for red pandas, blue sheep, and rare Himalayan wildlife.
Overland jeep travel through the scenic tea gardens of Ilam and Taplejung.
Full expedition management by Zenex Travels & Tours with permits, flights, private transport, guide, and porters.

itinerary.title: Arrival in Kathmandu (1,350 m)
itinerary.description: Welcome to Nepal! Upon arrival at Tribhuvan International Airport (TIA) in Kathmandu, you will be met by our representative from Zenex Travels & Tours and transferred to your hotel. Pre-trip briefing meeting held in the evening.

itinerary.title: Free Day in Kathmandu for Permit Preparation & Sightseeing
itinerary.description: Free day in Kathmandu while our team submits passport details to immigration to issue the Kanchenjunga Special Restricted Area Permit. Option to explore UNESCO World Heritage Sites like Boudhanath, Pashupatinath, or Bhaktapur.

itinerary.title: Kathmandu - Bhadrapur (Flight) & Drive to Taplejung (1,820 m)
itinerary.description: Morning 45-minute domestic flight from Kathmandu to Bhadrapur. Meet your driver and proceed on a 7 to 8 hour overland jeep drive (214 km) through the rolling tea gardens of Ilam to Taplejung.

itinerary.title: Taplejung - Sekathum (1,585 m)
itinerary.description: Drive off-road by private jeep (4 to 5 hours) to Sekathum along the Tamor River valley, passing terraced farms and rural Limbu/Sherpa villages.

itinerary.title: Sekathum - Amjilasa (2,395 m)
itinerary.description: Begin trekking along Ghunsa Khola valley. Ascend stone staircases through bamboo and rhododendron forests, crossing suspension bridges to reach the cliffside village of Amjilasa (6 hours).

itinerary.title: Amjilasa - Gyabla (2,730 m)
itinerary.description: Trek for 6 hours past Thyangyan through oak and rhododendron forests. Spot yaks grazing in meadows as you reach the Tibetan-Sherpa village of Gyabla.

itinerary.title: Gyabla - Ghunsa (3,427 m)
itinerary.description: Trek 7 hours past Phale village—a Tibetan refugee settlement—crossing iron bridges over Ghunsa Khola to Ghunsa (3,427 m), the largest Sherpa settlement in the region.

itinerary.title: Ghunsa - Khambachen (4,050 m)
itinerary.description: Ascend through pine and larch forests alongside Ghunsa Khola. Pass mani walls as mountain views of Mt. Jannu (Kumbhakarna) open up. Reach Khambachen in 5 hours.

itinerary.title: Acclimatization Day in Khambachen (Hiking to Kumbhakarna Base Camp)
itinerary.description: Rest and acclimatize in Khambachen. Take a 3-hour side hike uphill to Kumbhakarna Base Camp (4,100 m) for dramatic views of Mount Jannu's sheer north face.

itinerary.title: Khambachen - Lhonak (4,780 m)
itinerary.description: Ascend over rocky glacial moraines past Ramtang viewpoint with views of Kirat Chuli and Mera Peak. Reach the windswept plateau of Lhonak after 5 hours.

itinerary.title: Lhonak - Kanchenjunga North Base Camp (Pangpema – 5,143 m) - Lhonak
itinerary.description: Early departure on a 3.5-hour trek along Kanchenjunga Glacier to North Base Camp (Pangpema – 5,143 m). Enjoy spectacular close-up views of Mt. Kanchenjunga (8,586 m). Return to Lhonak (2 hours).

itinerary.title: Lhonak - Khambachen - Ghunsa (3,427 m)
itinerary.description: Descend back down the valley past Khambachen to Ghunsa (6 to 7 hours walking). Enjoy a warm meal and rest in preparation for the high passes.

itinerary.title: Ghunsa - Selele Phedi (4,000 m)
itinerary.description: Leave Ghunsa and climb steeply through rhododendron and juniper forests into high alpine pastures. Reach the staging point of Selele Phedi (4,000 m) after 5 to 6 hours.

itinerary.title: Selele Phedi - Sele La (4,480 m) - Sinion La (4,646 m) - Mirgin Pass (4,480 m) - Tseram (3,870 m)
itinerary.description: High pass crossing day! Early morning start (5 AM) traversing three passes: Sele La (4,480 m), Sinion La (4,646 m), and Mirgin Pass (4,480 m). Enjoy views of Kabru, Talung, and Kanchenjunga South before descending to Tseram (7 hours).

itinerary.title: Tseram - Ramche (4,580 m)
itinerary.description: Ascend wide Yalung Valley along glacial streams for 5 hours, passing Lapsang to reach Ramche (4,580 m) with views of Rathong and Kokthang.

itinerary.title: Ramche - Yalung Base Camp (5,400 m) / Oktang View Point (4,730 m) - Ramche
itinerary.description: Hike along Yalung Glacier to Oktang View Point (4,730 m) for panoramas of Kanchenjunga South Face and Yalung Kang (8,505 m). Continue to Yalung Base Camp (5,400 m) before descending to Ramche (7 to 8 hours round trip).

itinerary.title: Ramche - Tortang (2,995 m)
itinerary.description: Descend along Simbuwa Khola through high alpine and rhododendron forests to Tortang (7 hours walking).

itinerary.title: Tortang - Kyansar / Yasang (1,700 m)
itinerary.description: Continue descending through bamboo and pine forests to Yasang / Kyansar (5 to 6 hours).

itinerary.title: Yasang - Hellok (Trek) - Taplejung / Ilam (1,200 m) (Drive)
itinerary.description: Trek 2 hours down to Hellok, then board a private jeep for a 7 to 8 hour drive via Taplejung to Ilam / Kanyam tea gardens.

itinerary.title: Ilam / Taplejung - Bhadrapur (Drive) & Fly to Kathmandu (1,350 m)
itinerary.description: Drive from Ilam to Bhadrapur Airport (7 to 8 hours drive from Taplejung or 2.5 hours from Ilam) and catch your domestic flight back to Kathmandu. Overnight at hotel.

itinerary.title: Free Buffer / Sightseeing Day in Kathmandu
itinerary.description: Reserve day in Kathmandu for rest, optional UNESCO World Heritage sightseeing, or souvenir shopping in Thamel. Farewell dinner hosted by Zenex Travels & Tours.

itinerary.title: Final Departure from Kathmandu
itinerary.description: Breakfast at hotel. Our Zenex Travels & Tours correspondent will pick you up and transfer you to Kathmandu Airport for your international flight.

treks.overview:
Lower Dolpo Trek from Jhuphal 18 Days | High Altitude Wilderness & Phoksundo Lake Expedition

The Lower Dolpo Trek from Jhuphal (18 Days) offers an extraordinary expedition through one of Nepal's most remote, pristine, and culturally rich trans-Himalayan regions. Flying into Juphal in western Nepal, trekkers journey through rugged river gorges, windswept high plateaus, and ancient stone villages like Dho-Tarap before arriving at the ethereal turquoise waters of Shey Phoksundo Lake (3,641 m).

This challenging expedition crosses two high-altitude mountain passes: Numa La Pass (5,238 m) and Bagala Pass (5,169 m), presenting breathtaking panoramas of Mount Kanjiroba and the Dhaulagiri range. The trail traverses Shey Phoksundo National Park, immersing trekkers in pre-Buddhist Bon culture, ancient gompas, and uncrowded alpine wilderness.

At Zenex Travels & Tours, we manage all expedition details—including domestic flights (Kathmandu – Nepalgunj – Juphal round trip), Lower Dolpo Restricted Area Permits (RAP), Shey Phoksundo National Park Entry Permits, full tented camping crew (cook, kitchen staff, mules/yaks), licensed mountain guide, lodge arrangements, and hotel stays in Kathmandu and Nepalgunj.
highlights: Cross two formidable high mountain passes above 5,000 meters: Numa La Pass (5,238 m) and Bagala Pass (5,169 m).
Visit Shey Phoksundo Lake (3,641 m)—Nepal's deepest and most sacred turquoise-blue lake surrounded by dramatic cliffs.
Explore Dho-Tarap (3,944 m)—one of the highest permanent human settlements on Earth with authentic Bonpo and Tibetan Buddhist culture.
Visit ancient spiritual sites including Ribo Bhumpa Gompa, Drakmar Dewa, and traditional Bon monasteries in Ringmo.
Trek through Shey Phoksundo National Park, sanctuary for rare wildlife like snow leopards, blue sheep, and Himalayan thar.
Experience a mix of mountain lodge stays and full wilderness tented camping with dedicated kitchen crew.
Scenic mountain flights connecting Kathmandu, Nepalgunj, and the remote airstrip of Juphal in Dolpa.
Comprehensive expedition management by Zenex Travels & Tours with permits, flights, camping logistics, guide, and staff.
