itinerary.title: Arrival in Kathmandu (1,350 m)
itinerary.description: Welcome to Nepal! Upon arrival at Tribhuvan International Airport (TIA) in Kathmandu, our Zenex Travels & Tours representative greets you and transfers you to your hotel. Pre-trip briefing meeting in the evening.

itinerary.title: Kathmandu: Permit Preparation & Sightseeing
itinerary.description: Free day in Kathmandu while our team submits your passport and visa copies to Nepal Immigration to issue the Special Restricted Area Permit for Lower Dolpo. Sightseeing options include Kathmandu Durbar Square, Swoyambhunath, and Boudhanath Stupa.

itinerary.title: Kathmandu - Nepalgunj (173 m) (Flight)
itinerary.description: Afternoon 1-hour flight from Kathmandu to Nepalgunj in southwestern Terai near the Indian border. Check into your hotel and rest. Overnight in Nepalgunj.

itinerary.title: Nepalgunj - Juphal (2,475 m) (Flight) & Trek to Dunai (2,140 m)
itinerary.description: Early morning 45-minute flight from Nepalgunj to Juphal airstrip in Dolpa. Meet your trekking team, pack mules/yaks, and trek 3 to 4 hours downhill alongside Thuli Bheri River to Dunai (2,140 m), the administrative headquarters of Dolpa.

itinerary.title: Dunai - Beluwa (2,545 m)
itinerary.description: Trek for 6 to 7 hours (15 km) following Thuli Bheri River upstream. Pass through pine forests and small settlements to reach Beluwa (2,545 m), a quiet village surrounded by terraced fields.

itinerary.title: Beluwa - Laina Odar (3,370 m)
itinerary.description: Ascend along Suli Gad River through narrow gorges, waterfalls, and pine/juniper forests (7 to 8 hours, 15 km). Reach Laina Odar (3,370 m), a cliffside camp used by mule caravans.

itinerary.title: Laina Odar - Langa Camp (3,870 m)
itinerary.description: Follow Tarap Khola through deep canyons and rocky paths cut into cliff faces (7 to 8 hours, 14 km). Cross wooden bridges to reach Langa Camp (3,870 m) in a quiet riverside valley.

itinerary.title: Langa Camp - Dho-Tarap (3,944 m)
itinerary.description: Ascend through Tarap Khola gorge as the valley widens into broad alpine meadows. Arrive at Dho-Tarap (3,944 m), one of the world's highest permanent villages rich in Tibetan Buddhist and Bon heritage (7 to 8 hours).

itinerary.title: Rest & Acclimatization Day in Dho-Tarap (3,944 m)
itinerary.description: Essential acclimatization rest day in Dho-Tarap. Explore ancient monasteries such as Ribo Bhumpa Gompa and Drakmar Dewa, meet local Dolpo-pa villagers, and soak in the trans-Himalayan scenery.

itinerary.title: Dho-Tarap - Numa La Base Camp (4,440 m)
itinerary.description: Trek for 6 to 7 hours (11 km) ascending gradually along Tarap Khola past yak pastures and chortens to reach Numa La Base Camp (4,440 m), a high windswept valley below the pass.

itinerary.title: Numa La Base Camp - Numa La Pass (5,238 m) - Danigar (4,512 m)
itinerary.description: Challenging pass crossing day! Steep early morning climb to Numa La Pass (5,238 m) for panoramic vistas of Mt. Dhaulagiri and Kanjiroba range. Descend to Danigar campsite (4,512 m) after 8 to 9 hours (13 km).

itinerary.title: Danigar - Bagala Pass (5,169 m) - Ringmo / Phoksundo Lake (3,641 m)
itinerary.description: Climb steeply over scree and rocky ridges to cross Bagala Pass (5,169 m) with views of Mt. Kanjiroba. Descend steeply through alpine meadows into pine forests to Ringmo village on the shore of turquoise Phoksundo Lake (9 to 10 hours, 19 km).

itinerary.title: Exploration Day at Ringmo & Shey Phoksundo Lake (3,641 m)
itinerary.description: Rest and explore the magical turquoise Phoksundo Lake (3,641 m), Nepal's deepest lake. Visit ancient Bonpo Gompa in Ringmo, walk along cliffside trails, and admire the majestic waterfall outlet.

itinerary.title: Ringmo - Chekpa (2,678 m)
itinerary.description: Descend steadily from Phoksundo Lake along Phoksundo Khola through pine and cedar forests to Chekpa (2,678 m) after 6 to 7 hours (15 km).

itinerary.title: Chekpa - Juphal (2,475 m)
itinerary.description: Trek for 5 to 6 hours (13 km) down river valleys and terraced farmlands back to Juphal (2,475 m). Celebrate the completion of the trek with your guiding team.

itinerary.title: Juphal - Nepalgunj - Kathmandu (1,350 m) (Flights)
itinerary.description: Morning flight from Juphal to Nepalgunj (30 mins) and connecting flight to Kathmandu (1 hour). Transfer to your hotel and enjoy a warm shower and evening rest.

itinerary.title: Free Day in Kathmandu
itinerary.description: A buffer day in Kathmandu in case of weather delays in Juphal. Spend the day resting, shopping in Thamel, or enjoying a traditional Nepali Farewell Dinner hosted by Zenex Travels & Tours.

itinerary.title: Final Departure from Kathmandu
itinerary.description: Breakfast at the hotel. Our Zenex Travels & Tours representative will transfer you to Tribhuvan International Airport 3 hours prior to your flight departure.

Essential Information for Lower Dolpo Trek from Jhuphal

Permits Required

Trekking in Lower Dolpo requires two mandatory permits:

  • Lower Dolpo Restricted Area Permit (RAP): USD $500 per person for the first 10 days, plus USD $50 per person per day thereafter.
  • Shey Phoksundo National Park Entry Permit: NPR 3,000 per person.

Individual/solo trekking is prohibited in Dolpo. A minimum of two trekkers accompanied by a licensed guide from a registered agency like Zenex Travels & Tours is required.

Best Time to Trek

The optimal trekking seasons are:

  • Spring (March to May): Clear skies, mild temperatures, blooming alpine flowers, and active local cultural festivals.
  • Autumn (September to November): Peak season with post-monsoon crystal clarity, dry trails, and spectacular mountain views.
  • Summer (June to August): Dolpo lies in a Himalayan rain shadow, making monsoon trekking possible with lush greenery and quiet trails.

Accommodations & Meals

The trek combines basic teahouse lodges in villages like Juphal, Dunai, and Ringmo with full wilderness tented camping across high-pass sections (Dho-Tarap, Numa La, Danigar). Our expedition cook provides fresh, hot, nutritious meals during camping days.

faqs.question: Where is Lower Dolpo located?
faqs.answer: Lower Dolpo is located in the rain-shadow region of the Dolpa district in mid-western Nepal, surrounded by Dhaulagiri and Kanjiroba mountain ranges inside Shey Phoksundo National Park.

faqs.question: How difficult is the Lower Dolpo Trek from Juphal?
faqs.answer: The trek is graded Hard. It involves crossing two 5,000+ meter passes (Numa La 5,238 m and Bagala Pass 5,169 m), with daily walks of 6 to 10 hours across remote trans-Himalayan wilderness.

faqs.question: What is the maximum altitude on this trek?
faqs.answer: The highest elevation reached is Numa La Pass at 5,238 meters (17,185 feet).

faqs.question: What permits are required for Lower Dolpo?
faqs.answer: You need the Lower Dolpo Special Restricted Area Permit (RAP) and the Shey Phoksundo National Park Entry Permit, arranged via Zenex Travels & Tours.

faqs.question: What is the best time to trek Lower Dolpo?
faqs.answer: Spring (March to May) and Autumn (September to November) offer clear skies and dry trails. Summer/Monsoon (June to August) is also possible due to Dolpo's rain-shadow location.

faqs.question: What makes Shey Phoksundo Lake special?
faqs.answer: At 3,641 m, Phoksundo Lake is Nepal's deepest lake, famous for its mesmerizing turquoise-blue color, steep cliffs, and sacred Bonpo monasteries in Ringmo.

faqs.question: What accommodation is available during the trek?
faqs.answer: Accommodation is a mix of basic teahouses/lodges in lower settlements and full tented camping with a dedicated cook staff in high-pass sections.

faqs.question: Can I trek Lower Dolpo solo?
faqs.answer: No, Nepal immigration regulations require a minimum of 2 trekkers accompanied by a licensed guide.

faqs.question: Is travel insurance mandatory?
faqs.answer: Yes, travel insurance covering medical expenses and emergency high-altitude rescue up to 6,000 meters is mandatory.

faqs.question: How do I book this trek?
faqs.answer: Contact Zenex Travels & Tours to process restricted permits, arrange domestic flights, and organize full camping expedition logistics.

treks.overview:
Upper Dolpo Trek 25 Days | Sacred Shey Gompa, Phoksundo Lake & High Pass Trans-Himalayan Expedition

The Upper Dolpo Trek (25 Days) is one of the ultimate wilderness expeditions in Nepal, taking experienced adventurers across Nepal's last unexplored frontier. Located in the rain-shadow of the Dhaulagiri and Kanjiroba ranges, Upper Dolpo offers high-altitude desert plateaus, turquoise glacial lakes, ancient salt-trade routes, and centuries-old Bon and Tibetan Buddhist monasteries.

This 25-day grand circuit crosses multiple high mountain passes above 5,000 meters—including Jungben La (5,550 m), Nagdalo Pass (5,350 m), Niwas La (5,120 m), Sele La (5,094 m), and Mo La Pass (5,027 m). The journey highlights the sacred 800-year-old Shey Gompa (4,343 m) at the foot of Crystal Mountain, magical Phoksundo Lake (3,641 m), and remote trans-Himalayan stone villages like Saldang, Tinjegaon, and Chharka Bhot before exiting via Kagbeni to Jomsom and Pokhara.

At Zenex Travels & Tours, we provide full expedition support—including Upper Dolpo Restricted Area Permits (RAP), Shey Phoksundo National Park Entry Permits, domestic flights (Kathmandu – Nepalgunj – Juphal & Jomsom – Pokhara), full camping setup with experienced cooks and kitchen staff, yaks/mules, licensed mountain guides, and hotel stays in Kathmandu, Nepalgunj, and Pokhara.
highlights: Cross four major high Himalayan passes over 5,000 meters: Jungben La (5,550 m), Nagdalo Pass (5,350 m), Niwas La (5,120 m), and Sele La (5,094 m).
Visit the sacred 800-year-old Shey Gompa (4,343 m) and pilgrimage around the mystical Crystal Mountain.
Experience the turquoise-blue Phoksundo Lake (3,641 m)—Nepal's deepest lake surrounded by towering sheer cliffs.
Explore isolated Tibetan-Bon settlements of Saldang, Tinjegaon, Chharka Bhot, and Simengaon along historic salt trade routes.
Immerse in ancient pre-Buddhist Bon culture, animism, and Tibetan Buddhist traditions preserved for centuries.
Traverse Shey Phoksundo National Park, sanctuary for snow leopards, Himalayan blue sheep, and rare alpine flora.
Exit the expedition through Kagbeni—the medieval gateway village to Upper Mustang in the Kali Gandaki Valley.
Full expedition management by Zenex Travels & Tours including permits, flights, camping crew, guide, and porters.

itinerary.title: Arrival in Kathmandu (1,350 m)
itinerary.description: Welcome to Nepal! Upon arrival at Tribhuvan International Airport (TIA) in Kathmandu, our Zenex Travels & Tours correspondent meets you and transfers you to your hotel. Pre-trip briefing held in the evening.

itinerary.title: Kathmandu: Permit Preparation & Sightseeing
itinerary.description: Free day in Kathmandu while our team submits passport details to Nepal Immigration to issue the Upper Dolpo Special Restricted Area Permit. Option to explore UNESCO World Heritage Sites such as Pashupatinath, Boudhanath, and Kathmandu Durbar Square.

itinerary.title: Kathmandu - Nepalgunj (173 m) (Flight)
itinerary.description: Afternoon 1-hour flight from Kathmandu to Nepalgunj in Terai region near the Indian border. Check into hotel and rest overnight.

itinerary.title: Nepalgunj - Juphal (2,475 m) (Flight) & Trek to Dunai (2,140 m)
itinerary.description: Early morning 45-minute flight to Juphal airstrip in Dolpa. Meet your porters and yak team, then trek 3 to 4 hours downhill along Thuli Bheri River to Dunai (2,140 m).

itinerary.title: Dunai - Chhekpa (2,678 m)
itinerary.description: Trek for 6 to 7 hours (17-18 km) following Phoksundo Khola River upstream through forested hills and terraced fields to Chhekpa (2,678 m).

itinerary.title: Chhekpa - Ringmo / Phoksundo Lake (3,641 m)
itinerary.description: Trek for 7 hours ascending through pine and rhododendron forests, crossing wooden bridges. Reach Ringmo village on the shore of turquoise Phoksundo Lake (3,641 m).

itinerary.title: Exploration Day around Phoksundo Lake & Bon Monastery (3,600 m)
itinerary.description: Rest and explore Phoksundo Lake, Nepal's deepest lake. Visit ancient Bonpo Monastery in Ringmo, learn local Bon Buddhist customs, and admire lake reflections.

itinerary.title: Ringmo - Phoksundo Khola Camp / Sallaghari (3,750 m)
itinerary.description: Trek along the famous cliffside trail above Phoksundo Lake, entering the remote inner Dolpo region. Camp at Sallaghari (3,750 m) after 7 hours of walking.

itinerary.title: Sallaghari - Nagdalo Phedi / High Camp (4,500 m)
itinerary.description: Ascend through wide alpine grasslands past grazing yak herds to Nagdalo Phedi / High Camp (4,500 m) in 7 hours.

itinerary.title: Nagdalo Phedi - Nagdalo Pass (5,350 m) - Shey Gompa (4,343 m)
itinerary.description: Cross Nagdalo Pass (5,350 m) with views of Mt. Kanjiroba and Tangtung Lake. Descend to the sacred Shey Gompa (4,343 m) at the base of Crystal Mountain (7 hours).

itinerary.title: Rest & Spiritual Exploration Day at Shey Gompa (4,343 m)
itinerary.description: Rest day at Shey Gompa. Visit the 800-year-old monastery, Shey Gompa Cave, interact with local monks, and explore the sacred pilgrimage trails of Crystal Mountain.

itinerary.title: Shey Gompa - Sele La Pass (5,094 m) - Namagung (4,360 m)
itinerary.description: Climb through barren rocky landscapes over Sele La Pass (5,094 m) for panoramic mountain vistas, then descend to the quiet village of Namagung (4,360 m) after 7 hours.

itinerary.title: Namagung - Saldang (3,770 m)
itinerary.description: Trek for 7 hours into arid trans-Himalayan desert terrain to Saldang (3,770 m), one of the largest ancient stone-built villages in Upper Dolpo.

itinerary.title: Saldang - Shimengaon (3,885 m)
itinerary.description: Follow gentle trails through the highlands of Dolpo past river streams and prayer flag chortens to Shimengaon (3,885 m) after 7 hours.

itinerary.title: Simengaon - Tinjegaon (4,110 m)
itinerary.description: Trek 7 hours through diverse meadows and desert canyons, crossing small streams to reach Tinjegaon (4,110 m).

itinerary.title: Tinjegaon - Keheing Khola / Kharka (4,500 m)
itinerary.description: Trek for 7 hours across open high-altitude plains and yak pastures to Keheing Khola campsite (4,500 m).

itinerary.title: Yak Kharka - Mo La Pass (5,027 m) - Chharka Bhot (4,302 m)
itinerary.description: Climb over Mo La Pass (5,027 m) with views of Dhaulagiri range before descending to the ancient walled salt-trade village of Chharka Bhot (4,302 m) (7 hours).

itinerary.title: Chharka Bhot - Nulungsumde Kharka (4,987 m)
itinerary.description: Trek 7 hours through remote barren valleys with views of Nilgiri and Dhaulagiri peaks to Nulungsumde Kharka (4,987 m).

itinerary.title: Nulungsumde - Niwas La (5,120 m) - Jungben La (5,550 m) - Ghaldan Ghuldun Khola (4,247 m)
itinerary.description: High pass expedition day! Cross Niwas La (5,120 m) and Jungben La (5,550 m)—the highest elevation of the trek. Descend to Ghaldan Ghuldun Khola Camp (4,247 m).

itinerary.title: Ghaldan Ghuldun Khola Camp - Santa (3,777 m)
itinerary.description: Trek 6 to 7 hours descending into warmer valleys towards the traditional village of Santa (3,777 m).

itinerary.title: Santa - Bhima Lojun La (4,460 m) - Yak Kharka (3,478 m)
itinerary.description: Cross Bhima Lojun La (4,460 m) and descend towards Yak Kharka (3,478 m) above Kali Gandaki Valley.

itinerary.title: Yak Kharka - Sangdak - Kagbeni - Marpha - Pokhara (820 m)
itinerary.description: Descend to Kagbeni, gateway to Upper Mustang. Board private vehicle for a drive down Kali Gandaki Valley past Marpha to Pokhara (820 m). Overnight at hotel.

itinerary.title: Pokhara - Kathmandu (1,350 m) (Fly / Drive)
itinerary.description: Return from Pokhara to Kathmandu by tourist bus or short domestic flight. Check into hotel and rest in Kathmandu.

itinerary.title: Free Buffer Day in Kathmandu
itinerary.description: A reserve day in Kathmandu for shopping in Thamel or city sightseeing. Traditional Nepali Farewell Dinner hosted by Zenex Travels & Tours in the evening.

itinerary.title: Final Departure from Kathmandu
itinerary.description: Breakfast at hotel. Our Zenex Travels & Tours representative will transfer you to Tribhuvan International Airport 3 hours prior to your international flight departure.

Essential Information for Upper Dolpo Trek - 25 Days

Permits Required

Trekking Upper Dolpo requires two mandatory permits:

  • Shey Phoksundo National Park Entry Permit: NPR 3,000 per person.

All permits are arranged in advance by Zenex Travels & Tours.

Best Time to Trek

The optimal trekking seasons are:

  • Spring (March to May): Pleasant weather, dry trails, blooming wildflowers, and vibrant local cultural festivals.
  • Autumn (September to November): Post-monsoon crystal clarity, dry passes, and breathtaking mountain panoramas.
  • Summer (June to August): Upper Dolpo lies in a Himalayan rain shadow, making monsoon trekking dry and ideal with vibrant green alpine meadows.

faqs.question: Where is Upper Dolpo located?
faqs.answer: Upper Dolpo is located in the far western trans-Himalayan region of Nepal, bordering Tibet inside Shey Phoksundo National Park.

faqs.question: How do I reach Upper Dolpo?
faqs.answer: Fly from Kathmandu to Nepalgunj, then take a mountain flight to Juphal airstrip in Dolpa. The trek ends in Kagbeni/Jomsom with flights to Pokhara and Kathmandu.

faqs.question: When is the best time for Upper Dolpo trek in Nepal?
faqs.answer: Spring (March to May), Autumn (September to November), and Summer (June to August) are ideal because Upper Dolpo lies in a Himalayan rain shadow.

faqs.question: What permits are required for the Upper Dolpo trek?
faqs.answer: You need the Upper Dolpo Special Restricted Area Permit ($500 USD for 10 days + $50/day after) and Shey Phoksundo National Park Permit, arranged via Zenex Travels & Tours.

faqs.question: How difficult is the Upper Dolpo trek?
faqs.answer: The trek is graded Challenging. It crosses multiple passes above 5,000 meters including Jungben La (5,550 m), Nagdalo (5,350 m), and Sele La (5,094 m), requiring 6 to 9 hours of daily walking.

faqs.question: What kind of accommodation is available on Upper Dolpo trek?
faqs.answer: Accommodation is a mix of basic teahouses in gateway villages and full wilderness tented camping with a dedicated cook crew throughout Upper Dolpo.

faqs.question: What food can I expect during Upper Dolpo trek?
faqs.answer: During camping days, our cook staff prepares hot soups, rice, pasta, curries, tsampa, and traditional Dal Bhat.

faqs.question: Is it possible to do the Upper Dolpo trek independently?
faqs.answer: No, Nepal government restricted area regulations prohibit solo trekking. A minimum of 2 trekkers accompanied by a licensed guide is required.

faqs.question: What are the major highlights of the Upper Dolpo trek?
faqs.answer: Highlights include the 800-year-old Shey Gompa, Crystal Mountain, turquoise Phoksundo Lake, Saldang, Tinjegaon, Chharka Bhot, and Kagbeni.

faqs.question: How is mobile and internet connectivity during Upper Dolpo trek?
faqs.answer: Connectivity is non-existent past Ringmo/Dunai. Satellite phone support is carried for safety.

faqs.question: Is altitude sickness a concern on Upper Dolpo trekking?
faqs.answer: Yes, passes exceed 5,500m. Acclimatization rest days at Dho-Tarap, Phoksundo, and Shey Gompa are built into the 25-day itinerary.

faqs.question: How do I book this trek?
faqs.answer: Contact Zenex Travels & Tours to arrange restricted area permits, charter/domestic flights, guides, porters, and full camping logistics.

treks.title: Lower Dolpo Trek - 17 Days
treks.description:
Lower Dolpo Trek of 17 days is a breathtaking journey through one of Nepal’s most remote and culturally rich Himalayan Dolpo regions. This off-the-beaten-path trek offers stunning mountain views, amazing views of Phoksundo lake, traditional Tibetan-influenced villages, and pristine natural landscapes, including high mountain passes like Muria La (3,840 m) and Kagmara La (5,115 m) passes. Ideal for adventurous trekkers seeking solitude and authentic cultural experiences, the Lower Dolpo Trek combines challenging terrain with rewarding encounters, making it a unique and unforgettable Nepal trekking adventure.

Organized by Zenex Travels & Tours, this 17-day trek takes you through Shey Phoksundo National Park and the restricted Lower Dolpo region. Starting with domestic flights to Nepalgunj and Jumla, the trail leads through pristine alpine meadows, sacred Bonpo monasteries, deep pine forests, and high mountain ridges.
highlights: Remote and Untouched Region: Experience one of Nepal’s most isolated and least visited trekking areas, preserving authentic Tibetan culture and traditions.
Stunning Mountain Scenery: Spectacular views of high peaks like Dhaulagiri, Annapurna ranges, and snow-capped Himalayan giants.
High Mountain Passes: Cross challenging passes such as Muria La (3,840 m) and Kagmara La (5,115 m) offering panoramic vistas.
Traditional Tibetan Villages: Visit ancient settlements like Ringmo and Lasa, known for their unique architecture, monasteries, and warm local hospitality.
Phoksundo Lake Exploration: Behold Nepal's deepest turquoise blue lake (3,600 m), sacred to Bonpo and Tibetan Buddhist communities.
Rich Cultural Heritage: Immerse yourself in ancient Bon Buddhist culture, sacred monasteries, prayer flags, and traditional festivals.
Diverse Wildlife: Chance to spot rare Himalayan fauna including blue sheep, snow leopard, and rare Himalayan birds inside Shey Phoksundo National Park.

itinerary.title: Arrival in Kathmandu
itinerary.description: Upon arrival at Tribhuvan International Airport (TIA) in Kathmandu, you will be greeted by our Zenex Travels & Tours representative who will assist with your transfer to the hotel. Once checked in, we arrange a pre-trip briefing to go over the trek, gear check, meet your guide, and answer any questions. Spend the rest of the day at leisure. Overnight at hotel.

itinerary.title: Kathmandu – Nepalgunj
itinerary.description: Breakfast at hotel. Afternoon transfer to Kathmandu TIA airport for a 1-hour flight to Nepalgunj in southwestern Nepal. On clear days, enjoy views of the Langtang, Dhaulagiri, Annapurna, and Manaslu ranges. Nepalgunj lies in the Terai region near the Indian border with a warm climate. Overnight at hotel in Nepalgunj.

itinerary.title: Nepalgunj – Jumla (2,370 m) – Gothichaur
itinerary.description: Early morning 30-minute flight in a light aircraft to Jumla (2,370 m) in Karnali province. Jumla is renowned for organic apples, high-altitude red rice (Jumli Marsi), and Yarsagumba. Meet porters and mule team at Jumla airport and trek along country roads through Depalgaun, apple orchards, and the Tila River bank to Gothichaur (2,995 m). Overnight at tented camp.

itinerary.title: Gothichaur – Kunri Santha (Kurigaun)
itinerary.description: Trek through mountain roads, pine forests, grasslands, and apple farms. Spot grazing sheep and cattle against mountain backdrops. Reach Kunri Santha (Kurigaun), a picturesque village where Chhetri, Thakali, and Tibetan communities coexist peacefully. Explore the village in the afternoon. Overnight at tented camp.

itinerary.title: Kunri Santha – Chorta (3,010 m) – Naphukana
itinerary.description: Trek along Mani Sangu village and follow the bank of Chorta Khola through lush forests to Chorta (3,010 m). Continue through dense pine and rhododendron woods past shepherd huts, ancient chortens, and fluttering prayer flags to Naphukana (2,990 m). Overnight at tented camp.

itinerary.title: Naphukana – Muria La Pass (3,840 m) – Chaurikot
itinerary.description: A challenging and rewarding pass crossing. Ascend steeply from Naphukana through alpine meadows to Muria La Pass (3,840 m). Enjoy 360-degree panoramas of snow-capped Himalayan ranges. Descend through forested slopes to Chaurikot (3,060 m), a traditional settlement surrounded by grazing pastures. Overnight at tented camp.

itinerary.title: Chaurikot – Kaigaon (2,610 m) – Hurikot
itinerary.description: Descend towards Kaigaon and follow river valleys through traditional settlements. Ascend steadily along scenic ridges with views of surrounding alpine hills to Hurikot (3,760 m), a high Tibetan village. Overnight at tented camp.

itinerary.title: Hurikot – Toijum
itinerary.description: Trek along lush forest trails and mountain streams towards Toijum (3,160 m), an entry checkpoint for the Shey Phoksundo National Park and Lower Dolpo Restricted Area. Overnight at tented camp.

itinerary.title: Toijum – Kagmara Phedhi
itinerary.description: Ascend gradually along the Kagmara Khola valley through alpine terrain, dwarf juniper bushes, and rocky trails to Kagmara Phedhi (4,000 m), the high base camp before crossing Kagmara La Pass. Overnight at tented camp.

itinerary.title: Kagmara Phedhi – Kagmara La Pass (5,115 m) – Lasa
itinerary.description: The highest and most dramatic day of the trek! Climb early morning over moraine and snow slopes to Kagmara La Pass (5,115 m). Marvel at sweeping vistas of Kagmara peak, Dhaulagiri range, and deep Dolpo wilderness. Descend steeply to Lasa (4,060 m). Overnight at tented camp.

itinerary.title: Lasa – Pungmo (3,500 m) – Ringmo
itinerary.description: Descend along Pungmo Khola through birch and pine forests passing ancient chortens to Pungmo village. Continue ascending towards Ringmo (3,641 m), a famous Tibetan Bonpo settlement situated right beside Phoksundo Lake. Overnight at lodge/camp.

itinerary.title: Ringmo: Exploration around Phoksundo Lake
itinerary.description: Rest and exploration day at Ringmo and sacred Phoksundo Lake (3,600 m), Nepal's deepest turquoise blue lake. Hike along lake cliffs, visit ancient Bonpo Monasteries (Pal Sentan Thasho Chholing), interact with local Tibetan villagers, and absorb the peaceful spiritual atmosphere. Overnight at lodge/camp.

itinerary.title: Ringmo – Chekpa
itinerary.description: Descend steadily from Phoksundo Lake through forested valleys, river streams, and terraced fields. Pass through traditional hamlets to Chekpa (2,678 m), enjoying warmer air and temperate lush surroundings. Overnight at lodge/camp.

itinerary.title: Chekpa – Dunai (2,140 m) – Juphal
itinerary.description: Trek along gentle downhill trails following the Bheri River valley past Dunai (2,140 m), district headquarters of Dolpa. Continue ascending to Juphal (2,475 m), gateway village with airstrip for flights to Nepalgunj. Overnight at lodge/camp.

itinerary.title: Juphal – Nepalgunj – Kathmandu
itinerary.description: Morning flight from Juphal to Nepalgunj (30 min) followed by connecting flight from Nepalgunj to Kathmandu (1 hr). Transfer to hotel in Kathmandu. Celebrate successful completion of Lower Dolpo Trek with Zenex team. Overnight at hotel.

itinerary.title: Kathmandu Free Day / City Sightseeing
itinerary.description: A free buffer day in Kathmandu for rest, souvenir shopping in Thamel, or optional UNESCO World Heritage sightseeing (Pashupatinath, Boudhanath, Swayambhunath, Kathmandu Durbar Square). Overnight at hotel.

itinerary.title: Final Departure from Kathmandu
itinerary.description: Enjoy your final breakfast at hotel. According to your flight schedule, Zenex Travels & Tours representative will pick you up and transfer you to Kathmandu Tribhuvan International Airport for your homebound flight.

treks.essentialInfo:
### Restricted Area Permits & Regulations
Lower Dolpo is a restricted region near Tibet. All trekkers require a Special Lower Dolpo Restricted Area Permit (USD 500 for 10 days + USD 50/day extra) and a Shey Phoksundo National Park Entry Permit (NPR 3,000). Zenex Travels & Tours manages all permit applications and official documentation. Solo trekking is strictly prohibited; minimum 2 trekkers accompanied by a licensed guide is mandatory.

### Best Season to Trek
- **Spring (March to May):** Stable weather, clear mountain views, blooming alpine wildflowers, and vibrant local Bon Buddhist festivals.
- **Autumn (September to November):** Crystal clear skies post-monsoon, panoramic mountain vistas, dry trails, and ideal temperatures.
- **Summer/Monsoon (June to August):** Lower Dolpo lies in a rain-shadow area behind Dhaulagiri, making trekking possible with greener landscapes and fewer crowds.

### Meals & Accommodation
Accommodation is a mix of basic village tea houses (Dunai, Juphal, Ringmo) and wilderness camping (tented camps with private cook crew) across remote passes like Kagmara La. Meals are prepared fresh by our camp cook, providing warm nutritious Dal Bhat, soups, pasta, porridge, tsampa, and local Tibetan specialties.

faqs.question: How challenging is the 17 Days Lower Dolpo Trek?
faqs.answer: The trek is graded Hard / Challenging. It crosses Muria La Pass (3,840 m) and Kagmara La Pass (5,115 m) with 6 to 9 hours of daily walking.

faqs.question: What is the highlight of the Lower Dolpo Trek?
faqs.answer: Key highlights include Phoksundo Lake (Nepal's deepest turquoise lake), Bonpo Ringmo monastery, Kagmara La Pass (5,115 m), and remote Tibetan villages.

faqs.question: What kind of accommodation is provided during the trek?
faqs.answer: A mix of basic village lodges (in Ringmo, Dunai, Juphal) and organized wilderness tented camping with a dedicated Zenex cook staff across high passes.

faqs.question: Can beginners undertake the Lower Dolpo Trek?
faqs.answer: Prior high-altitude trekking experience and good physical stamina are strongly recommended due to high passes and remote camping conditions.

regions.name: Manaslu Circuit Adventures
regions.description:
The Manaslu Trekking Region is one of Nepal’s premier off-the-beaten-path Himalayan destinations, encircling Mount Manaslu (8,163 m / 26,781 ft) — the eighth highest mountain in the world. Named after the Sanskrit word 'Manasa', meaning "Mountain of the Spirit", Manaslu offers a perfect blend of high-altitude adventure, dramatic glacial landscapes, and deeply preserved Tibetan-Buddhist cultural heritage.

Designated as a restricted trekking area in 1991 to protect its pristine wilderness and fragile ecosystems, the Manaslu Circuit requires special restricted permits and mandatory licensed guide support. This controlled tourism keeps the trails uncrowded and quiet compared to neighboring classic routes, allowing trekkers to experience the authentic raw beauty of the remote Himalayas.

The ultimate highlight of trekking in the Manaslu region is crossing the formidable Larke La Pass (5,106 m / 16,752 ft). This dramatic mountain pass connects the Gorkha and Manang districts, rewarding adventurers with 360-degree panoramas of Mount Manaslu, Himlung Himal (7,126 m), Cheo Himal, Kang Guru, and Annapurna II. The route descends into high-alpine glacial basins, passing icefalls, turquoise lakes, and ancient lateral moraines.

tourTrips.shortDescription: Embark on the legendary 15-day trek to Everest Base Camp (5,364 m) and Kala Patthar summit (5,545 m). Experience thrilling Lukla flights, Sherpa culture in Namche Bazaar, and up-close panoramas of Mount Everest.
tourTrips.overview:
The Everest Base Camp Trek - 15 Days is the ultimate bucket-list Himalayan adventure. Starting with a spectacular mountain flight to Lukla, the route follows the Dudh Kosi river through pine forests and Sherpa villages up to Namche Bazaar (3,440 m), the bustling capital of Khumbu.

Trek past famous Buddhist monasteries like Tengboche, under the majestic shadows of Ama Dablam, Lhotse, and Nuptse, until you reach Everest Base Camp (5,364 m) at the foot of the Khumbu Icefall. The journey culminates with an early morning sunrise climb to Kala Patthar (5,545 m) for the grandest 360° view of Mount Everest (8,848.86 m).

Explore Namche Bazaar (3,440 m) — the historic Sherpa capital with colorful cafes and bakeries
Visit ancient Tengboche Monastery — the spiritual heart of Khumbu region with views of Ama Dablam
Cross iconic high suspension bridges adorned with Buddhist prayer flags over Dudh Kosi River
Immerse in Sherpa Buddhist heritage, spinning prayer wheels, and ancient mani stone walls
Hike through Sagarmatha National Park (UNESCO World Heritage site) spotting Himalayan Tahr and Danphe pheasants
Rest and acclimatize safely with dedicated days in Namche Bazaar and Dingboche
Taste authentic Sherpa and Nepali teahouse cuisine with warm mountain hospitality

faqs.question: How hard is the Everest Base Camp Trek?
faqs.answer: It is rated Hard (3.5 out of 5). You trek 5 to 7 hours daily on steep mountain paths. No technical climbing experience is needed, but strong cardiovascular fitness is essential.

faqs.question: What is the highest point of the trek?
faqs.answer: The highest point reached is Kala Patthar summit at 5,545 meters (18,192 ft), which offers the famous panoramic sunrise view of Mount Everest.

faqs.question: How cold does it get on the EBC trek?
faqs.answer: At higher altitudes (Gorak Shep & EBC), night temperatures can drop to -10°C to -15°C (5°F to 14°F) in Spring/Autumn. A good -15°C down jacket and sleeping bag are mandatory.

faqs.question: How do we handle altitude sickness (AMS)?
faqs.answer: Our 15-day itinerary includes 2 mandatory acclimatization rest days in Namche Bazaar (3,440 m) and Dingboche (4,410 m). Guides carry pulse oximeters to check oxygen levels daily.

faqs.question: What are the accommodations like?
faqs.answer: Accommodation is in traditional Sherpa teahouses with basic twin beds, warm blankets, and central heated dining halls.

tourTrips.overview:
Manaslu Circuit Trek - 16 Days is a remote and adventurous journey around Mount Manaslu (8,163 m / 26,781 ft), the world’s 8th highest peak. Opened to foreign trekkers in 1992, this 16-day circuit offers breathtaking mountain vistas, deeply preserved Tibetan Buddhist culture, and peaceful teahouse trails far from crowded routes.

Trekking in the Manaslu region requires a Special Restricted Area Permit issued by Nepal Immigration and mandatory accompaniment by a Nepal Government licensed guide. During the trek, you will cross the formidable Larkya La Pass (5,106 m), visit ancient monasteries like Pungyen Gompa, and take side trips to Manaslu Base Camp (4,895 m) and serene Birendra Lake.

Experience authentic Tibetan village life in Samagaun, Samdo, and Namrung with stone houses and mani walls
Visit ancient monasteries including Pungyen Gompa in Samagaun and the monastery in Lho
Scenic hike to Birendra Lake — a serene, turquoise glacial lake at the foot of Manaslu
Relax at Tatopani’s natural hot springs after crossing the Machha Khola suspension bridge
Trek through rhododendron and pine forests, bamboo groves, and alpine yak pastures along Budi Gandaki gorge
Taste authentic home-cooked dal bhat at traditional teahouses with warm Gurung and Tibetan hospitality
Ever-changing landscapes from sub-tropical river gorges up to stark high-altitude glacial zones

essentialInfo.title: Permits Required for Manaslu Circuit Trek
essentialInfo.content:
Three official permits are mandatory for the Manaslu Circuit Trek:

  • Manaslu Restricted Area Permit (RAP): Issued by Nepal Immigration for restricted zone between Jagat and Bhimtang. September–November: USD 100/week + USD 15/day extra. December–August: USD 75/week + USD 10/day extra. Must be booked via a registered Nepali agency with min. 2 trekkers & licensed guide.
  • Manaslu Conservation Area Permit (MCAP): NPR 3,000 per person.
  • Annapurna Conservation Area Permit (ACAP): NPR 3,000 per person (required after crossing Larkya La Pass into Dharapani).

essentialInfo.title: Best Seasons to Trek
essentialInfo.content:
Spring (March to May): Mild temperatures, clear morning views, and rhododendrons blooming along the lower gorge.

Autumn (September to November): The peak season with stable weather, crisp skies, and crystal-clear views of Mount Manaslu and surrounding peaks.

essentialInfo.title: Meals & Accommodation
essentialInfo.content: Accommodations consist of mountain teahouses and lodges. Rooms are basic twin-share with comfortable mattresses and blankets. Meals include local Nepali Thali (Dal Bhat), soups, fried rice, chowmein, pasta, Tibetan bread, and hot beverages.

faqs.question: Where is the Manaslu Circuit Trek located?
faqs.answer: The trek is located in western Nepal in the Gorkha and Manang districts, encircling Mount Manaslu (8,163 m) just east of the Annapurna range.

faqs.question: What is the highest point of the trek?
faqs.answer: The highest point is Larkya La Pass at 5,106 meters (16,751 feet), offering breathtaking 360-degree views of Manaslu, Himlung Himal, and Annapurna II.

faqs.question: How difficult is the Manaslu Circuit Trek?
faqs.answer: It is graded Hard (3 out of 5 difficulty). Trekkers walk 6 to 8 hours daily over rugged terrain. Good physical fitness and proper acclimatization are essential.

faqs.question: Can a solo trekker do this trek?
faqs.answer: No. Because Manaslu is a restricted area, Nepal Immigration requires at least 2 trekkers in a group accompanied by a licensed Nepali guide.

faqs.question: What permits are required?
faqs.answer: You need the Manaslu Restricted Area Permit (RAP), Manaslu Conservation Area Permit (MCAP), and Annapurna Conservation Area Permit (ACAP).

faqs.question: What is the accommodation like?
faqs.answer: Accommodation is in local family-run teahouses with basic twin-bed rooms, shared bathrooms, and central heated dining halls.

faqs.question: Is altitude sickness a risk?
faqs.answer: Yes, as you cross above 5,000 meters. The 16-day itinerary includes a dedicated acclimatization day in Samagaun (3,520 m) with side hikes to Base Camp or Birendra Lake.

faqs.question: Is there Wi-Fi and mobile network?
faqs.answer: Mobile network (Ncell/NTC) works up to Namrung. Above Samagaun, signal is sparse, but teahouses offer paid Wi-Fi (Everest Link / Ncell cards).

faqs.question: Are there ATMs on the trek?
faqs.answer: No ATMs exist on the trail beyond Arughat/Besisahar. You must carry sufficient Nepali cash (NPR) from Kathmandu for personal expenses.

faqs.question: Can I combine Manaslu with Tsum Valley?
faqs.answer: Yes! Tsum Valley can be added to the Manaslu Circuit for a 18-21 day extended spiritual journey into the sacred hidden valley.

itinerary.title: Arrival in Kathmandu
itinerary.description: Upon arrival at Tribhuvan International Airport (TIA) in Kathmandu, our representative will transfer you to your hotel. We will host a pre-trip briefing to review equipment, introduce your licensed trekking guide, and answer any questions. Enjoy the rest of the day relaxing in Thamel.
highlights: Airport pickup and hotel check-in
Trek orientation and guide introduction
Explore Thamel tourist hub

itinerary.title: Permit Preparation & Free Day in Kathmandu (1,350 m)
itinerary.description: While our team submits your original passport to Nepal Immigration to issue the official Manaslu Restricted Area Permit, you can explore UNESCO World Heritage sites in Kathmandu including Durbar Square, Swoyambhunath (Monkey Temple), Boudhanath Stupa, and Pashupatinath Temple.
highlights: Official Manaslu Restricted Permit processing
Sightseeing at UNESCO World Heritage sites
Final gear check in Thamel

itinerary.title: Kathmandu – Arughat Bazaar (608 m) – Machha Khola (870 m)
itinerary.modeOfTravel: Private Jeep / Vehicle (8-9 hours drive, 146 km)
itinerary.description: We depart Kathmandu early at 7:00 AM in a private 4WD jeep, driving through winding mountain roads, terraced farmland, and along the Trishuli and Budi Gandaki rivers via Arughat Bazaar and Soti Khola to reach Machha Khola. Machha Khola is a pleasant Gurung village where we stay overnight.
highlights: Scenic drive through Himalayan foothills
Cross Budi Gandaki river valley at Arughat Bazaar
Overnight at Machha Khola Gurung village

itinerary.title: Machha Khola to Jagat (1,340 m)
itinerary.description: We start our trek by crossing the suspension bridge over Machha Khola and following a winding trail to Tatopani, a natural hot spring where we can take a refreshing break. Passing Doban, we cross another suspension bridge over the roaring Budi Gandaki river at Lauri and climb through Sal forests to reach the stone-paved village of Jagat, the entry checkpoint for the restricted zone.
highlights: Cross Machha Khola suspension bridge
Relax at Tatopani natural hot springs
Enter Jagat restricted area checkpoint

itinerary.title: Jagat to Deng (1,860 m)
itinerary.description: Descending from Jagat to the riverbed, we cross a suspension bridge to Nagjet and climb uphill to Philim, a large Gurung village surrounded by terraced fields of wheat and barley. Continuing through bamboo forests, we cross the Budi Gandaki river again at Dyang and press onward to Deng, enjoying first views of Siringi Himal.
highlights: Walk through Philim village and terraced barley fields
Explore bamboo forests along Budi Gandaki gorge
Stunning views of Siringi Himal

itinerary.title: Deng to Namrung (2,630 m)
itinerary.description: Today's trek ascends steeply into Tibetan-influenced cultural territory. Crossing multiple suspension bridges, we walk through dense pine and rhododendron forests past the cliffside settlements of Rana and Bihi Phedi. As we climb higher, snow-capped peaks come into view before arriving at Namrung, famous for stone houses, Buddhist monasteries, and friendly locals.
highlights: Enter Tibetan Nubri cultural valley
Pass ancient mani walls and prayer wheels
Overnight at Namrung with views of Himalchuli

itinerary.title: Namrung to Samagaun (3,520 m)
itinerary.description: A breathtaking day of trekking uphill through pine forests to Lho village, home to a grand Buddhist monastery and a stunning panoramic view of Mount Manaslu (8,163 m). After exploring Lho and Shyala village, surrounded by glaciers and peaks, we walk across a broad alpine valley to Samagaun, the central hub of the Nubri people.
highlights: Unforgettable view of Mount Manaslu from Lho village
Visit Lho Gompa monastery and chortens
Arrive in historic Samagaun stone village

itinerary.title: Acclimatization Day in Samagaun (3,520 m)
itinerary.description: A crucial acclimatization day in Samagaun. Option 1: A rewarding side hike to Manaslu Base Camp (4,895 m, 6-7 hrs round trip) offering up-close views of Manaslu Glacier and icefalls. Option 2: An easy 1-hour walk to turquoise Birendra Glacial Lake. Option 3: A hike to Pungyen Gompa monastery resting on a high meadow plateau.
highlights: Hike to Manaslu Base Camp (4,895 m)
Visit turquoise Birendra Glacial Lake
Spiritual side trip to Pungyen Gompa

itinerary.title: Samagaun to Samdo (3,875 m)
itinerary.description: We follow a gentle uphill trail past long stone mani walls and birch forests as the valley widens near the Tibetan border. We cross a wooden bridge over Budi Gandaki river and ascend slowly to Samdo, a traditional Tibetan refugee village where yak herding and border trade thrive.
highlights: Gentle scenic alpine trek along widening valley
Views of Samdo Peak and Tibetan border ridge
Explore Samdo Tibetan refugee community

itinerary.title: Samdo to Dharmasala / Larkya Phedi (4,460 m)
itinerary.description: We descend from Samdo to cross the river, then climb steadily past the ruins of the ancient Larkya Bazaar market. Traversing alpine yak pastures and moraine ridges with views of Manaslu Glacier and Larkya Peak, we reach Dharmasala (Larkya Phedi), the high base camp lodge before the pass. We rest early for tomorrow's big climb.
highlights: Cross high alpine moraine ridges
Views of Larkya Glacier and Larkya Peak
Early rest at Dharmasala base camp (4,460 m)

itinerary.title: Dharmasala – Larkya La Pass (5,106 m) – Bhimtang (3,590 m)
itinerary.description: The peak highlight of the trek! We start early at 4:30 AM, ascending a steep glacial moraine trail to cross Larkya La Pass (5,106 m / 16,751 ft). Decorated with colorful prayer flags, the pass delivers 360° panoramas of Mount Manaslu, Himlung Himal (7,126 m), Cheo Himal, Kang Guru, and Annapurna II. We descend long rocky slopes to the peaceful green valley of Bhimtang.
highlights: Summit Larkya La Pass (5,106 m / 16,751 ft)
360-degree panoramas of Manaslu, Himlung Himal & Annapurna II
Descend through moraines to Bhimtang valley

itinerary.title: Bhimtang to Tilche (2,300 m)
itinerary.description: From Bhimtang, we descend through lush pine, fir, and rhododendron forests alongside the Dudh Khola river. Passing Yak Kharka, Karche, and Gho village, we observe traditional stone houses, farming terraces, and friendly local Gurung communities before reaching Tilche.
highlights: Descend through ancient rhododendron and fir forests
Follow the rushing waters of Dudh Khola river
Overnight at Tilche Gurung village

itinerary.title: Tilche to Dharapani (1,860 m) – Drive to Besisahar (760 m)
itinerary.modeOfTravel: Trek (2 hours) + Private Jeep Drive (3 hours)
itinerary.description: A short 2-hour morning walk brings us from Tilche to Dharapani, where our trail merges with the classic Annapurna Circuit route. Here we board a private 4WD jeep and drive along the Marshyangdi River gorge to Besisahar, celebrating the end of our trekking journey.
highlights: Reach Dharapani joining Annapurna Circuit route
Scenic jeep ride along Marshyangdi River gorge
Celebratory dinner in Besisahar

itinerary.title: Besisahar to Kathmandu (1,350 m)
itinerary.description: After breakfast in Besisahar, we drive back to Kathmandu in a comfortable private vehicle, following the Trishuli River. Upon arrival in Kathmandu, check in at your hotel and spend the evening shopping for souvenirs or relaxing.
highlights: Drive back to Kathmandu along Trishuli River
Hotel check-in and evening relaxation
Souvenir shopping in Thamel

itinerary.title: Free Day in Kathmandu
itinerary.description: A leisure day in Kathmandu for shopping, spa/massage, or relaxing. In the evening, we host a celebratory farewell dinner at an authentic Nepali restaurant featuring traditional cultural dance performances to celebrate your Manaslu Circuit achievement.
highlights: Leisure day for relaxation or shopping in Kathmandu
Authentic Nepali farewell dinner with cultural show
Receive official Manaslu Trek completion certificate

itinerary.title: Final Departure from Kathmandu
itinerary.description: After breakfast, our team will transfer you to Tribhuvan International Airport (TIA) 3 hours before your international flight home, taking back unforgettable Himalayan memories of Mount Manaslu.
highlights: Hotel checkout and airport transfer
Final departure from Nepal

tourTrips.title: Everest Base Camp Trek with Gokyo - Chola Pass - 17 Days
tourTrips.destination: Gokyo & Everest Base Camp, Nepal
tourTrips.shortDescription: Comprehensive high-altitude circuit combining turquoise Gokyo Lakes, Gokyo Ri (5,360 m), challenging Cho La Pass (5,330 m), Everest Base Camp (5,360 m), and Kala Patthar (5,545 m).
tourTrips.description:
Everest Base Camp trek with Gokyo - Chola Pass is one of the most adventurous and popular journeys in the Himalayas of Nepal, loved by trekkers since the 1950s. EBC from Gokyo with Chola Pass is a must-do trek in Nepal where you explore the majestic Himalayas of the Khumbu Region along with high passes: Chola Pass (5,330 m), Gokyo Ri (5,360 m), and Kala Patthar (5,545 m). During this trek, travelers not only get to explore giant mountains but also experience authentic Sherpa culture.

Gokyo Chola Pass with EBC trekking is an extended version of the classic Everest Base Camp Trek, taking you to explore the highest altitude turquoise lakes at Gokyo (4,790 m) and cross the thrilling Chola Pass (5,330 m). Trekking through this route in Everest is truly a once-in-a-lifetime journey into the heart of the Himalayas.

Get Up Close to Mount Everest Like Never Before with Gokyo Lakes & Chola Pass

During this Everest – Gokyo Trekking, you get the chance to explore beautiful Sherpa villages and magnificent scenic views of the high Everest Himalayan range. This trek takes you to Gokyo (4,790 m), Gokyo Ri (5,360 m) with challenging Chola Pass (5,330 m), and then leads directly to Everest Base Camp (5,360 m).

This trek can be done clockwise (from Namche Bazaar to Gokyo side, crossing Chola Pass, and finally Everest Base Camp) or anti-clockwise. Our itinerary follows the clockwise route, which provides superior gradual acclimatization for high altitudes.

The trek begins with a scenic flight to Lukla's Tenzing-Hillary Airport, heading to Namche Bazaar, passing Dole and Machhermo before arriving at the stunning Gokyo Lakes. A hike up Gokyo Ri offers breathtaking views of Everest, Cho Oyu, Makalu, and Lhotse. After crossing the steep Chola Pass, trekkers hike up Kala Patthar and visit Everest Base Camp before descending past Tengboche Monastery.

Lukla Flight Information

Flight from Ramechhap (March, April, May, October & November): During peak seasons, due to heavy air traffic at Kathmandu airport, flights to Lukla operate from Ramechhap Airport. We take an early morning 4-hour drive from Kathmandu to Ramechhap, followed by a 20-minute flight to Lukla.

Flight from Kathmandu (December – February & June – September): During off-peak months, flights operate directly from Kathmandu to Lukla (35 minutes).

Everything You Need to Know About Chola Pass (5,330 m)

Chola Pass is the high-altitude bridge between Gokyo Valley and Everest Base Camp. Widely known as a summit pass, ascending Chola Pass feels like climbing a high rock mountain. With cold temperatures and rocky paths, it is a thrilling challenge. From the top of Chola Pass, enjoy panoramic views of Mount Ama Dablam, Cholatse, Mount Pumori, and Lobuche before descending into the Khumbu valley toward Everest Base Camp.

Who Can Do This Trek?

This trek is suitable for beginners with good fitness and determination, experienced trekkers looking for a Himalayan high-pass challenge, as well as solo travelers, couples, and group adventurers. No prior mountaineering experience is required—just good physical stamina and the right guidance!

Alternative Everest Treks

If you are looking for alternative options in the Everest region, we also offer:

  • Everest Base Camp Trek & Return by Heli – 12 Days
  • Everest Renjo La Pass to Gokyo Trek – 13 Days
  • Everest Base Camp Trek – 15 Days
  • Everest Three Passes Trek – 19 Days
  • Everest Trek from Jiri – Gokyo – 22 Days
highlights: Visit Sagarmatha National Park (UNESCO World Heritage Site)
Experience a thrilling flight to Tenzing Hillary Airport in Lukla with aerial mountain views
Explore Namche Bazaar, gateway and cultural heart of the Everest Region
Explore Everest View Hotel with 360-degree panoramic views of Mount Everest & Ama Dablam
Experience authentic Sherpa culture and traditional mountain villages
Visit the high-altitude turquoise Gokyo Lakes and climb Gokyo Ri (5,360 m)
Cross the challenging high-mountain Chola Pass (5,330 m)
Trek to Everest Base Camp (5,360 m) and view the Khumbu Icefall
Hike to Kala Patthar (5,545 m) for unforgettable sunrise views of Mount Everest
Option to hike Nangkartshang Peak (5,083 m) from Dingboche
Visit the famous Tengboche Monastery, the spiritual center of Khumbu Buddhism

itinerary.title: Arrival in Kathmandu (1350 m)
itinerary.details:
Upon arrival at Tribhuvan International Airport (TIA) in Kathmandu, you will be warmly greeted by our correspondent holding a greeting sign with your name. After assisting with your luggage, you will be transferred via private vehicle to your hotel situated in the vibrant tourist district of Thamel or city center.

Once checked in, we will arrange a pre-trip meeting where we will brief in short about the trek, review your equipment, answer any queries you have, and introduce your trekking guide. Afterwards, you can relax and spend the rest of the day exploring at your leisure. Stay overnight at the hotel in Kathmandu.

itinerary.title: Kathmandu – Lukla (2840 m) – Phakding (2610 m)
itinerary.details:
Early in the morning, our guide will pick you up from the hotel and transfer you to the domestic terminal of TIA. Take a scenic and thrilling 35-minute mountain flight to Tenzing-Hillary Airport in Lukla (2,840 m), enjoying spectacular aerial views of the snow-capped Himalayan ranges.

After landing in Lukla, rest for a while, assemble your gear with our local Sherpa team, and begin the trek. The trail descends through terraced landscapes, traditional Sherpa hamlets, carved mani stones, and prayer wheels along the Dudh Koshi River bank. Cross sturdy suspension bridges over the river and reach Phakding in 3 hours. Stay overnight at Lodge in Phakding.

itinerary.title: Phakding - Namche Bazar (3440 m)
itinerary.details:
Following breakfast, prepare for a 5 to 6-hour trek to Namche Bazaar. The trail follows the Dudh Koshi River, crossing high suspension bridges decorated with colorful prayer flags. Walk through pine and rhododendron forests, passing small Sherpa hamlets like Benkar and Tok Tok with views of Thamserku (6,608 m). Arrive at Monjo (2,835 m) to register permits at Sagarmatha National Park entrance.

Enjoy lunch in Jorsalle before tackling the famous double-decked Hillary Suspension Bridge over the river confluence. Begin a steep, zig-zag climb through pine forests, catching your first view of Mount Everest through the trees. Emerge into the vibrant crescent-shaped mountain amphitheater of Namche Bazaar (3,440 m). Explore local bakeries, shops, and cafes in the evening. Stay overnight at Lodge in Namche.

itinerary.title: Acclimatization & Hike to Everest View Hotel (3880 m)
itinerary.details:
Today is an essential acclimatization day in Namche Bazaar to help your body adapt to the elevation. Staying active helps speed up acclimatization. In the morning, embark on a scenic 4-hour hike up to Syangboche, Khumjung village, and the famous Everest View Hotel (3,880 m)—one of the highest luxury hotels in the world.

From the hotel terrace, enjoy breathtaking 360-degree panoramic views of Mount Everest, Ama Dablam, Lhotse, Nuptse, and Thamserku. Visit Khumjung Monastery to view the historical yeti scalp and stop by the Hillary School. Return to Namche in the afternoon to explore local markets, craft shops, and bakeries. Stay overnight at Lodge in Namche.

itinerary.title: Namche Bazar – Phortse Tenga (3680 m) – Dole (4200 m)
itinerary.details:
After breakfast, begin your trek toward Dole via Phortse Tenga (6–7 hours total). The trail ascends along high mountain contours to Mongla Pass (3,972 m), a picturesque high ridge adorned with chortens. Stop here to rest, take photos, and enjoy magnificent views of Ama Dablam, Phortse, and Kantega.

Descend steeply for an hour to Phortse Tenga by the riverbank for lunch. Afterward, undertake a 2 to 3-hour steep climb through rhododendron, birch, and bamboo forests. Pass wooden bridges, waterfalls, and yak pastures along the trial until reaching the high alpine settlement of Dole (4,200 m). Stay overnight at Lodge in Dole.

itinerary.title: Dole – Machermo (4470 m)
itinerary.details:
Depart Dole after breakfast for a 4 to 5-hour trek to Machermo. The trail ascends steeply above the tree line to 4,000 meters, offering retro views of Dole village and the deep valley below. Walk through high summer pastures of Labharma and Luza, with constant stunning views of Ama Dablam, Thamserku, and Cho Oyu.

Follow the contouring high ridge above the river canyon to reach Machermo (4,470 m) by lunchtime. After lunch and rest, you can take an optional afternoon hike to nearby ridges for acclimatization and glacier valley photography. Stay overnight at Lodge in Machermo.

itinerary.title: Machermo – Gokyo (4790 m)
itinerary.details:
Trek from Machermo to Gokyo Valley (4–5 hours). The trail climbs gently past high alpine terrain before ascending steep rocky steps beside the roaring meltwater of the terminal moraine of Ngozumpa Glacier.

Pass the First Gokyo Lake (Longponga) and Second Gokyo Lake (Taujung), marveling at their intense turquoise blue waters against the snow-capped mountain backdrop. Arrive at the Third Gokyo Lake (Dudh Pokhari) and check into your lodge in Gokyo village (4,790 m). Spend the afternoon exploring the glacier edge and lake shore. Stay overnight at Lodge in Gokyo.

itinerary.title: Gokyo – Gokyo Ri (5360 m) - Thagnag (4700 m)
itinerary.details:
Wake early at 4:30 AM for the 3-hour steep summit hike up Gokyo Ri (5,360 m). Reaching the summit flags rewards you with one of the most stunning Himalayan panoramas on Earth, featuring four 8,000-meter giants: Mt. Everest, Lhotse, Makalu, and Cho Oyu, as well as the turquoise Gokyo Lakes and Ngozumpa Glacier below.

Descend back to Gokyo for breakfast and a short rest. Afterwards, pack up and trek across the Ngozumpa Glacier moraine toward Thagnag (4,700 m). Navigate boulder-strewn glacial paths for 3 hours, preparing for the high pass crossing the next day. Stay overnight at Lodge in Thagnag.

itinerary.title: Thagnag – Chola Pass (5330 m) – Dzonglha (4830 m)
itinerary.details:
Today is one of the most thrilling days of the trek as you cross Chola Pass (5,330 m). Start early at 4:30 AM after breakfast. Climb steeply over rocky scree and ice-draped slopes for 3 hours to reach the summit of Chola Pass.

Standing atop Chola Pass (5,330 m), admire magnificent views of Cho Oyu, Cholatse, Baruntse, and Ama Dablam. After taking photos and enjoying a packed lunch, carefully descend the eastern side of the pass down boulder fields into the peaceful high valley of Dzonglha (4,830 m). Stay overnight at Lodge in Dzonglha.

itinerary.title: Dzonglha – Gorakshep (5140 m)
itinerary.details:
Depart Dzonglha after breakfast, enjoying views of towering peaks including Cholatse (6,440 m), Taboche (6,495 m), and Lobuche (6,119 m). Contour along the high ridge above Cholatse Lake to join the main Everest Base Camp trail at Lobuche.

After a break in Lobuche, trek along the rocky lateral moraine of the Khumbu Glacier. Walk past glacial debris and ice towers for 3 hours to reach Gorak Shep (5,140 m), the final accommodation stop before Base Camp. Check into the lodge, rest, and prepare for Base Camp and Kala Patthar. Stay overnight at Lodge in Gorakshep.

itinerary.title: Gorakshep – Kala Patthar (5545 m) – EBC (5360 m) - Lobuche (4910 m)
itinerary.details:
Wake before dawn (4 AM) for the challenging climb up Kala Patthar (5,545 m). Watch golden sunrise rays illuminate the South Face of Mount Everest (8,848.86 m), Nuptse, and Pumori in a 360-degree panorama. Descend back to Gorak Shep for breakfast.

After breakfast, trek across the Khumbu Glacier moraine to Everest Base Camp (5,360 m). Stand beside the iconic EBC rock marker, take team photos, view the Khumbu Icefall, and return down to Lobuche (4,910 m) for the night. Stay overnight at Lodge in Lobuche.

itinerary.title: Lobuche - Tengboche (3860 m)
itinerary.details:
Following breakfast, begin your descent down the Khumbu valley from Lobuche toward Tengboche (7–8 hours). The route passes Thokla Pass memorial ridge and Pheriche, crossing the Imja Khola River via a wooden bridge.

Climb up through birch and rhododendron forests to reach Tengboche (3,860 m). Visit the iconic Tengboche Monastery in the afternoon, meet the Buddhist monks, observe evening prayers, and admire views of Ama Dablam. Stay overnight at Lodge in Tengboche.

itinerary.title: Tengboche (3860 m) – Namche Bazar (3440 m)
itinerary.details:
Descend from Tengboche through pine forests down to Phunki Tenga by the riverbank. Cross the suspension bridge over the Dudh Koshi River and climb the high contouring trail around the ridge back to Namche Bazaar (3,440 m).

Enjoy a hot shower, fresh espresso, apple pie at local bakeries, and celebrate completing the high passes and Everest Base Camp. Stay overnight at Lodge in Namche Bazar.

itinerary.title: Namche Bazar – Phakding – Lukla (2840 m)
itinerary.details:
On your final day on the trekking trail, descend steeply down from Namche Bazaar, crossing the Hillary Suspension Bridge and walking back along the Dudh Koshi River bank. Pass through Monjo and Phakding (lunch stop).

Make the final gradual uphill climb back to Lukla town (2,860 m). Gather with your guide and Sherpa porter crew in the evening for a celebratory farewell dinner. Stay overnight at Lodge in Lukla.

itinerary.title: Lukla - Kathmandu (1350 m)
itinerary.details:
Take an early morning flight from Lukla Airport back to Kathmandu (or Ramechhap during peak season). Enjoy your final aerial view of the Himalayan mountain range during the flight.

Upon arrival in Kathmandu, our representative will transfer you back to your hotel. Spend the rest of the day resting and recovering. Stay overnight at Hotel in Kathmandu.

itinerary.title: Kathmandu Free Day & Sightseeing
itinerary.details:
Enjoy a free leisure day in Kathmandu for sightseeing, shopping, or relaxation massage. You can do an optional half-day guided sightseeing tour of UNESCO World Heritage sites including:

- Swoyambhunath (Monkey Temple): Panoramic views of Kathmandu valley.
- Boudhanath: One of the largest Buddhist stupas in the world.
- Pashupatinath: Sacred Hindu temple complex on the Bagmati River.

Spend the evening shopping for souvenirs in Thamel. Stay overnight at Hotel in Kathmandu.

itinerary.title: Departure from Kathmandu
itinerary.details: Enjoy your final breakfast at the hotel in Kathmandu. At your scheduled departure time, our representative will pick you up from the hotel and transfer you to Tribhuvan International Airport (TIA) approximately 3 hours before your international flight departure. Board your flight home carrying lifelong memories of your 17-Day Everest Base Camp, Gokyo Lakes & Chola Pass adventure!

essentialInfo.title: Permits Required for Gokyo and Renjo La Pass Trek - 13 Days
essentialInfo.content:
For travelers interested in the Gokyo Lake & Renjo La Pass trek in Everest, you will need two main permits:

• Sagarmatha National Park Permit – NPR 3,000
• Khumbu Pasang Lhamu Rural Municipality Entry Permit – NPR 3,000

These permits are mandatory and will be arranged by Zenex Travels on your behalf before your trek begins. No need to worry about visiting offices or standing in lines!

essentialInfo.title: Best Time for Everest Gokyo & Renjo La Pass Trek
essentialInfo.content:
• Spring (March – May): Weather is stable and temperatures are moderate. Rhododendron forests are in full bloom, adding vibrant colors, and skies offer clear views of Everest and surrounding peaks.
• Autumn (September – November): Monsoon rains clear the air, providing crisp blue skies, comfortable temperatures, and excellent visibility of snow-capped mountains.

essentialInfo.title: Meals & Accommodations During Trek
essentialInfo.content:
Trekkers stay in local tea house lodges with basic twin beds, blankets, and shared bathrooms. Higher villages like Namche and Lukla offer attached bathroom options. Communal dining rooms are heated with central stoves.

• Breakfast: Bread, Muesli, Porridge, Pancakes, Tibetan Bread, Chapati, Eggs, Sandwiches with tea/coffee.
• Lunch: Chowmein, Fried Rice, Pasta, French Fries, Momo, Spring Rolls, Pizza, Soups.
• Dinner: Soups (Mushroom, Garlic, Veg) + Main Course (Macaroni, Pasta, Fried Rice, Spaghetti, Momo, Nepali Dal Bhat).

essentialInfo.title: Difficulty Level of Nepal Gokyo and Renjo La Pass Trek - 13 Days
essentialInfo.content: Graded as MODERATE to HARD. Suitable for fit beginners and experienced trekkers. You will walk 5–6 hours per day at high altitudes reaching Renjo La Pass (5,340 m) and Gokyo Ri (5,360 m). Prior walking, hiking, jogging, or cardio exercise is recommended.

faqs.question: What is Renjo La Pass?
faqs.answer: Renjo La Pass (5,340 m) is one of the high mountain passes in the Everest region connecting the remote Bhote Koshi valley with the Gokyo Lakes valley. It offers breathtaking panoramic views of Mt. Everest, Lhotse, Makalu, and Cho Oyu.

faqs.question: What is the depth of Gokyo Lake?
faqs.answer: Gokyo Lake (Dudh Pokhari) is part of the world's highest freshwater lake system situated at an elevation of 4,700–5,000 meters. The maximum depth of Gokyo Main Lake is approximately 43 meters (141 ft).

faqs.question: How difficult is the Everest Gokyo & Renjo La Pass Trek?
faqs.answer: The trek is graded as Moderate to Hard. Trekkers walk 5–7 hours per day at altitudes exceeding 4,000–5,300 meters. Good physical fitness and mental determination are required, but no technical climbing skills are needed.

faqs.question: When is the best time to do the Everest Gokyo & Renjo La Trek?
faqs.answer: Spring (March to May) and Autumn (September to November) offer optimal weather, clear skies, and comfortable trekking temperatures.

faqs.question: Do I need a guide for this Everest - Renjo La Pass trek?
faqs.answer: Yes, having a licensed English-speaking local guide is strongly recommended for high-altitude safety, navigating high passes, permit arrangements, and local cultural interaction.

faqs.question: Can I combine this trek with Everest Base Camp?
faqs.answer: Yes! You can combine Gokyo and Renjo La Pass with Everest Base Camp via the Cho La Pass on our 17-Day Everest Base Camp Trek with Gokyo - Chola Pass.

faqs.question: What currency shall I carry during Gokyo-Renjo La pass trek?
faqs.answer: You should carry Nepalese Rupees (NPR) in cash for personal expenses, hot showers, Wi-Fi, battery charging, and snacks during the trek, as ATMs are only available up to Namche Bazaar.

faqs.question: What kind of accommodation will I get during the Gokyo-Renjo La Pass Lake Trek?

tourTrips.title: Gokyo and Renjo La Pass Trek - 13 Days
tourTrips.destination: Gokyo & Renjo La Pass, Nepal
tourTrips.shortDescription: Scenic, quieter high-pass trek to turquoise Gokyo Lakes, Gokyo Ri (5,360 m), and across the breathtaking Renjo La Pass (5,340 m).
tourTrips.description:
Gokyo and Renjo La Pass Trek in Nepal of 13 days is a scenic alternative trek to the classic EBC route, offering spectacular views of Everest, Cho Oyu, Makalu, and more. This trek is less crowded compared to the Everest Base Camp route and features the thrilling high-altitude Renjo La Pass (5,340 m), providing breathtaking Himalayan scenery and vistas of the amazing turquoise glacial lakes of Gokyo.

Gokyo and Renjo La Pass trek in Everest is a short, beautiful trek blending natural wonders with the Sherpa culture of the Khumbu region. During this trek, you pass through beautiful villages like Lukla, Phakding, Namche Bazaar, Thame, and Lungden before crossing the high Renjo La Pass. After descending to Gokyo Lake (4,790 m), a hike to Gokyo Ri (5,360 m) offers one of the best Himalayan panoramas.

Explore Gokyo Lakes & Cross Renjo La Pass | Stunning Alternative to EBC Trek

The Gokyo and Renjo La Pass trek is a scenic and less crowded journey in the Khumbu region of Nepal, offering stunning views of Mount Everest and other Himalayan peaks. The main highlight is crossing the high and beautiful Renjo La Pass (5,340 m), which offers one of the best mountain views in Nepal.

The trek starts with a scenic flight to Lukla (2,840 m), followed by a walk to Phakding along the Dudh Koshi River. From there, the trail continues to Namche Bazaar (3,440 m). After acclimatization, the trail heads west to the peaceful, quiet Sherpa village of Thame and on to Lungden (4,380 m).

From Lungden, you cross the challenging Renjo La Pass (5,340 m) and descend to the beautiful Gokyo Lake (4,790 m). A short hike up Gokyo Ri (5,360 m) gives you a stunning sunrise view of Everest, Cho Oyu, Makalu, and other peaks before descending down through Dole and Namche to Lukla.

When is the Best Time for Gokyo & Renjo La Pass Trekking?

The best time to do this trek is in Spring (March–May) and Autumn (September–November). December is also a great option for those who prefer fewer crowds. While demanding due to high altitude, with proper guidance and preparation, it offers a once-in-a-lifetime Himalayan experience.

Who Can Do This Trek?

The Everest Gokyo & Renjo La Pass Trek can be done by anyone with good fitness, a sense of adventure, and a positive mindset. It is ideal for beginners with good fitness & willpower, trekkers with past experience (e.g. Poon Hill, Langtang, Mardi Himal), as well as solo travelers, couples, and groups seeking a quieter, scenic high-pass route.

Alternatives for Gokyo & Renjo La Pass Trek

If you are exploring other options in the Everest region, consider:

  • Everest Base Camp Trek & Return by Heli – 12 Days
  • Everest Base Camp Trek – 15 Days
  • Everest Base Camp Trek with Gokyo – Chola Pass – 17 Days
  • Everest Three Passes Trek – 19 Days
  • Everest View Short Trek – 7 Days

Lukla Flight Information

Flight from Ramechhap (March, April, May, October & November): During peak seasons, flights operate from Ramechhap Airport to avoid air traffic in Kathmandu. Includes a 5-6 hour drive from Kathmandu to Ramechhap followed by a 20-minute flight to Lukla.

Flight from Kathmandu (December – February & June – September): Direct 35-minute flight from Kathmandu's Tribhuvan International Airport to Lukla.

itinerary.title: Arrival in Kathmandu (1350 m)
itinerary.details: Upon arrival at Tribhuvan International Airport (TIA) in Kathmandu, you will be greeted by our correspondent who will assist with your transfer to the hotel. Once checked in, we will arrange a pre-trip meeting where we will brief in short about the trek, answer any queries you have and meet your trekking guide as well. After the short brief, you can relax and spend rest of the day at your leisure. Stay overnight at the hotel.

itinerary.title: Kathmandu – Lukla (2840 m) – Phakding (2610 m)
itinerary.details: This day after an early breakfast at the hotel, we will meet our guide and drive to the domestic terminal of Tribhuvan International Airport for a 35-minute scenic and adventurous flight to Lukla in the Everest region, weather permitting. Upon landing at Tenzing-Hillary Airport in Lukla (2840 m), we will rest briefly, meet our Sherpas at the lodge, and begin our trek. The three-hour walk to Phakding (2610m) will take us through Lukla Bazaar, offering unforgettable views of terraced landscapes, river valleys, Sherpa villages, and up-close perspectives of some of the world's highest mountains. Stay overnight at a lodge.

itinerary.title: Phakding - Namche Bazar (3440 m)
itinerary.details: This day we will have breakfast in early morning and trek towards Namche Bazzar. At the beginning of the trek, we have to walk straight uphill path and we will cross the Dudh Koshi river several times. After walking about 1.5 hours we will reach Monjo village (2835 m). Then we will continue our trek with a steep zig-zag trial crossing the waterfall, crossing biggest and amazing suspension bridge. After almost 5 to 6 hours of walking we will reach Namche Bazar, the capital of Sherpa people. The first view of Namche Bazar with the stupa, monastery, lodges and the beautiful gates is amazing. Stay overnight at lodge.

itinerary.title: Acclimatization at Namche Bazar (3440 m)
itinerary.details:
Today will be the acclimatization day in Namche Bazar. As trekking in higher elevations can lead to altitude sickness, we have to make sure to acclimatize so that our body can adapt with increasing elevation.

In the morning, we will have breakfast in the hotel and get ready to hike for about 4 hours to the monastery above Namche Bazar, then after we will go to Syangboche and Khumjung village and finally to the luxurious hotel at highest altitude: Hotel Everest View. From the hotel, we can see first view of Mount Everest, and other beautiful Himalayas like: Mount Ama Dablam, Mount Lhotse, Mount Nuptse and so on.

Today's hike will serve us for acclimatization and where we will enjoy magnificent views of Everest. As we return back to Namche Bazar, in the afternoon we will have free time to wander around and visit the markets, purchase trekking equipment's (if needed), local handicrafts and so on around Namche Bazar. Stay overnight at Lodge.

itinerary.title: Namche Bazzar - Thame (3800 m)
itinerary.details:
This day you will have breakfast at the lodge and then begin the trek to Thame which takes about 4-5 hours of walking.

Following Bhote Koshi River along the pine and rhododendron forests, we trek towards Thame. On the way you can see large set of prayer flags, Chorten, carved stones, stupa at Phurte and so on.

Thame is located at the end of the Khumbu Valley and the iconic value of Thame is its terrain of peoples who are untouched by the effects of modern civilization. On the way to Thame, you can visit a place named Thamu where there is Ani Monastery, we can visit there on the way and we reach Thame we can visit the older monastery of Everest Region, 'Dechen Chokhorling Monastery Thame'. Stay overnight at Lodge.

itinerary.title: Thame - Lungden (4380m)
itinerary.details:
This day you will have breakfast at the lodge and then trek towards Lungden which takes about 5-6 hours.

Today's walking is mostly uphill trials, enjoying the view of landscape, vegetation and mountains. During the trek you pass through old Sherpa walled villages like Taranga, then Marulung (4200 m) and finally reach Lungden. Today you will also be able to observe Sherpa culture en route. We can also visit Nakpa valley which used to be old trade route to Tibet and also share the road with Tibetan Yak Caravan as it is the road to and from Namche with trade to Tibet with the villagers. Stay overnight at Lodge.

itinerary.title: Lungden – Renjola Pass (5340 m) – Gokyo (4790 m)
itinerary.details:
This day you will have breakfast in the early morning (around 5 am) and get ready to cross Renjo La Pass (5340 m). Today you will have to trek for about 6-7 hours to reach Gokyo.

Today's trekking will be mostly uphill trial until you reach Renjo La Pass. From the top of Renjo La Pass (5340 m), you can see majestic views of towering peaks such as Mount Everest (8848 m), Mount Lhotse (8516 m), Mount Nuptse, Mount Makalu (8463 m), and Mount Cho Oyu (8201 m) and many more.

After enjoying the view from Renjola pass you start to descend towards Gokyo, and reach Gokyo in another 2 hours. Upon arrival in Gokyo valley, you can also admire the Gokyo Lake with the picturesque Gokyo village nestled along its shores from the pass. Stay overnight at Lodge.

itinerary.title: Gokyo – Gokyo Ri (5360 m) - Dole (4200 m)
itinerary.details:
Today is one of the important day of the trekking. You will have to wake up in the early morning (4:30 – 5 am) and then get ready to hike 1.8 km uphill to Gokyo Ri (5360 m) which takes about 3 hours.

Climbing Gokyo Ri is totally ascending uphill trial but the view from the top of Gokyo Ri is totally worth it! We can enjoy the panoramic view of the Himalayas like Mount Everest, Mount Makalu, Mount Lhotse, Ama Dablam, Thamserku and so on. Along with the views of magnificent peaks, you can also see glaciers and very beautiful views of Gokyo Lakes. After enjoying the view from Gokyo Ri, descend back to Gokyo in lodge which takes about 1.5 hours.

After arrival in the lodge in Gokyo, you will have breakfast and rest for a while. Then prepare to trek back towards Dole which takes about 5 hours of walking. Today you will descend back towards Dole and trek alongside Dudh Koshi River to reach Dole. On the way you can see beautiful views of Cho Oyu, Kangtega, Thamserku, Taboche and Cholatse peaks. Stay overnight at Lodge.

itinerary.title: Dole - Namche Bazaar (3440 m)
itinerary.details: This day after having breakfast, trek towards Namche Bazaar which takes about 6 hours. You will walk zig-zag trials till we reach Namche Bazaar crossing Phortse and Phunke Tenga. Stay overnight at Lodge.

itinerary.title: Namche Bazaar – Lukla (2840 m)
itinerary.details:
After having breakfast in the lodge, you will descend back towards Lukla through the same trail via Phakding. As you trek back to Lukla you get to spend the last night in the Khumbu region of Everest. You will descend towards Phakding from Namche in about 3.5 hours and have lunch in Phakding. From here, we will again descend towards Lukla through the zigzag trail in another 4.5 hours.

Upon arrival in Lukla, enjoy your last stay in Khumbu region, have group dinner and enjoy your final stay with warm memories and lifetime adventure in Khumbu region just spent. Stay overnight at Lodge.

itinerary.title: Lukla – Kathmandu (1350 m)
itinerary.details: Today in the early morning (6 am onwards) you will take a flight from Tenzing Hillary Airport (an 'eagle's nest') to fly to Kathmandu or Ramechhap (subject to availability). The time of the flight will depend on the weather conditions. After arrival in Kathmandu, you can rest the whole day. Stay overnight at hotel.

itinerary.title: Free day in Kathmandu
itinerary.details:
This day you have a free day in Kathmandu. Stay overnight at Hotel in Kathmandu.

Taking advantage of the extra day, you can go for:
- UNESCO World Heritage sightseeing (Swayambhunath, Boudhanath, Pashupatinath)
- Panoramic Mount Everest Mountain flight to see beautiful views of Everest range
- Shopping / Massage, rest in hotel, etc.

NOTE: In case travellers do not need an extra day in Kathmandu, it is possible to reduce 1 extra night in Kathmandu.

itinerary.title: Departure from Kathmandu
itinerary.details: Enjoy your last day in Kathmandu before departure. At your scheduled departure time, our correspondent will pick you up from the hotel, transfer you to the airport, and bid you farewell with warm hearts.

essentialInfo.title: Permits Required for Gokyo and Renjo La Pass Trek - 13 Days
essentialInfo.content:
For travelers interested in the Gokyo Lake & Renjo La Pass trek in Everest, you will need two main permits:

• Sagarmatha National Park Permit – NPR 3,000
• Khumbu Pasang Lhamu Rural Municipality Entry Permit – NPR 3,000

These permits are mandatory and will be arranged by Zenex Travels on your behalf before your trek begins. No need to worry about visiting offices or standing in lines!

essentialInfo.title: Best Time for Everest Gokyo & Renjo La Pass Trek
essentialInfo.content:
• Spring (March – May): Weather is stable and temperatures are moderate. Rhododendron forests are in full bloom, adding vibrant colors, and skies offer clear views of Everest and surrounding peaks.
• Autumn (September – November): Monsoon rains clear the air, providing crisp blue skies, comfortable temperatures, and excellent visibility of snow-capped mountains.

essentialInfo.title: Meals & Accommodations During Trek
essentialInfo.content:
Trekkers stay in local tea house lodges with basic twin beds, blankets, and shared bathrooms. Higher villages like Namche and Lukla offer attached bathroom options. Communal dining rooms are heated with central stoves.

• Breakfast: Bread, Muesli, Porridge, Pancakes, Tibetan Bread, Chapati, Eggs, Sandwiches with tea/coffee.
• Lunch: Chowmein, Fried Rice, Pasta, French Fries, Momo, Spring Rolls, Pizza, Soups.
• Dinner: Soups (Mushroom, Garlic, Veg) + Main Course (Macaroni, Pasta, Fried Rice, Spaghetti, Momo, Nepali Dal Bhat).

essentialInfo.title: Difficulty Level of Nepal Gokyo and Renjo La Pass Trek - 13 Days
essentialInfo.content: Graded as MODERATE to HARD. Suitable for fit beginners and experienced trekkers. You will walk 5–6 hours per day at high altitudes reaching Renjo La Pass (5,340 m) and Gokyo Ri (5,360 m). Prior walking, hiking, jogging, or cardio exercise is recommended.
