faqs.question: What is Renjo La Pass?
faqs.answer: Renjo La Pass (5,340 m) is one of the high mountain passes in the Everest region connecting the remote Bhote Koshi valley with the Gokyo Lakes valley. It offers breathtaking panoramic views of Mt. Everest, Lhotse, Makalu, and Cho Oyu.

faqs.question: What is the depth of Gokyo Lake?
faqs.answer: Gokyo Lake (Dudh Pokhari) is part of the world's highest freshwater lake system situated at an elevation of 4,700–5,000 meters. The maximum depth of Gokyo Main Lake is approximately 43 meters (141 ft).

faqs.question: How difficult is the Everest Gokyo & Renjo La Pass Trek?
faqs.answer: The trek is graded as Moderate to Hard. Trekkers walk 5–7 hours per day at altitudes exceeding 4,000–5,300 meters. Good physical fitness and mental determination are required, but no technical climbing skills are needed.

faqs.question: When is the best time to do the Everest Gokyo & Renjo La Trek?
faqs.answer: Spring (March to May) and Autumn (September to November) offer optimal weather, clear skies, and comfortable trekking temperatures.

faqs.question: Do I need a guide for this Everest - Renjo La Pass trek?
faqs.answer: Yes, having a licensed English-speaking local guide is strongly recommended for high-altitude safety, navigating high passes, permit arrangements, and local cultural interaction.

itinerary.title: Namche Bazaar - Tengboche (3860 m)
itinerary.details:

Today trek will be through the most scenic route of Everest from where we can see Dudh Koshi River and on the way, you can see scenic view of Mount Ama Dablam, Mount Lhotse, Mount Nuptse, Mount Everest, Mount Kangtega, Thamserku and many more. As you leave Namche Bazar, walk through the descending trial along the Dudh Koshi valley until you reach Phungi Thanga. You get to see most amazing view of Mount Ama Dablam and monastery near Phungi Thanga, a best place to take the picture of nature, mountain and monastery. After resting for a while in Phungi Thanga, cross the suspension bridge and walk uphill trial for about 3 hours to reach Tengboche.

Tengboche is one of the famous destinations with old monastery for the travelers in khumbu region of Nepal, here you can visit the Tengboche monastery and pray with monks in the evening or morning with Lamas. Stay overnight at Lodge in Tengboche.

itinerary.title: Tengboche - Dingboche (4410 m)
itinerary.details:
This day you have breakfast in morning gear yourself to trek towards Dingboche which takes about 5-6 hours of walking.

Before you head to Dingboche, you can see mesmerizing view of sunrise on Mount Amadablam, Mount Everest, Mount Lhotse and Thamserku from Tengboche. You have to walk through the alpine forest crossing Imja Khola (river) through the suspension bridge on the way to reach Dingboche. You will also pass through different villages like: Debuche, Pangboche before Dingboche Village. On the way you can also see mani walls, prayer flags, yaks grazing, and so on.

Dingboche is a beautiful village with settlement of Sherpa people in Everest region of Nepal. It is also known as "summer valley" due to its warmer sun exposure compared to neighboring villages. Dingboche is a common acclimatization point for trekkers heading toward Everest Base Camp, Island Peak, or Ama Dablam. Stay overnight at Lodge in Dingboche.

itinerary.title: Acclimatization in Dingboche (4410 m)
itinerary.details:
Today is a rest and acclimatization day in Dingboche. Though today is a "rest day," it's important to stay active for acclimatization.

To adapt with the altitude and changing environment and prevent ourselves from altitude sickness, we can hike to Nangkartsang peak (5083 m) which takes about 3.5 hours to reach there and 2 hours to descend back. This hike is a great opportunity to see amazing views of Makalu (8,485 m), Lhotse (8,516 m), Ama Dablam (6,812 m), Island Peak, and Cho Oyu (8,188 m) on a clear day.

After the hike, return to Dingboche for a relaxed afternoon. You can explore the village, interact with the local Sherpa people, or rest at the lodge. The landscape around Dingboche, with its traditional stone walls, potato fields, and wide open valleys, is both peaceful and picturesque. Stay overnight at Lodge.

itinerary.title: Dingboche - Lobuche (4940 m)
itinerary.details:
This day you will have breakfast in morning and then prepare to continue the journey to Lobuche which takes about 5 hours of walking uphill trials.

You have to walk through the straight ascending trial to climb towards Pheriche valley. Passing through the alpine scrub and yak pastures along with the beautiful view of mountains behind. You can see the memorial statues of climbers who passed away during expeditions in Everest and then from there walking further, you reach Thukla Pass. You will rest there for a while and begin to walk towards Lobuche. Here, in Lobuche you will have basic place for lodging. Stay overnight at Lodge in Lobuche.

itinerary.title: Lobuche - EBC (5360 m) - Gorak Shep (5140 m)
itinerary.details:
This day you will have breakfast in early morning and then hike for about 2 hours to reach Gorakshep. From Lobuche we have to walk through rocky ways, uphill trial to reach Gorakshep. Today is one of the important days of the Everest Base Camp trek where you will be able to reach the foot of world tallest mountain - Mount Everest's base camp - EBC.

As we reach Gorakshep, we will keep our luggage in the lodge and then go to the main destination of the trek, Everest Base Camp (5360 m). If weather is clear, you can see amazing views of Mount Everest followed by Mount Nuptse, Mount Lhotse and so on. Also, you can see Khumbu Glaciers from here. After enjoying the scenic view in EBC return back to Gorakshep. Stay overnight at Lodge in Gorakshep.

itinerary.title: Gorak Shep - Kala Patthar (5550 m) – Lukla (2840 m) – Kathmandu (1350 m) by Heli
itinerary.details:
Today is one of the most adventurous and thrilling days of the Everest Base Camp trek, where you will reach the maximum altitude of the trek - Kala Patthar (5,545 m).

You will wake up in the early morning (4-5am) and begin to hike towards Kala Patthar, the viewpoint of the trek. Walking uphill trial for about 2.5 hours you will reach Kala Patthar - meaning "Black Stone" in Nepali. When you are ascending towards Kala Patthar you can see Mount Pumori right straight to your sight. From the top you can see beautiful 360-degree views of the Everest Range: Mount Everest, Mount Nuptse, Mount Lhotse, Mount Pumori, Mount Ama Dablam and many more.

After celebrating and capturing the successful climb to Kala Patthar, descend back to the lodge and have breakfast. After breakfast, prepare to return back to Kathmandu and wait for the Helicopter to arrive at the Heli pad of Kala Patthar / Gorak Shep and fly back to Kathmandu (stopover in Lukla for refueling). Transfer to your hotel upon landing in Kathmandu. Stay overnight at Hotel in Kathmandu.

itinerary.title: Free day in Kathmandu
itinerary.details:
Free day in Kathmandu for sightseeing / shopping / massage. We can do half-day sightseeing in UNESCO-listed World Heritage sites like:

- Kathmandu Durbar Square: Historical, cultural, and religious heritage site with amazing architecture.
- Swoyambhunath (Monkey Temple): Offers panoramic views of Kathmandu valley.
- Boudhanath: One of the largest stupas in the world.
- Pashupatinath: Sacred Hindu temple complex on the banks of the Bagmati River.

Stay overnight at Hotel in Kathmandu.

itinerary.title: Departure from Kathmandu
itinerary.details: Enjoy your last day in Kathmandu before departure. At your scheduled departure time, our correspondent will pick you up from the hotel, transfer you to the airport, and bid you farewell with warm hearts.

essentialInfo.title: Permits Required for Everest Base Camp Trekking with Helicopter Return
essentialInfo.content:
For travelers doing the Everest Base Camp Trek with Helicopter Return, you will need two main permits:

• Sagarmatha National Park Entry Permit: Required to enter the park covering EBC, Kala Patthar, and Khumbu glacier.
• Khumbu Pasang Lhamu Rural Municipality Permit: Local permit required to trek in the Khumbu region.

Note: The TIMS card is no longer required for treks in the Everest region. At Zenex Travels, we arrange all permits in advance!

essentialInfo.title: Best Time for Everest Base Camp Trek with Heli Return
essentialInfo.content:
• Spring (March – May): Stable weather, moderate temperatures, vibrant rhododendron blooms, clear mountain views, and active Everest expeditions.
• Autumn (September – November): Crisp blue skies, dry conditions, clear visibility, and comfortable trekking weather.
• Winter (December – February): Off-season with fewer crowds, serene mountain views, pristine snowy vistas, and direct Lukla flights from Kathmandu.

essentialInfo.title: Weather & Temperature Guide
essentialInfo.content:
• Spring (March - May): Daytime 10°C to 15°C at lower altitudes; nighttime -10°C to -15°C at Gorak Shep / Kala Patthar.
• Autumn (Sept - Nov): Daytime 10°C to 20°C at lower altitudes; nighttime -10°C or lower at high camps.
• Winter (Dec - Feb): Daytime 5°C to 10°C; nighttime -15°C to -20°C above 4,000 meters. Clear skies with minimal crowds.

essentialInfo.title: Meals & Accommodations During EBC Trek
essentialInfo.content:
Trekkers stay in cozy mountain tea house lodges with twin beds, blankets, and shared or attached bathrooms (Namche, Lukla, Dingboche). Dining halls are heated with central stoves.

• Breakfast: Bread, Muesli, Porridge, Pancakes, Tibetan Bread, Chapati, Eggs, Sandwiches with tea/coffee.
• Lunch: Chowmein, Fried Rice, Pasta, French Fries, Momo, Spring Rolls, Pizza, Soups with tea/coffee.
• Dinner: Soups (Mushroom, Garlic, Veg) + Main Course (Macaroni, Pasta, Fried Rice, Spaghetti, Momo, Nepali Dal Bhat) with tea/coffee.

essentialInfo.title: Difficulty Level & High-Altitude Acclimatization
essentialInfo.content:
Graded as MODERATE (Grade 2). Suitable for fit beginners and experienced hikers. Max altitude: 5,545 m (Kala Patthar) & 5,140 m sleeping altitude at Gorak Shep.

• Prevention & Remedies for Altitude Sickness (AMS):
- Ascend gradually & take active rest days in Namche (Day 4) and Dingboche (Day 7).
- Hydrate with 3-4 liters of water, garlic/ginger soup, and herbal tea daily.
- Eat carb-rich meals & dress in warm layers.
- Diamox (Acetazolamide) as recommended by your doctor; emergency helicopter rescue insurance required.

tourTrips.title: Gokyo Lake Trek - 14 Days
tourTrips.destination: Gokyo Lakes, Nepal
tourTrips.shortDescription: Trek to the turquoise Gokyo Glacial Lakes, climb Gokyo Ri (5,360 m), and explore the 5th Lake and Ngozumpa Glacier.
tourTrips.description:
The Gokyo Lake Trek of 14 days is a spectacular journey in the Everest region that leads trekkers to a series of pristine glacial lakes nestled at high altitudes, including the stunning Gokyo Lakes and the viewpoint of Gokyo Ri (5,360 m). This trek offers breathtaking views of the world’s highest peaks like Mount Everest, Mount Lhotse, Mount Makalu, and Cho Oyu—while passing through remote Sherpa villages, alpine valleys, and the massive Ngozumpa Glacier. Gokyo Ri provides one of the best panoramic vistas in the Himalayas, making this a perfect alternative to the classic Everest Base Camp trek.

Ideal for those seeking less crowded trails and natural beauty, the Gokyo Lake Trek typically takes 11 days of actual trekking from/to Lukla and reaches a maximum altitude of over 5,360 meters. The trek is moderately challenging and suitable for trekkers with good fitness and high-altitude enthusiasm.

Gokyo Lake Trek Nepal: Glacial Lakes, Everest Views & Sherpa Culture

The Gokyo Lake Trek of 14 days is a short alternative trek option in the Everest Region where we explore the 5 main lakes of Gokyo lying between 4,700 m to 5,000 m altitude. These lakes form the world’s highest freshwater lake system, designated as a Ramsar site of international importance and sacred to both Hindus and Buddhists. Lonely Planet praises the Gokyo Valley as "the most spectacular in the Khumbu."

The trek climbs to Gokyo Ri (5,360 m), offering a 360-degree panoramic view of Everest alongside the turquoise Gokyo Lakes and Gokyo village below. The trail passes through Namche Bazaar, Dole, Phortse, and Machhermo.

Lukla Flight Information

Flight from Ramechhap (March, April, May, October & November): During peak seasons, flights operate from Ramechhap Airport to avoid air traffic in Kathmandu. Includes a 5-6 hour drive from Kathmandu to Ramechhap followed by a 20-minute flight to Lukla.

Flight from Kathmandu (December – February & June – September): Direct 35-minute flight from Kathmandu's Tribhuvan International Airport to Lukla.

itinerary.title: Arrival in Kathmandu (1350 m)
itinerary.details: Upon arrival at Tribhuvan International Airport (TIA) in Kathmandu, you will be greeted by our correspondent who will assist with your transfer to the hotel. Once checked in, we will arrange a pre-trip meeting where we will brief in short about the trek, answer any queries you have and meet your trekking guide as well. After the short brief, you can relax and spend rest of the day at your leisure. Stay overnight at the hotel.

itinerary.title: Kathmandu – Lukla (2840 m) – Phakding (2610 m)
itinerary.details:
This day we will have breakfast early in the morning then our guide will pick us up and take us to the domestic terminal of TIA for an exciting 35-minute mountain flight to Lukla in eastern Nepal.

Upon landing at Tenzing-Hillary Airport in Lukla, rest for a while, meet our Sherpas, and prepare to begin the trek to Phakding (2610 m). The 2 to 3-hour walk takes us through Lukla Bazaar, offering unforgettable views of terraced landscapes, river valleys, Sherpa villages, and suspension bridges. Stay overnight at Lodge.

itinerary.title: Phakding - Namche Bazar (3440 m)
itinerary.details:
This day you will have breakfast in the morning and prepare to head towards Namche Bazar which takes about 5-6 hours.

Walk along the low-rise trail crossing the Dudh Koshi River several times. Pass Monjo village (2835 m) to enter Sagarmatha National Park. Ascend the steep zig-zag path, cross high suspension bridges, and catch your first glimpse of Mount Everest. Have lunch in Jorsalle before making the final push to Namche Bazaar (3440 m), the bustling capital of the Sherpa people. Free evening to explore bakeries, cafes, and local shops. Stay overnight at Lodge.

itinerary.title: Acclimatization & Hike to Everest View Hotel (3880 m)
itinerary.details:
Today is an essential acclimatization day in Namche Bazaar. In the morning, hike up to Syangboche, Khumjung village, and the famous Everest View Hotel (3,880 m)—the world's highest luxury hotel.

Enjoy 360-degree views of Mount Everest, Ama Dablam, Lhotse, Nuptse, and Thamserku while sipping hot tea on the hotel terrace. Return to Namche Bazaar in the afternoon for free leisure time to explore markets and bakeries. Stay overnight at Lodge.

itinerary.title: Namche Bazaar - Phortse Village (3840 m)
itinerary.details: After breakfast, trek towards Phortse Village (5–6 hours). Ascend uphill for 3 hours to reach Mongla Pass (3,972 m), enjoying breathtaking views of Ama Dablam from the stupa. Descend to Phortse Tenga, cross the river, and hike up to Phortse village (3,840 m), a scenic Sherpa village located at the base of Taboche Peak. Stay overnight at Lodge.

itinerary.title: Phortse Village – Machhermo (4470 m)
itinerary.details: Trek from Phortse Village to Machhermo (4–5 hours). Cross the Dudh Koshi River and ascend through Luza village, walking alongside high alpine trails with retro views of the valley. Arrive in Machhermo (4,470 m) for lunch and spend the afternoon exploring the surrounding ridge. Stay overnight at Lodge.

itinerary.title: Machermo – Gokyo (4790 m)
itinerary.details: Trek from Machermo to Gokyo Valley (4–5 hours). Ascend steep rocky steps beside the roaring meltwater of Ngozumpa Glacier. Pass the 1st Gokyo Lake (Longponga) and marvel at the intense turquoise waters of the 2nd and 3rd lakes (Dudh Pokhari). Check into your lodge in Gokyo village (4,790 m) nestled beside the lake shore. Explore the glacier in the afternoon. Stay overnight at Lodge.

itinerary.title: Gokyo - Climb Gokyo Ri (5360 m) – Hike to Fifth Lake
itinerary.details:
Wake early at 4:30 AM for the 3-hour climb up Gokyo Ri (5,360 m). Experience the breathtaking 360-degree sunrise panorama of Mount Everest, Lhotse, Makalu, Cho Oyu, Ngozumpa Glacier, and the Gokyo Lakes below. Descend back to the lodge for breakfast.

In the afternoon, embark on a scenic hike to the 4th Lake (Thonak Tsho) and 5th Lake (Ngozumpa Tsho) at 5,000 meters elevation for incredible up-close views of Cho Oyu and Mount Everest's North Face. Return to Gokyo for the night. Stay overnight at Lodge.

itinerary.title: Gokyo – Dole (4200 m)
itinerary.details: After breakfast, pack up and begin your descent back towards Dole (5 hours walking). Trek alongside the Dudh Koshi River with retro views of Cho Oyu, Kangtega, Thamserku, Taboche, and Cholatse peaks. Stay overnight at Lodge in Dole.

itinerary.title: Dole - Namche Bazaar (3440 m)
itinerary.details: Trek from Dole to Namche Bazaar (6 hours). Walk the zig-zag trail crossing Phortse Tenga and Phungi Thanga before contouring around the high valley ridge back to Namche Bazaar. Enjoy hot showers and bakeries in the evening. Stay overnight at Lodge.

itinerary.title: Namche Bazaar – Lukla (2840 m)
itinerary.details: Final day on the trekking trail. Descend from Namche Bazaar down to Phakding for lunch, then continue along the river valley to Lukla town (2,840 m). Gather with your guide and Sherpa porters for a celebratory farewell dinner. Stay overnight at Lodge.

itinerary.title: Lukla – Kathmandu (1350 m)
itinerary.details: Early morning flight from Lukla Airport back to Kathmandu (or Ramechhap depending on season). Transfer to your hotel upon landing and spend the rest of the day relaxing. Stay overnight at Hotel in Kathmandu.

itinerary.title: Free day in Kathmandu
itinerary.details: Free day in Kathmandu for leisure, shopping, or UNESCO World Heritage sightseeing including Swayambhunath (Monkey Temple), Boudhanath Stupa, and Bhaktapur Durbar Square. Stay overnight at Hotel in Kathmandu.

itinerary.title: Departure from Kathmandu
itinerary.details: Enjoy breakfast at your hotel before your private airport transfer to Tribhuvan International Airport (TIA) for your flight home.

faqs.answer: Spring (March to May) and Autumn (September to November) offer optimal weather, clear skies, and comfortable trekking temperatures.

faqs.answer: Yes, Wi-Fi access (Everest Link / Airship cards) and mobile cellular data (Ncell/NTC) are available at most lodges up to Gokyo village.

faqs.question: Is it safe to drink water during the Gokyo Lake Trek in Everest?

faqs.question: What currency should I carry during the Everest trek?

faqs.question: What religious customs or rituals might I witness during Everest Trek?
faqs.answer: You will pass Buddhist mani walls, chortens, prayer wheels, and ancient monasteries (such as Tengboche and Khumjung Monasteries) where you can observe monk prayer rituals.

faqs.question: What kind of accommodation will I get during the Gokyo Lake Trek?
faqs.answer: Cozy tea house lodges with twin-sharing rooms, warm dining halls heated by central stoves, and shared or attached bathrooms in lower Sherpa villages.

faqs.question: What kind of food is available during the Gokyo Lake Trek?
faqs.answer: Teahouse lodges serve a wide variety of fresh meals including local Dal Bhat, Chowmein, Fried Rice, Pasta, Momo, Pancakes, Soups, Eggs, and hot beverages.

faqs.question: Will I get vegetarian or vegan meal options during Gokyo Trek?
faqs.answer: Yes! Vegetarian and vegan options (Dal Bhat, vegetable noodles, fried rice, soups, potatoes) are widely available at all tea house lodges throughout the trek.

faqs.question: What is the daily walking distance and hours during Gokyo Lake trek?
faqs.answer: Trekkers walk approximately 5 to 6 hours each day covering 8 to 14 kilometers depending on elevation and terrain.

faqs.question: What are the highlights of the Gokyo Lake Trek?
faqs.answer: Turquoise Gokyo Lakes, 5th Lake (Ngozumpa Tsho), sunrise view from Gokyo Ri (5,360 m), Ngozumpa Glacier, Everest View Hotel, and Sherpa villages like Namche Bazaar and Phortse.

tourTrips.title: Amadablam Base Camp Trek - 11 Days
tourTrips.destination: Ama Dablam Base Camp, Nepal
tourTrips.shortDescription: Spectacular 11-day short trek to the base camp of Mount Ama Dablam (4,700 m) beneath one of the world's most iconic mountain pyramids.
tourTrips.description:
Ama Dablam Base Camp Trek of 11 days in the Khumbu region of Nepal is a spectacular short trek in the Everest region, ideal for trekkers seeking a close encounter with the Himalayas. Ama Dablam means 'Mother's Necklace' in English. Without going all the way to Everest Base Camp, this scenic 11-day journey takes you deep into the heart of Sherpa culture, vibrant villages, ancient monasteries, and breathtaking landscapes to the base of Mount Ama Dablam (6,812 m)—one of the most iconic peaks in the world.

From Ama Dablam Base Camp (4,700 m), trekkers are rewarded with breathtaking panoramic views of Himalayan giants set in a wide, open alpine valley. Mount Ama Dablam was first scaled on March 13, 1961, by a team led by Sir Edmund Hillary.

Himalayan Peaks Seen from Ama Dablam Base Camp

  • Ama Dablam (6,812 m): Towering directly above, incredibly close and dramatic
  • Mount Everest (8,848 m): Visible from high points along the trail near Pangboche
  • Lhotse (8,516 m): Standing just south of Everest
  • Kangtega (6,782 m) & Thamserku (6,608 m): Beautiful double summits sharply rising to the southeast
  • Taboche (6,495 m) & Cholatse (6,440 m): Visible across the valley ridges
  • Island Peak (6,189 m) & Peak 38 (7,590 m): Magnificent high mountain vistas

Lukla Flight Information

Flight from Ramechhap (March, April, May, October & November): During peak seasons, flights operate from Ramechhap Airport to avoid air traffic in Kathmandu. Includes a 5-6 hour drive from Kathmandu to Ramechhap followed by a 20-minute flight to Lukla.

Flight from Kathmandu (December – February & June – September): Direct 35-minute flight from Kathmandu's Tribhuvan International Airport to Lukla.

essentialInfo.title: Permits Required for Amadablam Base Camp Trekking
essentialInfo.content:
For travelers doing the Ama Dablam Base Camp Trek, you will need two main permits:

• Sagarmatha National Park Entry Permit: Required to enter the park covering Tengboche, Pangboche, and Base Camp.
• Khumbu Pasang Lhamu Rural Municipality Permit: Local permit required to trek in the Khumbu region.

Note: The TIMS card is no longer required for treks in the Everest region. At Zenex Travels, we arrange all permits in advance!

essentialInfo.title: Best Time for Everest Amadablam Base Camp Trek
essentialInfo.content:
• Spring (March – May): Stable weather, moderate temperatures, rhododendron blooms, and active expedition preparations.
• Autumn (September – November): Crisp air, clear blue skies, dry trail conditions, and excellent visibility of snow-capped peaks.
• Winter (December – February): One of the best short winter treks in Nepal! Max altitude of 4,700 m makes it ideal for winter trekking with fewer crowds, snow-covered peaks, and clear skies.

essentialInfo.title: Meals & Accommodations During Trek
essentialInfo.content:
Trekkers stay in cozy mountain tea house lodges with twin beds, blankets, and shared or attached bathrooms (Namche, Lukla, Pangboche). Dining halls are heated with central stoves.

• Breakfast: Bread, Muesli, Porridge, Pancakes, Tibetan Bread, Chapati, Eggs, Sandwiches with tea/coffee.
• Lunch: Chowmein, Fried Rice, Pasta, French Fries, Momo, Spring Rolls, Pizza, Soups with tea/coffee.
• Dinner: Soups (Mushroom, Garlic, Veg) + Main Course (Macaroni, Pasta, Fried Rice, Spaghetti, Momo, Nepali Dal Bhat) with tea/coffee.

Note: Please inform us in advance if you are vegetarian, vegan, or have food allergies!

essentialInfo.title: Difficulty Level & Altitude Sickness (AMS) Remedies
essentialInfo.content:
Graded as MODERATE in Nepal. Max altitude: 4,700 m at Ama Dablam Base Camp (option to descend to Pangboche for sleep if preferred). Walks 5–6 hours per day.

• Prevention & Remedies for Altitude Sickness (AMS):
- Ascend gradually with proper acclimatization rest days in Namche (Day 4).
- Hydrate with 3-4 liters of water, garlic/ginger soup, and herbal tea daily.
- Eat carb-rich meals & dress in warm layers.
- Diamox (Acetazolamide) as recommended by your doctor; high-altitude evacuation insurance required.

itinerary.title: Arrival in Kathmandu (1350 m)
itinerary.details: Upon arrival at Tribhuvan International Airport (TIA) in Kathmandu, you will be greeted by our correspondent who will assist with your transfer to the hotel. Once checked in, we will arrange a pre-trip meeting where we will brief in short about the trek, answer any queries you have and meet your trekking guide as well. After the short brief, you can relax and spend rest of the day at your leisure. Stay overnight at the Hotel in Kathmandu.

itinerary.title: Kathmandu – Lukla (2840 m) – Phakding (2610 m)
itinerary.details:
This day after an early breakfast at the hotel, meet your guide and drive to the domestic terminal of Tribhuvan International Airport for a 35-minute scenic and adventurous flight to Lukla in the Everest region, weather permitting.

Upon landing at Tenzing-Hillary Airport in Lukla (2840 m), rest briefly in the lodge of Lukla and meet your Sherpas at the lodge, and prepare to begin the first day trek. Walking 3 hours along terraced landscapes and river valleys, you reach Phakding (2610 m). Pass through Lukla Bazaar with up-close perspectives of snow-capped peaks. Stay overnight at a lodge in Phakding.

itinerary.title: Phakding - Namche Bazar (3440 m)
itinerary.details:
This day you will have breakfast in the early morning and begin the journey towards Namche Bazzar which takes about 5-6 hours of walking.

Walk along the Dudh Koshi River, crossing high suspension bridges decorated with prayer flags. Pass Monjo village (2835 m) to register permits at Sagarmatha National Park entry point. Cross the Hillary Suspension Bridge and ascend the steep zig-zag trail to reach Namche Bazaar (3,440 m), the bustling Sherpa capital. Stay overnight at Lodge in Namche Bazar.

itinerary.title: Acclimatization at Namche Bazar (3440 m)
itinerary.details:
Today will be the acclimatization day in Namche Bazar. In the morning, get ready to hike for about 4 hours to the monastery above Namche Bazar, then visit Syangboche, Khumjung village, and the famous Everest View Hotel (3,880 m).

Enjoy panoramic views of Mount Everest (8,848 m), Ama Dablam, Lhotse, and Nuptse while relaxing with hot tea on the terrace. Return to Namche Bazaar in the afternoon for free time to explore local markets and cafes. Stay overnight at Lodge in Namche Bazar.

itinerary.title: Namche Bazaar – Pangboche (3930 m)
itinerary.details:
After breakfast, trek along the scenic ridge towards Pangboche (6 hours). Enjoy sweeping views of the Dudh Koshi River, Ama Dablam, Everest, Lhotse, and Thamserku. Descend to Phungi Thanga for lunch, then cross the suspension bridge and climb for 3 hours through rhododendron forests to Tengboche Monastery.

Visit Tengboche Monastery to observe monks during prayer rituals. Continue descending 30 minutes to Debuche and another 30 minutes to Pangboche (3,930 m). Stay overnight at lodge in Pangboche.

itinerary.title: Pangboche – Ama Dablam Base Camp (4700 m)
itinerary.details:
Today is the highlight of the journey. After breakfast, begin the 5-hour trek to Ama Dablam Base Camp (4,700 m). Descend towards Imja Khola, cross the suspension bridge, and climb steeply up to Cholungche Kharka viewpoint.

Continue ascending to reach Ama Dablam Base Camp (4,700 m) set directly beneath the towering pyramid of Mount Ama Dablam (6,812 m). Marvel at close-up views of Ama Dablam, Lhotse, Nuptse, Lobuche Peak, Taboche, and the Minbo Glacier. Spend the afternoon exploring the open alpine plateau. Stay overnight at lodge in Base Camp / Pangboche.

itinerary.title: Amadablam Base Camp – Tengboche (3860 m) – Monjo (2835 m)
itinerary.details:
After enjoying a sunrise view over Ama Dablam, begin your descent back towards Monjo (8 hours walking). Pass Debuche, Tengboche Monastery, and descend through rhododendron forests to Phunki Thanga.

Climb up to Sanasa and contour around the high trail past Namche Bazaar and the Sagarmatha National Park checkpoint to reach the peaceful village of Monjo (2,835 m). Stay overnight at lodge in Monjo.

itinerary.title: Monjo – Lukla (2840 m)
itinerary.details:
Final trekking day. Descend from Monjo through Sherpa hamlets along the Dudh Koshi River, reaching Phakding in 2.5 hours for lunch.

After lunch, continue the gradual uphill climb for 3 hours to Lukla town (2,840 m). Celebrate completing the Ama Dablam Base Camp trek with your guide and porter crew in the evening. Stay overnight at Lodge in Lukla.

itinerary.title: Lukla – Kathmandu (1350 m)
itinerary.details: Take an early morning flight from Lukla Airport back to Kathmandu (or Ramechhap depending on season). Transfer to your hotel upon arrival and spend the rest of the day relaxing. Stay overnight at Hotel in Kathmandu.

itinerary.title: Free day in Kathmandu
itinerary.details: Free day in Kathmandu for sightseeing, shopping, or massage. Optional half-day guided tour of UNESCO World Heritage sites including Swayambhunath (Monkey Temple), Boudhanath Stupa, and Pashupatinath Temple. Stay overnight at Hotel in Kathmandu.

itinerary.title: Departure from Kathmandu
itinerary.details: Enjoy breakfast at your hotel before your private airport transfer to Tribhuvan International Airport (TIA) for your flight home.

tourTrips.title: Pikey Peak Trek - 9 Days
tourTrips.destination: Pikey Peak, Nepal
tourTrips.shortDescription: Peaceful 9-day trek in lower Solukhumbu offering Sir Edmund Hillary's favorite 360° summit view of Mt. Everest, Makalu, and Kanchenjunga.
tourTrips.description:
Pikey Peak Trek of 9 days is a short and peaceful journey in the lower Solukhumbu (Everest) region of Nepal, known for offering Sir Edmund Hillary’s favorite view of Mount Everest. From the 4,065 m summit, trekkers can enjoy a breathtaking 360-degree panorama of Himalayan giants including Mount Everest (8,848.86 m), Makalu, Lhotse, Kanchenjunga, and Annapurna, especially stunning at sunrise.

This less-traveled trail passes through traditional Sherpa villages, colorful rhododendron forests, ancient monasteries, and sacred mani walls, offering a rich cultural experience without the commercial crowds of Everest Base Camp. Ideal for beginners and experienced hikers alike, the trek can be completed in 9 days and is best enjoyed in spring, autumn, or even quiet December.

Pikey Peak Trek – Best Short Trek for Everest Views & Sherpa Culture

Named after the local Sherpa deity representing the Sky God worshipped during local festivals, Pikey Peak offers a visual and spiritual experience. The trek starts with a scenic drive along the BP highway to Dhap (2,932 m), followed by gradual ascents through Jhapre and Pikey Peak Base Camp (3,640 m).

The highlight is summiting Pikey Peak (4,065 m) for sunrise before descending through alpine meadows to Junbesi, home to the historic Thupten Chholing Monastery. The trek concludes at Phaplu before returning overland to Kathmandu.

Who Can Do The Pikey Peak Trek?

Anyone with a basic level of fitness and a love for nature and culture! It involves moderate altitudes (max 4,065 m) with 4–6 hours of daily walking, well-established teahouses, and no technical climbing skills required.

itinerary.title: Kathmandu – Dhap (2932 m)
itinerary.details:
Early morning breakfast around 6 am before starting the 8 to 9-hour road drive (234 km) from Kathmandu to Dhap in a private jeep.

The drive follows the BP Highway offering scenic countryside views of hills, terraced fields, and the Sunkoshi River into Okhaldhunga district. Dhap is a peaceful rural village and the starting point of the Pikey Peak trek. Stay overnight at lodge in Dhap.

itinerary.title: Dhap – Jhapre (2820 m)
itinerary.details:
First day of trekking. After breakfast, trek south from Dhap through descending trails for 2 hours to Sigane village. Ascend past Phokte Danda to reach the quiet Sherpa village of Jhapre (2,820 m) for lunch (5 hours walking total).

Jhapre offers a serene atmosphere and beautiful distant views of Mount Everest, Numbur Himal, Makalu, and Baruntse. Explore the local monastery. Stay overnight at lodge in Jhapre.

itinerary.title: Jhapre – Pikey Peak Base Camp (3640 m)
itinerary.details:
Trek from Jhapre to Pikey Peak Base Camp (6 hours, 12 km). The trail climbs through grassy alpine ridges, rhododendron forests, and past long mani walls.

Enjoy sweeping views of Everest and Numbur Himal as you climb closer to Pikey Peak. Reach Pikey Peak Base Camp (3,640 m) by late afternoon. Rest, stay warm, and prepare for tomorrow's early summit hike. Stay overnight at lodge in Pikey Peak Base Camp.
itinerary.overnight: Lodge in Pikey Peak Base Camp

itinerary.title: Pikey Peak BC – Pikey Peak (4065 m) - Junbesi (2700 m)
itinerary.details:
Wake early for a 1-hour pre-dawn summit climb to Pikey Peak (4,065 m). Experience a breathtaking 360-degree sunrise over Mount Everest (8,848.86 m), Makalu, Lhotse, Nuptse, Kanchenjunga, and Annapurna—the view Sir Edmund Hillary called his favorite in Nepal.

Descend back to Base Camp for breakfast. Pack up and trek downhill through pine forests and alpine meadows for 6 hours to Junbesi (2,700 m), an authentic Sherpa village. Visit the historic Thupten Chholing Monastery. Stay overnight at lodge in Junbesi.

itinerary.title: Junbesi – Ringmo (2720 m)
itinerary.details:
Trek from Junbesi to Ringmo (5 hours, 12 km). Walk along gentle uphill trails through rhododendron forests, passing Buddhist chortens and mani walls.

Arrive in Ringmo (2,720 m) for lunch. In the afternoon, take a 1-hour hike up to Taksindo to explore one of the largest Tibetan monasteries in Solu and enjoy panoramic views before returning to Ringmo. Stay overnight at lodge in Ringmo.

itinerary.title: Ringmo – Phaplu (2469 m)
itinerary.details:
Final trekking day. Ascend through rhododendron forests and descend past terraced farmlands and Sherpa hamlets to Phaplu (2,469 m), taking about 4 hours (9 km).

Phaplu is the district headquarters of Solukhumbu featuring an airstrip, cozy lodges, and ethnic Rai, Limbu, Sherpa, and Magar communities. Celebrate completing the trek. Stay overnight at lodge in Phaplu.

itinerary.title: Phaplu – Kathmandu (1350 m)
itinerary.details: After breakfast, take a 9 to 10-hour overland drive (270 km) back to Kathmandu in a private jeep. Enjoy scenic views of hilly terrain, rivers, and countryside villages like Ghurmi and Okhaldhunga. Transfer to your hotel upon arrival in Kathmandu. Stay overnight at Hotel in Kathmandu.

itinerary.title: Departure from Kathmandu
itinerary.details: Enjoy breakfast at your hotel before your private airport transfer to Tribhuvan International Airport (TIA) for your flight home.

tourTrips.title: Everest View Trek - 10 Days
tourTrips.destination: Everest View Hotel & Tengboche, Nepal
tourTrips.shortDescription: Ideal 10-day short family trek to Everest View Hotel (3,880 m) and Tengboche Monastery offering spectacular panoramas of Mt. Everest.
tourTrips.description:
Everest View Trek of 10 days is one of the best short trekking experiences in Nepal, offering spectacular views of the world’s highest mountains within a relatively short time. This trek is perfect for travelers who wish to experience the beauty of the Everest region without committing to a long and demanding expedition. The journey begins with a scenic flight from Kathmandu to Lukla, followed by a gradual trek through picturesque Sherpa villages, lush pine forests, and dramatic Himalayan landscapes.

Because of its unique combination of towering Himalayan peaks, Sherpa culture, and breathtaking trekking trails, the Everest View Trek in the Khumbu region remains one of the most iconic mountain destinations in the world.

Mount Everest & The Khumbu Region

Mount Everest, the tallest mountain on Earth, standing at 8,848.86 meters (29,031.7 ft) above sea level, lies on the border between Nepal and China (Tibet Autonomous Region). Known as “Sagarmatha” in Nepal and “Chomolungma” in Tibet, the Everest region attracts climbers and trekkers from every corner of the globe.

Located in northeastern Nepal within Sagarmatha National Park, the trail follows the classic Everest trekking route along the Dudh Koshi River through Phakding, Namche Bazaar, and up to the world-famous Everest View Hotel (3,880 m) and Tengboche Monastery (3,860 m).

Lukla Flight Information

Flight from Ramechhap (March, April, May, October & November): During peak seasons, flights operate from Ramechhap Airport to avoid air traffic in Kathmandu. Includes a 5-6 hour drive from Kathmandu to Ramechhap followed by a 20-minute flight to Lukla.

Flight from Kathmandu (December – February & June – September): Direct 35-minute flight from Kathmandu's Tribhuvan International Airport to Lukla.

itinerary.details: After breakfast, trek towards Namche Bazaar (5 to 6 hours). Cross the Dudh Koshi River several times over high suspension bridges. Pass Monjo (2,835 m) to enter Sagarmatha National Park. Ascend the steep zig-zag path through pine forests, catching your first view of Mount Everest before reaching the crescent-shaped mountain amphitheater of Namche Bazaar (3,440 m). Stay overnight at Lodge in Namche Bazzar.

itinerary.title: Acclimatization at Namche Bazzar (3440 m)
itinerary.details:
Acclimatization day in Namche Bazaar. In the morning, take a scenic 4 to 5-hour hike up to Syangboche, Khumjung village, and the famous Everest View Hotel (3,880 m).

Enjoy 360-degree views of Mount Everest (8,848.86 m), Ama Dablam, Lhotse, and Nuptse from the hotel terrace. Return to Namche Bazaar in the afternoon to visit local markets and craft shops. Stay overnight at Lodge in Namche Bazzar.

itinerary.title: Namche Bazaar - Tengboche (3860 m)
itinerary.details:
After breakfast, trek along high contouring trails offering magnificent views of Ama Dablam, Everest, and Lhotse. Descend to Phungi Thanga for lunch, then climb for 3 hours through rhododendron forests to reach Tengboche (3,860 m).

Visit the ancient Tengboche Monastery in the afternoon and observe monks during evening prayers amidst panoramic mountain views. Stay overnight at Lodge in Tengboche.

itinerary.title: Tengboche – Monjo (2835 m)
itinerary.details:
After breakfast at Tengboche, descend through rhododendron and pine forests with occasional retro views of Everest, Ama Dablam, and Thamserku. Pass Debuche and continue down to Namche Bazaar for lunch.

From Namche, descend steeply through pine forests, cross suspension bridges along the Dudh Koshi River, and arrive at the peaceful village of Monjo (2,835 m) at the entrance of Sagarmatha National Park. Stay overnight at Lodge in Monjo.

itinerary.title: Monjo - Lukla (2840 m)
itinerary.details:
Final day of trekking. Walk gently through pine forests alongside the Dudh Koshi River past Phakding village.

Make the gradual uphill push to Lukla town (2,840 m). Enjoy a free afternoon celebrating your successful Everest View Trek with your guide and porter crew near Tenzing-Hillary Airport. Stay overnight at Lodge in Lukla.

itinerary.title: Lukla - Kathmandu (1350 m)
itinerary.details: After breakfast, take an early morning scenic flight from Lukla Airport back to Kathmandu (or Ramechhap depending on season). Transfer to your hotel and spend the rest of the day relaxing. Stay overnight at Hotel in Kathmandu.

itinerary.title: Kathmandu Free Day & Sightseeing
itinerary.details: Free day in Kathmandu for leisure, shopping, or UNESCO World Heritage sightseeing including Swayambhunath (Monkey Temple), Boudhanath Stupa, and Pashupatinath Temple. Stay overnight at Hotel in Kathmandu.

itinerary.title: Departure from Kathmandu
itinerary.details: Enjoy breakfast at your hotel before your private airport transfer to Tribhuvan International Airport (TIA) for your onward flight home.

tourTrips.title: Everest Three Pass Trek - 19 Days
tourTrips.destination: Renjo La, Cho La, Kongma La Passes & Everest Base Camp, Nepal
tourTrips.shortDescription: Ultimate 19-day Himalayan adventure crossing 3 high passes (Renjo La, Cho La, Kongma La), Gokyo Lakes, Everest Base Camp & Kala Patthar.
tourTrips.description:
Everest Three Passes Trek of 19 days in Nepal is an adventurous & challenging route in the Everest region, designed for experienced trekkers seeking an immersive Himalayan expedition. This trek crosses three high-altitude passes: Renjo La Pass (5,340 m), Cho La Pass (5,330 m), and Kongma La Pass (5,535 m), offering breathtaking views of Everest, Lhotse, Nuptse, Ama Dablam, Makalu, Cho Oyu, and Pumori.

Along with the three passes, you will visit iconic Everest destinations including Gokyo Lakes, Gokyo Ri (5,360 m), Everest Base Camp (5,360 m), and Kala Patthar (5,545 m), while exploring traditional Sherpa villages and monasteries in Thame and Tengboche.

Everest Three Pass Trek: Ultimate High-Altitude Adventure in Khumbu

The route begins with a scenic flight to Lukla, heading to Namche Bazaar and Thame before crossing the first pass, Renjo La (5,340 m) into the Gokyo Valley. After ascending Gokyo Ri, the trail crosses Cho La Pass (5,330 m) over glaciers to reach Dzonglha, Lobuche, and Everest Base Camp.

After taking in sunrise from Kala Patthar (5,545 m), trekkers face the final and highest challenge: Kongma La Pass (5,535 m) before descending to Chhukung, Tengboche, Namche Bazaar, and returning to Lukla.

Lukla Flight Information

Flight from Ramechhap (March, April, May, October & November): During peak seasons, flights operate from Ramechhap Airport to avoid air traffic in Kathmandu. Includes a 5-6 hour drive from Kathmandu to Ramechhap followed by a 20-minute flight to Lukla.

Flight from Kathmandu (December – February & June – September): Direct 35-minute flight from Kathmandu's Tribhuvan International Airport to Lukla.

Who Can Do Nepal Everest Three Pass Trekking?

Graded as HARD (3/4). Best for physically fit trekkers, experienced high-altitude hikers, and adventure lovers ready for 6–8 hours of daily walking across high mountain passes above 5,300 meters.

faqs.answer: It is graded HARD. It requires strong physical fitness, stamina, and high-altitude experience to cross Renjo La (5,340 m), Cho La (5,330 m), and Kongma La (5,535 m).

faqs.question: When is the best time for Everest Three pass trek?
faqs.answer: Spring (March to May) and Autumn (September to November) offer the best weather, clear pass crossings, and dry trail conditions.

faqs.question: Do I need permits for the Everest Three Pass Trek?
faqs.answer: Yes, Sagarmatha National Park Entry Permit and Khumbu Pasang Lhamu Rural Permit are required and arranged by our team.

faqs.question: What is the highest point on the Everest Three Pass Trek?
faqs.answer: Kala Patthar at 5,545 meters and Kongma La Pass at 5,535 meters.

faqs.question: Is travel insurance required for Everest Three Pass Trek?
faqs.answer: Yes, comprehensive travel insurance covering emergency high-altitude medical helicopter evacuation up to 6,000 m is mandatory.

itinerary.title: Arrival in Kathmandu (1350 m)
itinerary.details: Upon arrival at Tribhuvan International Airport (TIA) in Kathmandu, you will be greeted by our correspondent who will assist with your transfer to the hotel. Once checked in, we will arrange a pre-trip meeting where we will brief in short about the trek, answer any queries you have and meet your trekking guide as well. After the short brief, you can relax and spend rest of the day at your leisure. Stay overnight at the hotel.

itinerary.title: Kathmandu – Lukla (2840 m) – Phakding (2610 m)
itinerary.details: Early morning breakfast at the hotel, transfer to the domestic airport for a 35-minute scenic flight to Lukla (2,840 m). Meet Sherpas and begin 3 hours of trekking along terraced landscapes and river valleys to Phakding (2,610 m). Stay overnight at a lodge in Phakding.

itinerary.title: Phakding - Namche Bazar (3440 m)
itinerary.details: Trek 5 to 6 hours to Namche Bazaar. Walk along the Dudh Koshi River, crossing high suspension bridges. Pass Monjo village (2,835 m) into Sagarmatha National Park. Climb the steep zig-zag trail to reach Namche Bazaar (3,440 m), the bustling Sherpa capital. Stay overnight at lodge in Namche Bazzar.

itinerary.title: Acclimatization & Hike to Everest View Hotel (3880 m)
itinerary.details: Acclimatization hike (4 hours) to Syangboche, Khumjung village, and Everest View Hotel (3,880 m) for panoramic vistas of Everest, Ama Dablam, Lhotse, and Nuptse. Free afternoon to explore Namche markets. Stay overnight at lodge in Namche Bazzar.

itinerary.title: Namche Bazzar - Thame (3820 m)
itinerary.details: Trek 4 to 5 hours following the Bhote Koshi River through pine and rhododendron forests to Thame (3,820 m). Pass mani walls, stupas, and visit Ani Monastery at Thamu and Dechen Chokhorling Monastery in Thame. Stay overnight at Lodge in Thame.

itinerary.title: Thame - Lungden (4380 m)
itinerary.details: Trek 5 to 6 hours uphill past traditional Sherpa walled villages of Taranga and Marulung (4,200 m) to Lungden (4,380 m). Walk along the historic trade route connecting Namche to Tibet. Stay overnight at Lodge in Lungden.

itinerary.title: Lungden – Renjola Pass (5340 m) – Gokyo (4790 m)
itinerary.details: Early morning pre-dawn start (5 am) to cross Renjo La Pass (5,340 m) taking 6 to 7 hours total. Reaching the summit rewards you with magnificent 360-degree vistas of Everest, Lhotse, Makalu, and Cho Oyu. Descend 2 hours to Gokyo village (4,790 m) on the shores of Gokyo Lake. Stay overnight at Lodge in Gokyo.

itinerary.title: Gokyo - Gokyo Ri (5360 m) - Thagnag (4700 m)
itinerary.details: Pre-dawn 3-hour steep uphill climb to Gokyo Ri (5,360 m) for breathtaking sunrise views over Everest, Lhotse, Makalu, Cho Oyu, and Ngozumpa Glacier. Descend to Gokyo for breakfast, then trek 3 hours across Ngozumpa Glacier moraines to Thagnag (4,700 m). Stay overnight at Lodge in Thagnag.

itinerary.title: Thagnag – Chola Pass (5330 m) – Dzonglha (4830 m)
itinerary.details: Start early at 4 am to cross Cho La Pass (5,330 m) taking 7 hours total. Climb rocky slopes and cross the icy glacier section using microspikes. Enjoy stunning views of Cho Oyu and Ama Dablam from the pass before descending down a long alpine valley to Dzonglha (4,830 m). Stay overnight at Lodge in Dzonglha.

itinerary.title: Dzonglha - Lobuche (4910 m)
itinerary.details: Short scenic 3 to 4-hour trek from Dzonglha to Lobuche (4,910 m). Walk below towering peaks of Cholatse (6,440 m), Taboche (6,495 m), and Lobuche East. Enjoy views of Khumbu Glacier moraine and Nuptse (7,861 m). Stay overnight at Lodge in Lobuche.

itinerary.title: Lobuche - EBC (5360 m) - Gorakshep (5140 m)
itinerary.details: Trek 2 hours along Khumbu Glacier moraines to Gorak Shep (5,140 m). Check in and continue 2.5 hours to Everest Base Camp (5,360 m). Stand at the foot of Mount Everest next to Khumbu Icefall. Return to Gorak Shep for overnight stay (6 hours total). Stay overnight at Lodge in Gorakshep.

itinerary.title: Gorak Shep - Kalapatthar (5545 m) - Lobuche (4910 m)
itinerary.details: Early 5 am climb to Kala Patthar (5,545 m)—the highest point of the trek! Marvel at unforgettable golden sunrise views over Mount Everest, Nuptse, Lhotse, and Pumori. Descend to Gorak Shep for breakfast, then trek back down alongside Khumbu Glacier to Lobuche (4,910 m). Stay overnight at Lodge in Lobuche.

itinerary.title: Lobuche – Kongma La Pass (5535 m) – Chukkung (4730 m)
itinerary.details: Cross the final and highest pass: Kongma La Pass (5,535 m) taking 5 to 6 hours. Cross Khumbu Glacier and ascend steep moraine slopes to the pass overlooking Kongma Lake, Mt. Lhotse, and Ama Dablam. Descend steeply to Chukkung (4,730 m). Stay overnight at Lodge in Chukkung.

itinerary.title: Chukkung – Tengboche (3860 m)
itinerary.details: Trek 5 to 6 hours descending through Imja Valley past Dingboche, Pangboche, and Debuche. Arrive at Tengboche (3,860 m) to visit Tengboche Monastery and observe evening prayer rituals. Stay overnight at Lodge in Tengboche.

itinerary.title: Tengboche – Namche Bazar (3440 m)
itinerary.details: Descend steeply to Phunki Thanga, cross the Dudh Koshi River, and climb up to Namche Bazaar (3,440 m) taking 5 hours total. Free afternoon for souvenir shopping and cafes in Namche. Stay overnight at Lodge in Namche Bazzar.

itinerary.title: Namche Bazar – Phakding – Lukla (2840 m)
itinerary.details: Final trekking day (7-8 hours). Descend along Dudh Koshi River past Monjo and Phakding for lunch. Make the final climb up to Lukla (2,840 m) and celebrate the successful completion of the Three Passes Trek with your crew. Stay overnight at Lodge in Lukla.

itinerary.title: Lukla - Kathmandu
itinerary.details: Early morning flight from Lukla Airport back to Kathmandu (or Ramechhap). Transfer to hotel and rest for the day. Stay overnight at Hotel in Kathmandu.

itinerary.title: Kathmandu Free Day & Sightseeing
itinerary.details: Free day in Kathmandu for leisure, massage, or UNESCO World Heritage sightseeing (Boudhanath Stupa, Pashupatinath Temple, Bhaktapur Durbar Square). Stay overnight at Hotel in Kathmandu.

itinerary.title: Departure from Kathmandu
itinerary.details: Enjoy breakfast at your hotel before your private airport transfer to Tribhuvan International Airport (TIA) for your flight home.

tourTrips.title: Jiri to Everest Base Camp Trek - 22 Days
tourTrips.destination: Jiri, Gokyo Lakes, Cho La Pass & Everest Base Camp, Nepal
tourTrips.shortDescription: The legendary pioneer trail used by Hillary & Tenzing in 1953 from Jiri to Gokyo Lakes, Cho La Pass, Everest Base Camp & Kala Patthar.
tourTrips.description:
Jiri to Everest Base Camp Trek of 22 days in Nepal is a historic and longer route to Everest, starting with a scenic drive from Kathmandu to Jiri and Bhandara. This 22-day trek offers a unique opportunity to explore the rich culture, diverse landscapes, and untouched nature of the lower Khumbu region—an area often missed by those who fly directly to Lukla.

Known as the "Classic Route to Everest", trekkers follow the exact pioneer path once walked by legendary mountaineers Sir Edmund Hillary and Tenzing Norgay during their historic 1953 expedition. Along the way, trekkers pass through vibrant Sherpa and Rai villages, Gaurishankar Conservation Area, Gokyo Lakes, Cho La Pass, Everest Base Camp, and Kala Patthar.

Jiri to Everest Base Camp Trek | The Legendary Pioneer Trail

The route begins with an overland drive to Bhandara via Jiri. The trail passes through Deurali, Sete, Junbesi, Nunthala, and Bupsa before merging with the main Everest Gokyo–Cho La Pass trail at Chheplung and Namche Bazaar.

After exploring Namche, Dole, Machhermo, and the turquoise Gokyo Lakes (4,790 m), trekkers climb Gokyo Ri (5,360 m) and cross Cho La Pass (5,330 m). The journey culminates at Everest Base Camp (5,360 m) and a pre-dawn climb of Kala Patthar (5,545 m) before descending past Tengboche to Lukla for a flight back to Kathmandu.

Lukla Flight Information

Flight from Ramechhap (March, April, May, October & November): During peak seasons, flights operate from Ramechhap Airport to avoid air traffic in Kathmandu. Includes a 5-6 hour drive from Kathmandu to Ramechhap followed by a 20-minute flight to Lukla.

Flight from Kathmandu (December – February & June – September): Direct 35-minute flight from Kathmandu's Tribhuvan International Airport to Lukla.

Who Can Do Jiri to Everest Base Camp Trek?

Graded as HARD (3/4). Best for physically fit trekkers, experienced long-distance hikers, and culture lovers who have time for a 3-week expedition with gradual high-altitude acclimatization.

faqs.answer: Spring (March to May) and Autumn (September to November) offer optimal weather, clear skies, and comfortable trekking conditions.

itinerary.title: Arrival in Kathmandu (1350 m)
itinerary.details: Upon arrival at Tribhuvan International Airport (TIA) in Kathmandu, you will be greeted by our correspondent who will assist with your transfer to the hotel. Once checked in, we will arrange a pre-trip meeting where we will brief in short about the trek, answer any queries you have and meet your trekking guide as well. After the short brief, you can relax and spend rest of the day at your leisure. Stay overnight at the hotel.

itinerary.title: Kathmandu – Bhandara (2190 m) via Jiri (1955 m)
itinerary.details: Early morning drive from Kathmandu to Bhandara via Jiri in a private vehicle (10 hours, 216 km). Enjoy scenic mountain views of Ganesh Himal, Dorje Lakpa, and Langtang. Explore Bhandara village, monastery, and coffee farms. Stay overnight at lodge in Bhandara.

itinerary.title: Bhandara - Sete (2580 m)
itinerary.details: Trek 7 hours from Bhandara to Sete. Walk uphill 3.5 hours to Kinja (1,630 m) for lunch, cross Kinja Khola, and climb 3.5 hours through rhododendron forests to reach Sete (2,580 m). Stay overnight at lodge in Sete.

itinerary.title: Sete - Junbesi (2700 m)
itinerary.details: Climb 4 hours uphill to Lamjura Pass (3,530 m) enjoying views of Pikey Peak and Mera Peak. Descend 3 hours through rhododendron forests to Junbesi (2,700 m), a charming Sherpa village. Explore local monasteries. Stay overnight at lodge in Junbesi.

itinerary.title: Junbeshi - Nunthala (2194 m)
itinerary.details: Trek 8 hours to Nunthala. Ascend 3.5 hours to Ringmo (2,720 m) for lunch, climb to Taksindu Pass (2,960 m) to visit Taksindu Monastery, then descend 3.5 hours to Nunthala (2,194 m). Stay overnight at lodge in Nunthala.

itinerary.title: Nunthala – Bupsa (2340 m)
itinerary.details: Descend 3 hours to Dudh Koshi River, cross suspension bridge, and climb 2 hours to Khari Khola for lunch. Continue 2 hours uphill to Bupsa (2,340 m). Stay overnight at lodge in Bupsa.

itinerary.title: Bupsa – Chheplung (2660 m)
itinerary.details: Ascend through bamboo and rhododendron forests past Tham Danda to Surke for lunch. Continue 2.5 hours to Chheplung (2,660 m), where the Jiri trail merges with the Lukla route. Stay overnight at lodge in Chheplung.

itinerary.title: Chheplung – Namche Bazaar (3440 m)
itinerary.details: Trek 7 hours to Namche Bazaar via Phakding and Monjo. Cross high suspension bridges over Dudh Koshi River and enter Sagarmatha National Park. Ascend steep zig-zag path to Namche Bazaar (3,440 m). Stay overnight at lodge in Namche Bazaar.

itinerary.title: Day of Acclimatization at Namche Bazaar (3440 m)
itinerary.details: Acclimatization hike (4 hours) to Syangboche, Khumjung village, and Everest View Hotel (3,880 m) for panoramic views of Mt. Everest, Ama Dablam, and Lhotse. Free afternoon in Namche markets. Stay overnight at Lodge in Namche Bazaar.

itinerary.title: Namche Bazar – Phortse Tenga (3680 m) – Dole (4200 m)
itinerary.details: Trek 6-7 hours to Dole. Climb to Mongla Pass (3,972 m) for views of Ama Dablam, descend to Phortse Tenga for lunch, and climb through rhododendron forests to Dole (4,200 m). Stay overnight at Lodge in Dole.

itinerary.title: Dole – Machermo (4470 m)
itinerary.details: Trek 4-5 hours to Machermo (4,470 m). Walk past Labharma and Luza with stunning vistas of Thamserku and Ama Dablam. Arrive by lunch; optional afternoon acclimatization hike. Stay overnight at Lodge in Machermo.

itinerary.title: Machermo – Gokyo (4790 m)
itinerary.details: Trek 4-5 hours to Gokyo. Pass 1st and 2nd Gokyo Lakes before reaching the turquoise 3rd Gokyo Lake and Gokyo village (4,790 m). Afternoon walk along Ngozumpa Glacier. Stay overnight at Lodge in Gokyo.

itinerary.title: Gokyo – Gokyo Ri (5360 m) - Thagnag (4700 m)
itinerary.details: Pre-dawn 3-hour climb to Gokyo Ri (5,360 m) for panoramic sunrise views over Everest, Lhotse, Makalu, and Cho Oyu. Descend to Gokyo for breakfast, then trek 3 hours across Ngozumpa Glacier to Thagnag (4,700 m). Stay overnight at Lodge in Thagnag.

itinerary.title: Thagnag – Chola Pass (5330 m) – Dzonglha (4830 m)
itinerary.details: Early 4 am start to cross Cho La Pass (5,330 m) taking 7 hours total. Ascend rocky trails, cross the glacier using microspikes, and enjoy views of Cho Oyu before descending to Dzonglha (4,830 m). Stay overnight at Lodge in Dzonglha.

itinerary.title: Dzonglha – Gorakshep (5140 m)
itinerary.details: Trek 6 hours from Dzonglha past Lobuche (4,910 m) along Khumbu Glacier moraines to Gorak Shep (5,140 m), the final lodge settlement before EBC. Stay overnight at Lodge in Gorakshep.

itinerary.title: GorakShep – Kala Patthar (5545 m) – EBC (5360 m) - Lobuche (4910 m)
itinerary.details: Pre-dawn climb to Kala Patthar (5,545 m) for golden sunrise views over Mt. Everest. Descend to Gorak Shep for breakfast, trek 2 hours to Everest Base Camp (5,360 m), and descend to Lobuche (4,910 m) taking 7 hours total. Stay overnight at Lodge in Lobuche.

itinerary.title: Lobuche - Tengboche (3860 m)
itinerary.details: Trek 7-8 hours descending through Imja Khola valley past Pangboche to Tengboche (3,860 m). Visit Tengboche Monastery. Stay overnight at Lodge in Tengboche.

itinerary.title: Tengboche (3860 m) – Namche Bazar (3440 m)
itinerary.details: Descend to Phunki Thanga, cross Dudh Koshi River, and climb to Namche Bazaar (3,440 m) taking 5-6 hours. Explore evening cafes. Stay overnight at Lodge in Namche Bazaar.

itinerary.title: Namche Bazar – Phakding – Lukla (2840 m)
itinerary.details: Final trekking day (7-8 hours). Descend along Dudh Koshi River past Monjo and Phakding to Lukla (2,840 m). Celebration dinner with guide and porters. Stay overnight at Lodge in Lukla.

itinerary.title: Lukla – Kathmandu
itinerary.details: Early morning flight from Lukla Airport back to Kathmandu (or Ramechhap). Transfer to hotel and rest. Stay overnight at Hotel in Kathmandu.

itinerary.title: Free day in Kathmandu
itinerary.details: Free day in Kathmandu for leisure, shopping, or UNESCO World Heritage sightseeing (Swayambhunath, Boudhanath, Pashupatinath). Stay overnight at Hotel in Kathmandu.

itinerary.title: Departure from Kathmandu
itinerary.details: Enjoy breakfast at your hotel before your private airport transfer to Tribhuvan International Airport (TIA) for your flight home.

tourTrips.title: Mera Peak Climbing and Amphu Lapcha Pass - 19 Days
tourTrips.destination: Mera Peak (6,461 m) & Amphu Lapcha Pass (5,845 m), Nepal
tourTrips.shortDescription: Summit Nepal's highest trekking peak (Mera Peak 6,461 m) and cross the technical Amphu Lapcha Pass (5,845 m) through remote Hongu Valley.
tourTrips.description:
Mera Peak Climbing and Amphu Lapcha Pass Expedition of 19 days is a challenging high-altitude adventure that combines trekking, peak climbing, and crossing a technical mountain pass. It takes you through the quiet Hinku and remote Hongu Valleys, far from the busy Everest routes.

You will climb Mera Peak (6,461 m)—the highest trekking peak in Nepal offering amazing summit views of five 8,000 m giants: Mount Everest (8,848 m), Lhotse (8,516 m), Makalu (8,485 m), Cho Oyu (8,188 m), and Kangchenjunga (8,586 m). After the summit, the journey continues into the wild Hongu Valley, culminating at the technical Amphu Lapcha Pass (5,845 m).

Amphu Lapcha Pass (5,845 m) – Technical & Thrilling

The Amphu Lapcha Pass is an icy mountain pass connecting Hongu Valley to Imja Valley near Chhukung. Crossing it involves fixed ropes, crampons, ice axes, helmets, and harnesses to ascend steep icy slopes and rappel down ice walls into Chhukung.

Who Can Do Mera Peak & Amphu Lapcha Pass?

Suitable for fit trekkers with basic mountaineering training (or willingness to learn rope techniques) and experienced high-altitude hikers looking for a true wilderness expedition experience.
highlights: Summit Mera Peak (6,461 m) – Nepal's highest trekking peak with 360-degree views of Everest, Lhotse, Makalu, Cho Oyu, and Kanchenjunga
Cross technical Amphu Lapcha Pass (5,845 m) – Demanding high-altitude pass requiring fixed ropes, crampons, and harness
Explore remote Hinku and untouched Hongu Valleys away from crowded Everest trails
Visit Seto Pokhari (White Lake) and pristine high-alpine lakes beneath Chamlang (7,319 m) and Baruntse
Includes full technical mountaineering gear support (ropes, ice stakes, fixed ropes, camping infrastructure)
Lodge accommodations in lower valleys and full tented camping setup at High Camp and Amphu Lapcha

essentialInfo.title: Permits Required for Mera Peak & Amphu Lapcha Pass
essentialInfo.content:
To climb Mera Peak and cross Amphu Lapcha Pass, you will need four permits:

• Mera Peak Climbing Permit (NMA): Official NMA climbing permit.
• Makalu Barun National Park Permit: Required for Hinku/Hongu valleys.
• Sagarmatha National Park Permit: Required for Imja valley/Khumbu section.
• Khumbu Pasang Lhamu Rural Municipality Permit: Local entry permit.

All permits are pre-arranged by Zenex Travels!

essentialInfo.title: Best Time for Mera Peak & Amphu Lapcha Pass
essentialInfo.content:
• Spring (March – May): Stable weather, mild temperatures, clear blue skies, blooming rhododendrons.
• Autumn (September – November): Crisp air, fresh snow, dry trails, crystal clear mountain visibility.

essentialInfo.title: Meals & Accommodations During Expedition
essentialInfo.content:
Tea house lodges are used in lower valleys (Lukla, Kothe, Tangnag, Khare, Chhukung). Tented camps with full expedition kitchen crew are set up at High Camp (5,780 m), Seto Pokhari, and Amphu Lapcha Base Camp.

• Meals: Fresh breakfast, lunch, and dinner with tea/coffee throughout the expedition.

essentialInfo.title: Difficulty & Technical Skills Required
essentialInfo.content: Graded as CHALLENGING / ALPINE. Peak summit (6,461 m) is non-technical glacier walking with crampons & ropes. Amphu Lapcha Pass (5,845 m) is technical, requiring fixed ropes, harnesses, descenders, and ice axes. Guided instruction provided!

items.name: Fleece Jacket, Down Jacket & Waterproof Gore-Tex Shell

faqs.question: How difficult is the Mera Peak and Amphu Lapcha Pass trek?
faqs.answer: It is graded Challenging. It combines non-technical 6,461 m peak climbing with technical 5,845 m pass crossing using fixed ropes and crampons.

faqs.question: Do I need prior climbing experience to attempt Mera Peak?
faqs.answer: Prior mountaineering experience is not mandatory for Mera Peak itself, but basic rope and crampon training will be provided by your guide in Khare.

faqs.question: Is Amphu Lapcha Pass technical?
faqs.answer: Yes! Amphu Lapcha Pass (5,845 m) requires technical gear including fixed ropes, harnesses, descenders, and crampons for steep ice wall rappelling.

faqs.question: What permits are required for Mera Peak & Amphu Lapcha Pass?
faqs.answer: NMA Mera Peak Permit, Makalu Barun NP Permit, Sagarmatha NP Permit, and Khumbu Local Permit.

faqs.question: What equipment is needed for Mera Peak & Amphu Lapcha Pass?
faqs.answer: Double mountaineering boots, crampons, ice axe, harness, helmet, carabiners, jumar, descender, and warm -25°C sleeping bag.

itinerary.title: Arrival in Kathmandu (1350 m)
itinerary.details: Upon arrival at Tribhuvan International Airport (TIA) in Kathmandu, you will be greeted by our correspondent who will assist with your transfer to the hotel. Once checked in, we will arrange a pre-trip meeting where we will brief in short about the trek, answer any queries you have and meet your trekking guide as well. After the short brief, you can relax and spend rest of the day at your leisure. Stay overnight at the hotel.

itinerary.title: Kathmandu - Lukla (2,840 m) - Chutanga (3020 m)
itinerary.details: Early morning flight from Kathmandu/Ramechhap to Lukla (2,840 m). Meet Sherpa crew and begin 4-hour trek through lush rhododendron forests and Sherpa hamlets to Chutanga (3,020 m). Stay overnight at lodge in Chutanga.

itinerary.title: Chutanga - Chetrabu (4170 m)
itinerary.details: Ascend 5 to 6 hours over steep alpine terrain and rocky ridges to Chetrabu (4,170 m), gaining elevation for acclimatization. Enjoy stunning views of the Dudh Koshi Valley. Stay overnight at lodge in Chetrabu.

itinerary.title: Chetrabu - Kothe (3691 m)
itinerary.details: Descend 6 to 7 hours through dense rhododendron and pine forests into Hinku Valley. Enjoy views of Mera Peak and yaks grazing in high-altitude pastures to reach Kothe (3,691 m). Stay overnight at lodge in Kothe.

itinerary.title: Kothe - Tangnag (4358 m)
itinerary.details: Trek 4 to 5 hours along Hinku River through alpine meadows. Visit historic Do Drul Monastery en route and reach Tangnag (4,358 m) nestled beneath the south face of Mera Peak. Stay overnight at lodge in Tangnag.

itinerary.title: Acclimatization Day in Tangnag
itinerary.details: Acclimatization rest day in Tangnag. Take a 3 to 4-hour acclimatization hike up toward Kusum Kanguru (5,000 m) for clear views of Mera Peak. Stay overnight at lodge in Tangnag.

itinerary.title: Tangnag - Khare (5045 m)
itinerary.details: Trek 4 to 5 hours following the Hinku Glacier moraines past Dig Glacier to Khare (5,045 m), the staging base for Mera Peak climbing. Enjoy views of Charpate Himal and Mera North face. Stay overnight at lodge in Khare.

itinerary.title: Acclimatization & Climbing Training in Khare (5099 m)
itinerary.details: Acclimatization and pre-climb training day in Khare. Practice using crampons, ice axe, harness, jumar, and fixed ropes under expert guide instruction. Stay overnight at lodge in Khare.

itinerary.title: Khare - High Camp (5780 m)
itinerary.details: Trek 5 to 6 hours over snow-covered rocky terrain and glacier slopes past Mera La (5,415 m) to Mera High Camp (5,780 m). Enjoy magnificent views of Everest, Lhotse, Makalu, and Cho Oyu. Stay overnight at tented camp.

itinerary.title: High Camp - Mera Peak Summit (6461 m) – Mera La – Kongma Dingma (5168 m)
itinerary.details: Early 2 AM summit push using headlamps, crampons, and fixed ropes. Reach the summit of Mera Peak (6,461 m) after 5-6 hours of climbing. Marvel at 360° views of Everest, Lhotse, Makalu, Cho Oyu, and Kanchenjunga. Descend past Mera La to Kongma Dingma (5,168 m) taking 10-11 hours total. Stay overnight at tented camp.

itinerary.title: Kongma Dingma – Seto Pokhari (5035 m)
itinerary.details: Trek 5 to 6 hours deeper into the untouched Upper Hinku Valley along glacial debris and moraines to Seto Pokhari (White Lake, 5,035 m), set beneath Chamlang (7,319 m) and Baruntse. Stay overnight at tented camp.

itinerary.title: Seto Pokhari – Amphu Lapcha Base Camp (5000 m)
itinerary.details: Trek 4 to 5 hours through wild high-altitude Hongu Valley along glacial moraines to Amphu Lapcha South Base Camp (5,000 m). Prepare climbing gear for pass crossing. Stay overnight at tented camp.

itinerary.title: Amphu Lapcha Base Camp – Amphu Lapcha Pass (5845 m) – Chhukung (4730 m)
itinerary.details: Pre-dawn technical climb up ice slopes and fixed ropes to Amphu Lapcha Pass (5,845 m). Rappel down the steep north ice wall into Imja Valley and trek down to Chhukung village (4,730 m) taking 9 to 10 hours total. Stay overnight at lodge in Chhukung.

itinerary.title: Chhukung - Pangboche (3930 m)
itinerary.details: Trek 3 to 4 hours descending Imja Valley past Dingboche to Pangboche (3,930 m). Visit Pangboche Monastery. Stay overnight at Lodge in Pangboche.

itinerary.title: Pangboche - Namche Bazzar (3440 m)
itinerary.details: Trek 5 hours descending through Debuche and Tengboche Monastery to Phunki Thanga, then climb up to Namche Bazaar (3,440 m). Stay overnight at Lodge in Namche Bazzar.

itinerary.title: Namche Bazaar - Lukla (2840 m)
itinerary.details: Final trekking day (7-8 hours). Descend along Dudh Koshi River past Monjo and Phakding to Lukla (2,840 m). Celebration dinner with expedition crew. Stay overnight at Lodge in Lukla.

itinerary.title: Lukla - Kathmandu (1350 m)
itinerary.details: Early morning flight from Lukla to Kathmandu (or Ramechhap). Transfer to hotel and rest for the day. Stay overnight at Hotel in Kathmandu.

tourTrips.title: Annapurna Base Camp Trek via Ghandruk - 12 Days
tourTrips.destination: Annapurna Base Camp & Ghandruk, Nepal
tourTrips.shortDescription: Iconic 12-day Himalayan trek into the heart of Annapurna Sanctuary (4,130 m) via traditional Gurung village of Ghandruk and Jhinu hot springs.
tourTrips.description:
Annapurna Base Camp (ABC) Trek of 12 days via Ghandruk, also known as the Annapurna Sanctuary Trek, is renowned amongst global adventurers drawing travelers to explore Annapurna's captivating landscapes. Positioned at an altitude of 4,130 meters above sea level, this trek is the best gateway to the towering beauty of Mount Annapurna I (8,091 m), the 10th highest mountain in the world.

The trek heads first to the traditional Gurung village of Ghandruk (1,970 m), famous for its stone-paved alleys, cultural heritage museum, and breathtaking vistas of Annapurna South and Machhapuchhre (Fishtail). The trail then follows the scenic Modi Khola Valley before entering the glacial basin of the Annapurna Sanctuary.

Explore Beauty, Culture & Mountains at Annapurna Base Camp

During this 12-day journey, trekkers pass through Machhapuchhre Base Camp (MBC, 3,700 m) to reach Annapurna Base Camp (ABC, 4,130 m), surrounded by 360-degree views of Annapurna I (8,091 m), Annapurna South (7,219 m), Machhapuchhre (6,993 m), and Himchuli (6,441 m).

On the return journey, relax and soothe tired muscles in the natural thermal hot springs at Jhinu Danda (1,780 m) before driving back to Pokhara.

Who Can Do This Trek?

Suitable for beginners with good physique, moderate-level trekkers, solo travelers, couples, and groups. No prior technical climbing experience required!
highlights: Explore scenic Pokhara's tranquil lake, nightlife, and views of Annapurna Range
Discover enriched Gurung heritage village of Ghandruk – traditional lifestyle, museum, and local cuisine
Trek through lush green Annapurna Sanctuary, rhododendron forests, and bamboo groves
Enjoy breathtaking views of Annapurna South, Annapurna I (8,091 m), Gangapurna, and Machhapuchhre (Fishtail)
Explore two majestic base camps: Machhapuchhre Base Camp (MBC) & Annapurna Base Camp (ABC)
Breathtaking sunrise views over glacier peaks from Annapurna Base Camp (4,130 m)
Spend overnight in the heart of Annapurna Sanctuary at 4,130 meters
Relax and rejuvenate in the natural hot springs at Jhinu Danda

essentialInfo.title: Permits Required for Annapurna Base Camp Trek
essentialInfo.content:
To trek to Annapurna Base Camp via Ghandruk, you will need two main permits:

• Annapurna Conservation Area Permit (ACAP): NPR 3,000 per person
• Trekkers' Information Management System (TIMS) Card: NPR 2,000 per person

All permits are arranged by Zenex Travels on your behalf in advance!

essentialInfo.title: Best Time for Annapurna Base Camp Trek
essentialInfo.content:
• Spring (March – May): Blooming rhododendron & bamboo forests, mild temperatures, clear blue skies.
• Autumn (September – November): Dry trails, crisp air, maximum mountain visibility of Annapurna I, Machhapuchhre, and Annapurna South.
• Winter & Summer: ABC trek via Ghandruk is a safe low-to-moderate altitude trek that can be comfortably done in all seasons!

essentialInfo.title: Meals & Accommodations
essentialInfo.content:
Trekkers stay in cozy tea house lodges with twin beds, blankets, and communal dining rooms heated with central stoves.

• Breakfast: Bread, Muesli, Porridge, Pancakes, Tibetan Bread, Chapati, Eggs with tea/coffee.
• Lunch & Dinner: Dal Bhat, Chowmein, Fried Rice, Pasta, French Fries, Momo, Pizza, Soups.

essentialInfo.title: Natural Hot Springs of Jhinu Danda
essentialInfo.content: A major highlight on the return route is Jhinu Danda (1,780 m), famous for its natural riverside thermal hot springs where trekkers can soak and soothe tired muscles in natural warm mineral waters!

faqs.question: How difficult is the Annapurna Base Camp Trek via Ghandruk?
faqs.answer: It is graded as Moderate. It reaches a maximum altitude of 4,130 meters with 4 to 6 hours of daily walking, making it very accessible for fit beginners and families.

faqs.question: What mountains can be seen from Annapurna Base Camp?
faqs.answer: Annapurna I (8,091 m - 10th highest peak), Annapurna South (7,219 m), Machhapuchhre / Fishtail (6,993 m), Himchuli (6,441 m), Gangapurna, and Annapurna III.

faqs.question: Why is the Ghandruk route recommended?
faqs.answer: Ghandruk is a famous heritage Gurung village offering rich local culture, traditional stone-paved architecture, Gurung museum, and incredible vistas of Annapurna South.

faqs.question: Are there hot springs on the ABC trek?
faqs.answer: Yes! Jhinu Danda features natural thermal hot springs along the Modi Khola River where trekkers can relax and rejuvenate before returning to Pokhara.

itinerary.title: Kathmandu – Pokhara (820 m)
itinerary.details: In the morning, depart Kathmandu by comfortable tourist bus (8-9 hours, 200 km) following the Trishuli and Marsyangdi rivers to Pokhara, the lake city beneath the Annapurna Range. Optional 25-minute flight available. Evening free to explore Phewa Lake lakeside. Stay overnight at hotel in Pokhara.

itinerary.title: Pokhara – Nayapul (1070 m) - Ghandruk (1970 m)
itinerary.details: 1-hour drive from Pokhara to Nayapul (40 km), the gateway to Annapurna. Begin 4 to 5-hour trek (17 km) to Ghandruk (1,970 m), a famous Gurung heritage village. Enjoy views of Annapurna South, Himchuli, and Fishtail. Visit Gurung cultural museum. Stay overnight at lodge in Ghandruk.

itinerary.title: Ghandruk – Chhomrong (2170 m)
itinerary.details: Trek 5 to 6 hours (10 km) from Ghandruk. Descend steep stone steps to Kimrong Khola, cross the river, and ascend through rhododendron forests past Chere Danda to Chhomrong village (2,170 m). Enjoy magnificent views of Annapurna South and Machhapuchhre. Stay overnight at lodge in Chhomrong.

itinerary.title: Chhomrong - Himalaya (2920 m)
itinerary.details: Check permits at Chhomrong entry post. Descend to Chhomrong Khola, ascend to Sinuwa, and trek through dense bamboo and rhododendron forests past Bamboo (2,335 m) and Dovan for lunch. Climb past Hinko Cave to reach Himalaya (2,920 m) taking 6 to 7 hours (13 km). Stay overnight at lodge in Himalaya.

itinerary.title: Himalaya – Annapurna Base Camp (4130 m)
itinerary.details: Highlights of the trek! Trek 6 to 7 hours (8.5 km) ascending past Deurali to Machhapuchhre Base Camp (MBC, 3,700 m) for 360° mountain vistas. Continue into the glacial basin of Annapurna Sanctuary to reach Annapurna Base Camp (ABC, 4,130 m) surrounded by Annapurna I (8,091 m), Annapurna South, and Himchuli. Catch sunset over the peaks. Stay overnight at lodge in ABC.

itinerary.title: Annapurna Base Camp - Bamboo (2310 m)
itinerary.details: Wake early for a magical golden sunrise over Annapurna I and surrounding peaks. After breakfast, bid farewell to the sanctuary and descend 6 to 7 hours (14 km) through MBC, Deurali, and Dovan back to Bamboo (2,310 m). Stay overnight at lodge in Bamboo.

itinerary.title: Bamboo – Jhinu Danda (1780 m)
itinerary.details: Trek 4 to 5 hours (9.5 km) from Bamboo up to Sinuwa and down to Chhomrong before descending through jungle trails to Jhinu Danda (1,780 m). Afternoon walk to the natural riverside thermal hot springs along Modi Khola to soak in warm mineral waters and relax muscles. Stay overnight at lodge in Jhinu Danda.

itinerary.title: Jhinu Danda – Pokhara (820 m)
itinerary.details: Short morning trek to Siwai or trail bridge (2 hours) and private jeep drive back to Pokhara (2.5 hours). Afternoon free to explore Lake Phewa, boat to Tal Barahi Temple, or enjoy Pokhara spa & lakeside cafes. Stay overnight at hotel in Pokhara.

itinerary.title: Pokhara – Kathmandu (1350 m)
itinerary.details: After breakfast, return to Kathmandu by tourist bus or private vehicle (8-9 hours, 200 km) or optional short flight. Check in to hotel. Stay overnight at Hotel in Kathmandu.

itinerary.details: Enjoy breakfast at your hotel before your private airport transfer to Tribhuvan International Airport (TIA) for your onward departure flight.

tourTrips.title: Annapurna Circuit Trek with Tilicho Lake - 18 Days
tourTrips.destination: Annapurna Circuit, Tilicho Lake (4,990 m) & Thorong La Pass (5,416 m), Nepal
tourTrips.shortDescription: Legendary 18-day Himalayan journey combining the classic Annapurna Circuit with high-altitude Tilicho Lake (4,990 m) and Thorong La Pass (5,416 m).
tourTrips.description:
Annapurna Circuit Trek with Tilicho Lake of 18 days in Nepal is an iconic trekking adventure that follows the legendary Annapurna Circuit and leads to Tilicho Lake (4,990 m), one of the highest alpine lakes in the world. Known as "The Great Ice Lake", Tilicho sits dramatically beneath snow-covered giants including Tilicho Peak (7,134 m) and the Annapurna Massif.

The trek takes you through diverse landscapes—from lush subtropical forests and terraced farmlands to arid high-altitude deserts—culminating with the crossing of Thorong La Pass (5,416 m), one of the highest trekking passes in the world. Along the way, enjoy close-up views of Annapurna I (8,091 m), Dhaulagiri (8,167 m), Manaslu (8,163 m), Gangapurna, and Nilgiri.

Culture, Sacred Pilgrimage & High Himalayan Passes

Explore rich Tibetan-Gurung heritage in traditional villages like Ghyaru, Ngawal, and Manang. Visit 900-year-old Braga Gompa and acclimatize with hikes to Gangapurna Glacier or Ice Lake. After visiting Tilicho Lake, traverse Sri Kharka and Thorong Phedi to conquer Thorong La Pass (5,416 m).

Descend into sacred Muktinath (3,760 m), renowned for its 108 holy water spouts and eternal natural gas flame worshipped by Hindus and Buddhists. Conclude your trek through Jomsom and the Kali Gandaki Gorge before relaxing in Pokhara.

Who Can Do This Trek?

Graded HARD (3/4). Recommended for physically fit trekkers who can walk 6-8 hours daily over rugged mountain trails. Ideal for adventure lovers seeking high-altitude lakes, sacred passes, and rich Himalayan culture!
highlights: Visit Tilicho Lake (4,990 m) – one of the highest alpine lakes in the world, known as "The Great Ice Lake"
Cross Thorong La Pass (5,416 m) – one of the world's highest trekking passes with views of Dhaulagiri and Mustang Himal
Explore remote mountain villages like Manang, Pisang, Ghyaru, and Sri Kharka
Visit the 900-year-old historic Braga Gompa in Manang and sacred Milarepa Cave
Explore ancient Tibetan Buddhist culture, mani walls, chortens, prayer wheels, and apple orchards in Bhratang
Visit sacred Muktinath Temple (3,760 m), a holy site for Hindus and Buddhists featuring 108 holy water spouts
Experience dramatic landscape transitions from subtropical forests to high-altitude Tibetan deserts
Enjoy sunrise views from Upper Pisang over Annapurna II (7,937 m), Gangapurna, and Tilicho Peak
Scenic mountain drive through Marsyangdi River Valley & optional Jomsom to Pokhara flight
Relax in Pokhara, the beautiful lakeside city, and enjoy Phewa Lake boating & lakeside cafes
Complimentary guided 1-day UNESCO World Heritage sightseeing tour in Kathmandu

essentialInfo.title: High Altitude & Acclimatization Safety
